### How DynamoDB global tables work

- ID: `dynamodb-global-tables-how`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/V2globaltables_HowItWorks.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 22
- この出典が支える主張:
  - In the default consistency mode, item changes are replicated asynchronously to all other replicas, typically within a second or less
  - Conflicting writes are resolved by last writer wins
  - A TTL delete in one replica is replicated to all other replicas
- 注記: The page states delete replication explicitly only for TTL deletes; that a user's DeleteItem replicates is read from 'item changes ... are replicated'.

### Working with delete markers

- ID: `s3-delete-markers`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/DeleteMarker.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 22
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A DELETE without a version ID in a versioning-enabled bucket does not delete the object: a delete marker becomes the current version
  - A GET without a version ID on a key whose current version is a delete marker returns 404
  - Delete markers are listed only by ListObjectVersions; ListObjectsV2 does not return keys whose current version is a delete marker
  - A delete marker is billed for the size of its key name

- この出典が支える主張:
  - To undelete an object, delete its delete marker with a DeleteObject request that names the marker's version ID
  - A DeleteObject without a version ID on a key whose current version is a delete marker removes nothing and adds another delete marker
  - An expired object delete marker is one with no versions left under it, and a lifecycle rule can remove it

### Lifecycle configuration elements

- ID: `s3-lifecycle-rules`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/intro-lifecycle-rules.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 22
- この出典が支える主張:
  - NoncurrentVersionExpiration permanently deletes noncurrent versions a number of days after they became noncurrent; they cannot be recovered
  - In a versioning-enabled bucket the Expiration action applies only to the current version and adds a delete marker instead of removing the object
  - ExpiredObjectDeleteMarker removes delete markers that have no versions left

### What does Amazon S3 replicate?

- ID: `s3-replication-what`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication-what-is-isnot-replicated.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 22
- この出典が支える主張:
  - By default only objects created after the replication configuration was added are replicated
  - With the latest configuration version (a rule with a Filter), delete markers are not replicated by default
  - A DELETE that names a version ID is not replicated to the destination
  - Actions performed by a lifecycle configuration are not replicated

### Replicating delete markers between buckets

- ID: `s3-delete-marker-replication`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/delete-marker-replication.html>

- 参照する章: 22
- この出典が支える主張:
  - By default a delete in the source bucket adds a delete marker in the source only
  - With delete marker replication enabled, markers are copied and S3 behaves as if the object was deleted in both buckets

### celld v0.6.2: README

- ID: `celld-readme-v062`
- URL: <https://github.com/denoland/celld/blob/v0.6.2/README.md>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 24
- この出典が支える主張:
  - celld runs a Cloudflare Workers application on your own machines and stores long-term state in an S3-compatible, Google Cloud Storage, or Azure Blob Storage bucket
  - A node is one celld process; nodes that share one bucket are a fleet; a conditional bucket write gives a node the ownership of a cell
  - celld uses the standard AWS credential chain; a node is started with --bucket, --listen, --internal-listen, and --advertise
  - The container example sets CELLD_WATCH to a directory on a persistent volume
  - One node proves each write through the bucket; with a second node the write finishes once that node holds it on disk
  - Put every advertised address on a trusted private network or an encrypted overlay; celld rejects a literal public IP unless --unsafe-public-advertise is given
  - Treat access to the bucket and its credentials as fleet administrator access
  - The installer downloads the binary from GitHub releases; provenance is verifiable with gh attestation verify

### celld v0.6.2: documentation (operate, shut down, upgrade notes, environment variables)

- ID: `celld-docs-v062`
- URL: <https://github.com/denoland/celld/blob/v0.6.2/docs/README.md>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 24
- この出典が支える主張:
  - CELLD_DURABILITY defaults to fleet; a one-node fleet waits for the bucket on every write; a fleet that loses all but one node falls back to the bucket and stays correct
  - celld shuts down gracefully on SIGTERM or SIGINT: health reports 503, accepted requests finish, and the node hands its cells off to a peer; POST /shutdown on the internal listener starts the same handoff
  - CELLD_SHUTDOWN_TOTAL_MS defaults to 40000; the orchestrator stop grace (systemd TimeoutStopSec) must be above it or SIGKILL can interrupt the handoff
  - To roll out a new version: stop each node with SIGTERM, wait for its replacement to report healthy, then move to the next node
  - During a rolling update, wait for restoring=0 on every node (celld diagnose) before restarting the next
  - A new process does not report healthy until the fleet settles; CELLD_READY_FLEET_GATE_MS defaults to 120000
  - Upgrade notes: v0.1.0 to v0.2.0 stop all; v0.2.1 to v0.3.0 rolling; v0.3.0 to v0.4.0 stop all; v0.4.0 to v0.4.1 rolling; v0.5.1 to v0.6.0 stop all with fleet durability; v0.6.0 to v0.6.1 rolling; v0.6.1 to v0.6.2 rolling
  - The node lease lives CELLD_TTL_MS (default 10000) and renews at one third of that; the fleet sample is read every CELLD_REBALANCE_INTERVAL_MS (default 5000); deploy/current.json is read every CELLD_DEPLOY_POLL_S (default 30)
  - CELLD_BUCKET, AWS_REGION, CELLD_ADDR, CELLD_INTERNAL_ADDR, CELLD_ADVERTISE, and CELLD_WATCH are the environment forms of the node settings; CELLD_NODE is an explicit node-session ID
  - A bucket value can add a key prefix (s3://BUCKET/PREFIX)
  - celld deploy needs esbuild on PATH for Worker code; CELLD_ESBUILD overrides the path; a running node adopts a new deployment without a restart
  - celld diagnose reads the node leases and probes each live peer without taking a lease; celld cell list prints one Class:ID scope per line
  - One 8 GB node holds 1,000 resident cells
  - celld does not scale itself; an external system starts and stops the nodes

### celld v0.6.2: what celld guarantees

- ID: `celld-guarantees-v062`
- URL: <https://github.com/denoland/celld/blob/v0.6.2/docs/guarantees.md>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 24
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Two promises: exactly one node serves a cell at a time, and an acknowledged write is never lost; both require a bucket with working conditional writes and ranged reads, and a supervisor that restarts the process
  - The qualified stores are Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, Tigris, Google Cloud Storage, and Azure Blob Storage; the release tests run against R2, and the S3 path uses the same client and headers
  - The supervisor must restart without an attempt limit and wait at least one lease lifetime between attempts
  - Each cell has one ownership record in the bucket, naming the owner's session and a fencing epoch, acquired by conditional create or compare-and-swap
  - In fleet mode the owner sends each write to one or two followers and every follower must fsync it; a fleet needs two running nodes for a fleet proof; a fleet of three or more holds three copies of an acknowledged write
  - In fleet mode celld can acknowledge a write before its bucket upload completes; a follower disk can hold acknowledged writes that the bucket does not yet hold
  - Recovery limits: a follower's HTTP error can block recovery and startup; a deleted final batch is undetectable if nothing later records its range; a mixed-version tail can stall recovery
  - A node whose lease expires fences itself, logs a line starting with SELF-FENCE:, and exits with code 3; only a restart returns it
  - celld reserves the key prefixes probe/, cells/, nodes/, node-cells/, fleet/, deploy/, deploy-blobs/, log/, wake/, and telemetry/
  - The v0.4.1 upgrade procedure: stop every node and wait for every lease to expire, back up the bucket and node data keeping node names, peer addresses, and data directories; to roll back, restore the full stopped-fleet backup, which loses writes made after it
  - Each node runs the storage test (four conditional writes and a ranged read) before it serves, and cannot disable it

### celld v0.6.2: testing

- ID: `celld-testing-v062`
- URL: <https://github.com/denoland/celld/blob/v0.6.2/docs/testing.md>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 24
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The coordination protocol is specified in TLA+ and exercised by deterministic simulation; the model grants a linearizable object store
  - Live-fleet fault scenarios include SIGKILL mid-write-stream, freezing an owner, cutting a node off from the bucket, and stopping a host; a verification pass fetches each cell through different nodes
  - A cell can be briefly unavailable while ownership moves
  - A fleet at its resident limit has no space for a lost node's cells

  - The S3 bucket provider handles LifecycleConfiguration, OwnershipControls, PublicAccessBlockConfiguration, and BucketEncryption
- 注記: Read from the installed package's dist directory. Nothing was run against AWS.

### Inference using Converse API

- ID: `bedrock-converse`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/conversation-inference.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-11
- 参照する章: 17
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Converse needs bedrock:InvokeModel; ConverseStream needs bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream
  - Order of ConverseStream events: messageStart, content block events, messageStop (with stopReason), metadata (usage and metrics)
  - contentBlockStart is sent for tool use only; a text delta is {contentBlockDelta: {delta: {text}, contentBlockIndex}}
  - Shape of a Converse response: output.message.content[].text, stopReason, usage, metrics

  - modelId accepts a base model ID or an inference profile ID
  - Stream members include internalServerException (500), modelStreamErrorException (424), serviceUnavailableException (503), throttlingException (429), validationException (400)
  - Errors: AccessDeniedException 403, ModelErrorException 424, ModelNotReadyException 429, ModelTimeoutException 408, ResourceNotFoundException 404, ServiceUnavailableException 503, ThrottlingException 429, ValidationException 400

### Response streaming for Lambda functions

- ID: `lambda-response-streaming`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-response-streaming.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-11
- 参照する章: 09, 17, 27
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Streaming is available through function URLs, InvokeWithResponseStream, and API Gateway proxy integrations
  - A streamed response is not interrupted when the client disconnects, and the full function duration is billed
  - Node.js managed runtimes support response streaming natively
  - Streamed payloads can be up to 200 MB; the first 6 MB is not rate limited
  - Function URLs do not support response streaming for a function in a VPC

  - The response stream is a Node.js writable stream; pipeline() is recommended for writing to it, and it ends the stream
  - The page does not describe awslambda.HttpResponseStream.from or the keys of the object passed to it

### Troubleshoot IAM: Changes that I make are not always immediately visible

- ID: `iam-eventual-consistency`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/troubleshoot.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 21
- この出典が支える主張:
  - IAM uses a distributed computing model called eventual consistency; changes take time to become visible from all possible endpoints
  - IAM also uses caching, so a change might not be visible until previously cached data times out
  - AWS recommends not including IAM changes in critical, high-availability code paths, and verifying that changes have propagated before production workflows depend on them

### Security best practices in IAM

- ID: `iam-best-practices`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/best-practices.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 01, 21
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Human users should use federation and temporary credentials; workloads should use IAM roles
  - Apply least-privilege permissions: grant only the permissions required to perform a task
  - Get started with AWS managed policies and move toward least-privilege permissions
  - Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate least-privilege policies based on access activity
  - Establish permissions guardrails across multiple accounts

### What's in a Secrets Manager secret?

- ID: `secretsmanager-secret`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/whats-in-a-secret.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 21
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A secret has versions; Secrets Manager tracks three by staging label: AWSCURRENT, AWSPREVIOUS, and AWSPENDING
  - A secret always has a version labeled AWSCURRENT, and that version is returned by default
  - Unlabeled versions are deprecated and removed when there are more than 100; versions created less than 24 hours ago are not removed
  - The secret ARN ends in six random characters, so a secret re-created under the same name has a different ARN

### PutSecretValue

- ID: `secretsmanager-put-secret-value`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/apireference/API_PutSecretValue.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 21
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Without VersionStages, AWSCURRENT moves to the new version and AWSPREVIOUS moves to the version AWSCURRENT was removed from
  - The operation is idempotent: the same ClientRequestToken with the same secret data succeeds and does nothing; with different data it fails
  - ClientRequestToken becomes the VersionId of the new version
  - Do not call PutSecretValue at a sustained rate of more than once every 10 minutes

### GetSecretValue

- ID: `secretsmanager-get-secret-value`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/apireference/API_GetSecretValue.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 21
- この出典が支える主張:
  - VersionStage selects a version by staging label; without it AWSCURRENT is returned
  - AWS recommends caching secret values on the client to improve speed and reduce cost
  - With a customer managed key the caller also needs kms:Decrypt on that key

### DeleteSecret

- ID: `secretsmanager-delete-secret`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/apireference/API_DeleteSecret.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 21
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A deleted secret has a recovery window: minimum 7 days, default 30 days
  - While scheduled for deletion, the secret value cannot be retrieved

### Service control policies (SCPs)

- ID: `organizations-scps`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 21, 63
- この出典が支える主張:
  - SCPs do not grant permissions; they set the maximum available permissions for IAM users and roles in member accounts
  - SCPs need an organization with all features enabled
  - SCPs do not affect users or roles in the management account, or service-linked roles
  - AWS strongly recommends not attaching SCPs to the root without testing; removing FullAWSAccess without a replacement makes all actions fail

### SCP evaluation

- ID: `organizations-scp-evaluation`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps_evaluation.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 21
- この出典が支える主張:
  - An action needs an explicit Allow at every level from the root through each OU to the account
  - A Deny at any level denies the action for everything beneath it
  - Organizations attaches the AWS managed SCP FullAWSAccess when SCPs are enabled

### SCP syntax

- ID: `organizations-scp-syntax`

- この出典が支える主張:
  - Principal and NotPrincipal are not supported in SCPs
  - Action, NotAction, Resource, NotResource, and Condition are supported in Allow and Deny statements
  - The example that denies operations outside chosen Regions uses NotAction with cloudfront:*, iam:*, route53:*, support:* and StringNotEquals on aws:RequestedRegion

### What Is Amazon EventBridge?

- ID: `events-eb-what-is`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-what-is.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 25
- この出典が支える主張:
  - EventBridge offers two event buses: the Custom Event Bus, which routes to subscribers, retains events, and supports ordered delivery and replay, and Custom Event Bus - Classic, which routes with rules and targets
  - The guide says to start new applications with the Custom Event Bus, and that Custom Event Bus - Classic remains available
  - A pipe with a DynamoDB stream as its source and an event bus as its target is given as a common use of pipes and buses together

### Amazon EventBridge event bus (default and Classic)

- ID: `events-eb-classic-bus`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-event-bus.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 25
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A Classic event bus evaluates each event against every rule on the bus and sends it to the targets of the rules it matches
  - An event may match several rules, and each rule can have up to five targets

### What is the EventBridge Custom Event Bus?

- ID: `events-eb-custom-bus`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-custom-bus-what-is.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 25
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The Custom Event Bus retains every event for 1 to 365 days, delivers in order within an event group per subscriber, and deduplicates at publish time within a 5-minute window
  - A subscriber delivers to exactly one target; a Classic rule delivers to up to five
  - On the Custom Event Bus replay is a subscriber's starting position over retained events; on Classic it is a replay from an archive

### Creating Custom Event Bus resources with CloudFormation

- ID: `events-eb-custom-bus-cfn`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-custom-bus-cloudformation.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 25
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Custom Event Bus resources are in the AWS::EventsV2 namespace (EventBus, Subscriber, EventSource, ResourcePolicy); the AWS::Events types belong to Classic and cannot configure a Custom Event Bus

### Ordering and deduplicating events on a Custom Event Bus

- ID: `events-eb-custom-bus-ordering`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-custom-bus-ordering.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 25
- この出典が支える主張:
  - EventBridge suppresses a duplicate publish that arrives within 5 minutes (300 seconds) of the entry it repeats
  - Ordering is a property of a subscriber (UNORDERED or FIFO) within an event group

### Migrating from Custom Event Bus - Classic to the Custom Event Bus

- ID: `events-eb-custom-bus-migrate`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-custom-bus-migrate.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 25
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A rule and one of its targets becomes one subscriber; an event pattern becomes a DATA filter unchanged for PutEvents traffic, except wildcards; archive and replay become retention on the bus and a subscriber starting position
  - A subscriber retries a failed delivery for 300 seconds and 5 attempts by default, where a Classic target retries for 24 hours and 185 attempts

### Amazon EventBridge event patterns

- ID: `events-eb-patterns`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-event-patterns.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 25
- この出典が支える主張:
  - An event pattern has the same structure as the events it matches, and either matches an event or does not
  - A rule can lead to an infinite loop when what it triggers matches the same rule again

### Creating Amazon EventBridge event patterns

- ID: `events-eb-create-pattern`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-create-pattern.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 25
- この出典が支える主張:
  - For a pattern to match, the event must contain all the field names in the pattern, in the same nesting; fields the pattern does not name are ignored
  - Values to match are given in an array, and any one of them matching is enough
  - Strings are matched character by character with no case folding; numbers are compared by their string representation, so 300, 300.0, and 3.0e2 are not equal

### Comparison operators for use in event patterns in Amazon EventBridge

- ID: `events-eb-pattern-operators`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-create-pattern-operators.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 25
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The operators: prefix, suffix, anything-but, exists, numeric, equals-ignore-case, wildcard, cidr, $or, with a table of which ones event buses and pipes support
  - Pipes do not support wildcard, nor anything-but combined with prefix, suffix, ignore-case, or wildcard
  - exists matching works only on leaf nodes
  - numeric matching compares 64-bit doubles

### How EventBridge retries delivering events

- ID: `events-eb-retry`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-rule-retry-policy.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 25
- この出典が支える主張:
  - By default EventBridge retries sending an event to a target for 24 hours and up to 185 times, with exponential backoff and jitter
  - An event not delivered after all retries is dropped unless a dead-letter queue is configured

### Using dead-letter queues to process undelivered events in EventBridge

- ID: `events-eb-dlq`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-rule-dlq.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 25
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A target's dead-letter queue is a standard SQS queue in the same Region; FIFO queues are not supported
  - Each message carries RULE_ARN, TARGET_ARN, ERROR_CODE, ERROR_MESSAGE, EXHAUSTED_RETRY_CONDITION, and RETRY_ATTEMPTS as attributes
  - Errors such as missing permissions or a target that no longer exists are not retried and go straight to the dead-letter queue
  - When the queue is set through the API, a resource policy must allow events.amazonaws.com to SendMessage, conditioned on the rule's ARN

### Amazon EventBridge input transformation

- ID: `events-eb-input-transformer`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-transform-target-input.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 25
- この出典が支える主張:
  - An input transformer defines up to 100 variables by JSON path and fills them into a template; the target receives the result instead of the event
  - EventBridge adds quotes to variables that hold strings; a variable whose path is not in the event is not created and does not appear in the output

### Archiving and replaying events in Amazon EventBridge

- ID: `events-eb-archive`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-archive.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 25
- この出典が支える主張:
  - An archive takes events from one bus, optionally filtered by a pattern, and keeps them indefinitely unless a retention is set
  - An event may reach the archive with a delay; the guide recommends waiting 10 minutes before replaying
  - A replay goes only to the bus the archive was filled from, optionally to named rules, and adds a replay-name field to each event; replayed events are not archived again
  - Events are not necessarily replayed in the order they were archived; a replay works through its window in one-minute intervals
  - At most ten replays can be active per account and Region, and a replay does not remove events from the archive

### Creating replays of archived events in Amazon EventBridge

- ID: `events-eb-replay`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-replay-archived-event.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 25
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A replay is given a start time and an end time, and either all rules or chosen rules

- ID: `events-eb-startreplay`

### Amazon EventBridge Pipes

- ID: `events-pipes`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-pipes.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 25
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A pipe connects one source to one target, with optional filtering and enrichment; you are charged only for events that match the filter

### Amazon DynamoDB stream as a source for EventBridge Pipes

- ID: `events-pipes-dynamodb`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-pipes-dynamodb.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 25
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A pipe polls each shard of a DynamoDB stream at a base rate of four times per second and keeps the order of records
  - Delivery is at least once; a retry policy with a maximum age shorter than the stream's retention is suggested
  - LATEST as the starting position can miss events sent during pipe creation or updates; TRIM_HORIZON does not
  - Disabling the stream makes the pipe unusable, even if the stream is enabled again, because the stream gets a new ARN

### Event filtering in Amazon EventBridge Pipes

- ID: `events-pipes-filtering`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-pipes-event-filtering.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 25
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Pipe filters use event patterns; fields added by the poller, among them eventName and eventID, cannot be used in them
  - After a stream record is filtered out the iterator moves past it

### Event enrichment in Amazon EventBridge Pipes

- ID: `events-pipes-enrichment`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/pipes-enrichment.html>

- 参照する章: 25

### Amazon EventBridge Pipes targets

- ID: `events-pipes-targets`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-pipes-event-target.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 25
- この出典が支える主張:
  - With an event bus as the target, the pipe's payload becomes the event's detail; Source and DetailType are set in PipeTargetEventBridgeEventBusParameters and may be JSON paths into the payload
  - A pipe can target an event bus in the same account and Region; the effective payload limit for that target is 1 MB

### Amazon EventBridge Pipes batching and concurrency

- ID: `events-pipes-batching`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-pipes-batching-concurrency.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 25
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The largest batch a pipe sends to an event bus is 10
  - For partial batch failure handling, the eventID of each DynamoDB record must be in the array an enrichment returns
  - A pipe execution is limited to 5 minutes including enrichment and target

### Amazon EventBridge Pipes error handling and troubleshooting

- ID: `events-pipes-errors`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-pipes-error-troubleshooting.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 25
- この出典が支える主張:
  - For a stream source, customer invocation errors are retried up to the pipe's maximum retry attempts or maximum record age; internal errors are retried until the record expires in the source
  - A pipe with a stream source can have a dead-letter queue (SQS or SNS); MaximumRecordAgeInSeconds should be less than the stream's own retention
  - A pipe can be disabled automatically after nearly continuous 4xx errors

  - Enrichment and target calls are made with the pipe's role, by the principal pipes.amazonaws.com

  - As of 2026-10-13 Vercel Queues is in beta on all plans: a topic is a durable append-only log that fans out to every consumer group, and a new consumer group can replay non-expired history
  - Delivery is at-least-once, and publishes can be deduplicated with idempotency keys

### Vercel Queues: Concepts

- ID: `events-vercel-queues-concepts`
- URL: <https://vercel.com/docs/queues/concepts>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 25
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Retention is set per message from 60 seconds to 7 days, 24 hours by default; consumer groups are isolated from each other; consumers should be idempotent

### Understand custom prefixes for Amazon S3 objects

- ID: `firehose-s3-prefixes`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/s3-prefixes.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 26
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A custom prefix overrides the default prefix of yyyy/MM/dd/HH; expressions have the form !{namespace:value} with the namespaces firehose, timestamp, partitionKeyFromQuery and partitionKeyFromLambda
  - For the timestamp namespace Firehose uses the approximate arrival timestamp of the oldest record contained in the S3 object being written; by default in UTC, and a time zone can be set with CustomTimeZone
  - ErrorOutputPrefix can be null only if Prefix contains no expressions; an ErrorOutputPrefix expression must include !{firehose:error-output-type}, and Prefix cannot contain it
  - error-output-type evaluates to one of processing-failed, AmazonOpenSearchService-failed, splunk-failed, format-conversion-failed, http-endpoint-failed

### Buffer data for dynamic partitioning

- ID: `firehose-dynamic-partitioning-buffering`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/buffering.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 26
- この出典が支える主張:
  - With dynamic partitioning each active partition has its own buffer and is delivered as its own object
  - Once the number of active partitions reaches the limit of 500 per stream, the remaining records go to the error prefix (activePartitionExceeded); the quota can be raised up to 2500 on request
  - Zero buffering is not available with dynamic partitioning

### Convert input data format in Amazon Data Firehose

- ID: `firehose-record-format-conversion`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/record-format-conversion.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 26
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Firehose can convert JSON input to Apache Parquet or Apache ORC before storing it in S3; it needs a deserializer, a schema from an AWS Glue table, and a serializer
  - Choose the OpenX JSON SerDe unless the input has timestamps it does not support; it accepts yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss[.S]'Z', epoch seconds and epoch milliseconds among others
  - The schema in the Glue Data Catalog should match the input structure; attributes not in the schema are not in the converted data
  - Several JSON documents in one record are accepted as {"a": 1}{"b": 1}, not as a JSON array

### Understand data delivery in Amazon Data Firehose

- ID: `firehose-basic-deliver`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/basic-deliver.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 26
- この出典が支える主張:
  - For S3, Firehose concatenates the incoming records of a buffer into one object, by default without any delimiter
  - Firehose uses at-least-once semantics for data delivery and retries can introduce duplicates, for all destination types except Amazon S3, Apache Iceberg Tables and Snowflake

### Configure backup settings (buffering hints)

- ID: `firehose-buffering-hints`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/create-configure-backup.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 26
- この出典が支える主張:
  - For an S3 destination the buffering size is 1 to 128 MB (default 5) and the interval 0 to 900 seconds (default 300); the first condition satisfied triggers delivery
  - S3 compression can be GZIP, Snappy, Zip, Hadoop-compatible Snappy, or none
  - With a buffer interval under 60 seconds Firehose uses multipart upload, which increases S3 PUT costs

### Handle data delivery failures

- ID: `firehose-retry`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/retry.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 26
- この出典が支える主張:
  - When delivery to S3 fails, Firehose keeps retrying for up to 24 hours; its maximum data storage time is 24 hours, after which the data is lost
  - Failed records go to the S3 error prefix only when Lambda processing or Parquet conversion fails

### PutRecord (Amazon Data Firehose API Reference)

- ID: `firehose-api-put-record`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/APIReference/API_PutRecord.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 26
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A record's data blob can be up to 1,000 KiB; by default a stream takes up to 2,000 transactions, 5,000 records, or 5 MB per second
  - Firehose buffers records before delivery; a common way to tell them apart at the destination is a delimiter such as a newline in the data
  - Re-invoking the Put API operations can result in data duplicates
  - Records are stored for 24 hours from the time they are added while Firehose tries to deliver them

### Use partition projection with Amazon Athena

- ID: `athena-partition-projection`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/partition-projection.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 26
- この出典が支える主張:

  - Enabling projection makes Athena ignore partition metadata registered for the table
  - A projected partition that does not exist in S3 returns no data and no error; if more than half of the projected partitions are empty, traditional partitions are recommended
  - Projection is used only when the table is queried through Athena

- この出典が支える主張:

### Cloudflare Workers Analytics Engine (overview, get started, limits, pricing, SQL API, sampling)

- この出典が支える主張:
  - Workers Analytics Engine has an API to write data points from Workers and a SQL API to query them; writeDataPoint() need not be awaited
  - A data point holds up to twenty blobs, twenty doubles and one index; at most 250 data points per Worker invocation; data is stored for three months
  - Queries operate on a single table; UNION and JOIN are not supported

### How DynamoDB global tables work

- ID: `mr-dynamodb-global-tables-how`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/V2globaltables_HowItWorks.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 28
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A global table has two or more replicas in different Regions, one per Region, all with the same table name and key schema
  - The default consistency mode is multi-Region eventual consistency (MREC), and the mode cannot be changed after creation
  - In MREC, item changes are replicated asynchronously, typically within a second or less
  - In MREC, simultaneous changes to one item in several Regions are resolved by the latest internal timestamp per item (last writer wins)
  - In MREC, a strongly consistent read may return stale data if the item was last updated in another Region, and a conditional write evaluates its condition against the item's version in the Region
  - In MRSC, a change is replicated synchronously to at least one other Region before the write returns, and conditional writes evaluate against the latest version
  - An MRSC global table spans exactly three Regions: three replicas, or two replicas and a witness that cannot be read or written
  - A write to an item being modified in another Region fails with ReplicatedWriteConflictException in MRSC and can be retried
  - TTL and local secondary indexes are not supported in MRSC; transactions are not supported in MRSC and are atomic only within one Region in MREC
  - MREC has an RPO equal to the replication delay; MRSC supports an RPO of zero
  - MREC publishes the ReplicationLatency metric per source and destination Region pair; MRSC does not
  - Global tables have a 99.999% availability SLA, single-Region tables 99.99%
  - AWS FIS can pause replication to and from a replica to simulate Region isolation
  - MRSC is available in Tokyo, Seoul and Osaka among other Regions
- 注記: This page says an MRSC table can combine any three of the listed Regions; the design guide (mr-dynamodb-global-tables-design) lists Region sets that cannot be mixed. Tokyo, Seoul and Osaka are in one set either way.

### Using DynamoDB global tables

- ID: `mr-dynamodb-global-tables-design`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/bp-global-table-design.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 28
- この出典が支える主張:
  - DynamoDB has no global endpoint: every request goes to a Regional endpoint and reaches the replica in that Region
  - MREC write conflicts are not recorded in CloudWatch or CloudTrail
  - There is no SLA on ReplicationLatency; a new item usually reaches all replicas within a second
  - Each item carries a private last-write timestamp, and an incoming replicated item is applied only if its timestamp is greater
  - Items are replicated individually, and the order of writes in a remote Region may differ from the source Region
  - The local Region accepts writes while another Region is offline, and pending replication is retried when it returns
  - With MRSC, a Region accepts reads and writes only while a second Region (replica or witness) is reachable; otherwise it serves eventually consistent reads only
  - MRSC Region sets: Tokyo, Seoul and Osaka form the AP set, and a table cannot span sets
  - MRSC was introduced in June 2025

### Write modes with DynamoDB global tables

- ID: `mr-dynamodb-write-modes`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/bp-global-table-design.prescriptive-guidance.writemodes.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 28
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Global tables are always active-active at the table level; treating one as active-passive is done by routing writes outside DynamoDB
  - Writing to one Region avoids conflicts in MREC and is what conditional expressions and transactions need
  - Writing to any Region suits MRSC tables, and MREC tables whose writes are idempotent assignments

### Evacuation processes

- ID: `mr-dynamodb-evacuation`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/bp-global-table-design.prescriptive-guidance.evacuation.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 28
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Moving the write Region of an MREC table means pausing writes, waiting for replication, then resuming in the new Region
  - No metric says with certainty that replication has completed; waiting ten times the recent maximum ReplicationLatency is given as typically sufficient for a healthy Region
  - When an MREC Region goes offline, its unreplicated writes are held and propagated after it returns, and a later update in the other Region suppresses them under last writer wins

### Understanding Amazon DynamoDB billing for global tables

- ID: `mr-dynamodb-global-tables-billing`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/global-tables-billing.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 28
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A write to a global table is billed as one replicated write request unit per replica table, in each replica's Region
  - Replicated write units are priced the same as single-Region write units
  - DynamoDB does not charge cross-Region data transfer for replication between the Regions of a global table
  - A witness incurs no replicated write, storage or transfer cost

### Best practices for global tables

- ID: `mr-dynamodb-global-tables-best-practices`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/globaltables-bestpractices.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 28
- この出典が支える主張:
  - CloudFormation cannot coordinate a global table across stacks: all replicas should be defined in one Region's stack
  - Changing a resource's type from AWS::DynamoDB::Table to AWS::DynamoDB::GlobalTable may delete the table
  - Deletion protection is enabled per replica
  - Point-in-time recovery on one replica may be enough for disaster recovery objectives

  - Two-way replication keeps buckets in two Regions in sync during a failover
  - Objects that existed before a rule was added are replicated with S3 Batch Replication, on demand

### What does Amazon S3 replicate?

- ID: `mr-s3-replication-what`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication-what-is-isnot-replicated.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 28
- この出典が支える主張:
  - By default S3 replicates objects created after the replication configuration is added
  - With the current configuration format, delete markers are not replicated by default
  - A DELETE that names a version ID is not replicated to the destination
  - Objects that are themselves replicas created by another rule are not replicated
  - Delete markers added by a lifecycle action are not replicated

### How Amazon Route 53 determines whether a health check is healthy

- ID: `mr-route53-health-determination`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover-determining-health-of-endpoints.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 28
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Health checkers in several locations each send requests every 10 or 30 seconds and do not coordinate
  - A health check is healthy while more than 18% of health checkers report the endpoint healthy; the value may change
  - For HTTP and HTTPS, a checker must connect within four seconds and receive a 2xx or 3xx status within two seconds after connecting

- ID: `mr-route53-health-values`

  - HTTPS health checks carry an additional charge, and the protocol cannot be changed after creation

  - The Init phase starts all extensions, bootstraps the runtime and runs the function's static code; it is limited to 10 seconds, and if it does not complete Lambda retries it at the first invocation with the configured function timeout
  - The 10-second limit does not apply to provisioned concurrency, SnapStart or Lambda Managed Instances
  - The function's timeout limits the entire Invoke phase, extensions included
  - After a failed invocation Lambda resets the environment and re-initializes it with the next invocation (a suppressed init), without reporting a separate Init phase in CloudWatch Logs
  - Lambda keeps an environment for some time after an invocation and terminates environments every few hours; objects declared outside the handler remain initialized while it is reused
  - Cold starts typically occur in under 1% of invocations and take from under 100 ms to over 1 second
  - The example REPORT and INIT_REPORT lines used as test fixtures, including Init Duration, Status and Error Type
  - Factors of initialization latency: package size including layers, the amount of initialization code, and the libraries' own setup; objects used only on some paths can be loaded lazily
  - For on-demand functions Lambda might occasionally initialize environments ahead of requests
- 注記: The page lists three Init tasks. Whether downloading the code and starting the environment are inside the reported Init Duration is not stated there.

### Understanding Lambda function scaling

- ID: `tune-lambda-concurrency`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-concurrency.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 29
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Concurrency = (average requests per second) x (average request duration in seconds)
  - An execution environment is busy for the whole of Init and Invoke and cannot process other requests meanwhile
  - The default account concurrency limit is 1,000 per Region, shared by all functions
  - Lambda always keeps 100 units for functions without reserved concurrency
  - Lambda enforces a requests-per-second limit of 10 times the concurrency, at the account and the function level
  - Reserved concurrency is both the maximum and the minimum for a function and is free of charge; provisioned concurrency pre-initializes environments and is charged
  - With provisioned concurrency a cold start can still occur when Lambda has to reset an environment
  - aws lambda get-account-settings returns ConcurrentExecutions and UnreservedConcurrentExecutions
- 注記: One paragraph of the page says a function can gain 500 concurrency every 10 seconds; the scaling page and the quotas page say 1,000. The chapter quotes the latter two.

### Lambda scaling behavior

- ID: `tune-lambda-scaling`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/scaling-behavior.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 29
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Per function and Region, concurrency scales by at most 1,000 execution environments every 10 seconds (or 10,000 requests per second every 10 seconds)
  - Requests that arrive faster than the function can scale, or at maximum concurrency, fail with a throttling error (429)

### Configuring provisioned concurrency for a function

- ID: `tune-lambda-provisioned`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/provisioned-concurrency.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 29
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Provisioned concurrency cannot be used with $LATEST; it is set on a version or an alias, and the event source must point at that qualifier
  - Provisioned concurrency cannot exceed the function's reserved concurrency
  - Initialization code runs at allocation time and again when Lambda recycles environments, and is billed even if the environment never serves a request
  - With provisioned concurrency Lambda logs a platform.initReport event in the JSON log format each time an environment is initialized
  - Excess traffic is served by on-demand environments; AWS_LAMBDA_INITIALIZATION_TYPE is provisioned-concurrency or on-demand
  - Lambda suggests a 10% buffer on top of the usual peak concurrency

### Data modeling foundations in DynamoDB

- ID: `model-dynamodb-foundations`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/data-modeling-foundations.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 30
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Single table design stores several entity types in one table; items with the same partition key (an item collection) are stored together, so one query can return several entity types
  - Listed disadvantages: backups are all or nothing, table encryption is shared, and every change goes to the stream even if only some entities are processed

### Using Global Secondary Indexes in DynamoDB

- ID: `model-dynamodb-gsi`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/GSI.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 30
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A global secondary index is updated asynchronously and eventually consistently; propagation is within a fraction of a second under normal conditions, and longer delays are possible
  - A global secondary index supports only eventually consistent reads, and GetItem and BatchGetItem cannot be used on it
  - Only items in which the index key attributes exist appear in the index
  - Index key attributes must be top-level String, Number, or Binary
  - Projection is KEYS_ONLY, INCLUDE, or ALL; a query on the index cannot fetch attributes that were not projected
  - Index write cost: one write to put a new entry, two when an index key attribute changes, one when only a projected attribute changes, none when neither keys nor projected attributes change
  - If an index has insufficient write capacity, writes to the base table are throttled
  - Index storage is billed in addition to the table's
  - Global secondary indexes support multi-attribute keys of up to four attributes each for the partition key and the sort key
- 注記: Multi-attribute keys are mentioned in the chapter but not used; they were not tried with cdkd 0.296.28 or DynamoDB Local 3.3.1.

### Managing Global Secondary Indexes in DynamoDB

- ID: `model-dynamodb-gsi-online`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/GSI.OnlineOps.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13

  - A skewed partition key on a new index can cause backfill and writes to throttle writes to the base table; Contributor Insights is suggested for seeing the distribution

### Amazon DynamoDB Transactions: How it works

- ID: `model-dynamodb-transactions`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/transaction-apis.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 30
- この出典が支える主張:
  - TransactWriteItems groups up to 100 actions on up to 100 distinct items, 4 MB in total, in one all-or-nothing operation within one account and Region
  - One transaction cannot target the same item with more than one action
  - Actions are Put, Update, Delete, and ConditionCheck
  - Each item in a transaction costs two underlying reads or writes, and the capacity is consumed even when the transaction is cancelled
  - A cancelled transaction fails with TransactionCanceledException, which lists CancellationReasons in the order of the request's items; the AWS SDKs do not retry it
  - A transaction conflicts with another ongoing transaction or write on the same item
  - A client token makes TransactWriteItems idempotent for 10 minutes
  - Isolation between a transaction and a Query or Scan is read-committed, not serializable
  - Changes of one transaction reach indexes and the stream gradually; stream consumers should not assume atomicity or ordering across its records
  - Transactions are not supported across Regions in global tables

### Using IAM with DynamoDB transactions

- ID: `model-dynamodb-transactions-iam`

- ID: `model-dynamodb-quotas`

  - Up to 5 local secondary indexes per table and a default of 20 global secondary indexes
  - Up to 100 attributes can be projected across all of a table's secondary indexes
  - Up to two simultaneous readers per stream shard for a table that is not a global table
  - DynamoDB counts 1 KB as 1024 bytes

### Change data capture for DynamoDB Streams

- ID: `model-dynamodb-streams`

- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 30
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A stream keeps item-level changes for up to 24 hours
  - Each stream record appears exactly once in the stream, and records for one item appear in the order of its modifications

  - StreamViewType is KEYS_ONLY, NEW_IMAGE, OLD_IMAGE, or NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES, and cannot be edited once set

### Understanding how the AWS AppConfig Agent Lambda extension works

- ID: `pd-appconfig-extension-how`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appconfig/latest/userguide/appconfig-integration-lambda-extensions-how-it-works.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 31
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The function calls the extension at an HTTP endpoint on localhost:2772; the extension keeps a local cache and calls AppConfig when the data is not cached
  - On each invocation the extension checks whether the poll interval has elapsed and, if so, checks AppConfig for newly deployed data
  - Each execution environment has its own cache

### Configuring the AWS AppConfig Agent Lambda extension

- ID: `pd-appconfig-extension-config`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appconfig/latest/userguide/appconfig-integration-lambda-extensions-config.html>

- この出典が支える主張:
  - AWS_APPCONFIG_EXTENSION_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS defaults to 45, AWS_APPCONFIG_EXTENSION_HTTP_PORT to 2772, AWS_APPCONFIG_EXTENSION_POLL_TIMEOUT_MILLIS to 3000 ms
  - When AppConfig does not answer within the poll timeout, the extension skips that poll and returns the previously cached data
  - AWS_APPCONFIG_EXTENSION_PREFETCH_LIST makes the extension retrieve a configuration, named by its /applications/.../environments/.../configurations/... path, before the function is initialized

### What is Service Quotas?

- ID: `limits-service-quotas-intro`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/servicequotas/latest/userguide/intro.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 32
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Quotas, also referred to as limits, are the maximum values for the resources, actions, and items in an AWS account; each service defines its quotas and their default values
  - The console shows whether a quota is adjustable; an applied quota is the value after an increase, the default value is the initial value AWS set
  - A quota applies to an account or to a Region; a global quota can be raised only from US East (N. Virginia)
  - Utilization is the percentage of a quota in use; the console graphs it after the account has been active for a period of time
  - Support might approve, deny, or partially approve an increase request

### Requesting a quota increase

- ID: `limits-service-quotas-increase`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/servicequotas/latest/userguide/request-quota-increase.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 32
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Smaller increases are usually approved automatically; larger requests go to Support and take time to review, process, approve and deploy
  - Quota increase requests do not receive priority support
  - aws service-quotas list-service-quotas --service-code <code> prints QuotaName, QuotaCode, Value and Adjustable for each quota
  - aws service-quotas request-service-quota-increase takes --service-code, --quota-code and --desired-value, and answers with a Status of PENDING
  - Requesting through the CLI needs permission to create a service-linked role (ServiceQuotasFullAccess or iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole)

### Lambda quotas

- ID: `limits-lambda-quotas`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/gettingstarted-limits.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 32
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Concurrent executions: default 1,000 per Region, can be increased up to tens of thousands
  - New AWS accounts have reduced concurrency and memory quotas; AWS raises them automatically based on usage
  - Function timeout is 900 seconds; the synchronous invocation payload is 6 MB each for request and response; these cannot be changed
  - Each instance of an execution environment can serve up to 10 requests per second, so the invocation limit is 10 times the concurrency
  - API Gateway's default throttle of 10,000 requests per second and Lambda's default concurrency of 1,000 do not match; the page recommends load testing to find the quota that limits first
  - Service quotas consist of hard limits, which cannot be changed, and soft limits, for which an increase can be requested

### Configuring reserved concurrency for a function

- ID: `limits-lambda-reserved-concurrency`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-concurrency.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 32
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Reserved concurrency is both the maximum and the minimum for a function: no other function can use it, and the function cannot scale past it
  - Configuring reserved concurrency incurs no additional charge
  - You can reserve up to the unreserved account concurrency minus 100; the remaining 100 are for functions without reserved concurrency
  - Setting reserved concurrency to 0 stops the function from processing any events
  - Concurrency = average requests per second x average request duration in seconds

### Lambda scaling behavior

- ID: `limits-lambda-scaling`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/scaling-behavior.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 32
- この出典が支える主張:
  - For each function in each Region, concurrency can grow by 1,000 execution environments every 10 seconds
  - Requests that arrive faster than the function can scale, or while it is at maximum concurrency, fail with a throttling error (429 status code)

### Throttle requests to your HTTP APIs for better throughput in API Gateway

- ID: `limits-apigw-http-throttling`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/http-api-throttling.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 32
- この出典が支える主張:
  - API Gateway throttles with the token bucket algorithm, where a token counts for a request
  - Throttles are applied on a best-effort basis and should be thought of as targets rather than guaranteed request ceilings
  - Past the rate and burst limits, clients may receive 429 Too Many Requests
  - Account-level limits apply to all APIs of the account in a Region; stage and route limits cannot exceed them
  - Route-level throttling is set with RouteSettings keyed by the route key, with ThrottlingBurstLimit and ThrottlingRateLimit
- 注記: The page does not show the body of a 429 or say whether it carries a Retry-After header.

  - Payload size: 10 MB, cannot be increased

### Amazon API Gateway quotas

- ID: `limits-apigw-account-quotas`

- 確認日: 2026-10-12

  - Throttle quota per account, per Region, across HTTP, REST and WebSocket APIs: 10,000 requests per second with a bucket of 5,000; can be increased (quota code L-8A5B8E43)
  - The burst quota is set by the API Gateway team from the account's rate quota and cannot be requested separately

### Usage plans and API keys for REST APIs in API Gateway

- ID: `limits-apigw-usage-plans`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-api-usage-plans.html>

### Error handling with DynamoDB

- ID: `limits-dynamodb-errors`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Programming.Errors.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 32
- この出典が支える主張:
  - ProvisionedThroughputExceededException, RequestLimitExceeded and ThrottlingException are HTTP 400 errors that are OK to retry
  - For on-demand tables ThrottlingException can be returned for any data plane operation; the error carries ThrottlingReason fields such as IndexWriteMaxOnDemandThroughputExceeded
  - After a 500 on a single-item write the write may or may not have happened; the application should read the item or use a condition before retrying
  - The page recommends stopping retries after about a minute

### Retry behavior (AWS SDKs and Tools Reference Guide)

- ID: `limits-sdk-retry-behavior`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdkref/latest/guide/feature-retry-behavior.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 32
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The page describes a retry behaviour that needs AWS_NEW_RETRIES_2026=true until it becomes the default
  - Retry modes: standard (default), adaptive (adds a client-side rate limiter that can delay first attempts; not recommended as a general default), legacy (not available in JavaScript)
  - Max attempts defaults to 3 including the first; DynamoDB clients default to 4 under the described behaviour
  - delay = random(0, 1) x min(20,000 ms, base x 2^retry); base is 50 ms for transient errors and 1,000 ms for throttling errors
  - Retry quota: 500 tokens, 14 per transient retry, 5 per throttling retry, 1 restored by a first-try success; typically scoped to one client instance
  - With 3 attempts the quota starts to drain above roughly 22% sustained transient failures or 32% throttling
  - Full jitter spreads retries so that clients that failed together do not retry together
- 注記: Read again for chapter 32. The installed @smithy/util-retry 4.6.2 uses the older numbers (100 ms / 500 ms bases, costs 5 and 10) unless the variable is set; see limits-smithy-util-retry.

### @smithy/util-retry 4.6.2 (installed package, with @smithy/core 3.35.2)

- ID: `limits-smithy-util-retry`
- URL: <https://www.npmjs.com/package/@smithy/util-retry/v/4.6.2>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 32
- この出典が支える主張:
  - DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS is 3 and DEFAULT_RETRY_MODE is standard
  - Without the opt-in: base delay 100 ms, throttling base delay 500 ms, maximum delay 20 s, 500 retry tokens, 5 per throttling retry, 10 per transient retry, 1 restored by a success without retry
  - The backoff is Math.floor(Math.random() x min(base x 2^i, 20,000))
  - ProvisionedThroughputExceededException, ThrottlingException, RequestLimitExceeded and TooManyRequestsException are classified as throttling errors
  - @aws-sdk/core 3.978.2 turns the 2026 behaviour on when AWS_NEW_RETRIES_2026 is "true"; the DynamoDB client then defaults to 4 attempts

### Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter (Amazon Builders' Library)

- ID: `limits-builders-library-retries`
- URL: <https://builder.aws.com/content/3EumjoZascWd1oZiEgL8ORlv3qE/timeouts-retries-and-backoff-with-jitter>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 32
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Retries are selfish: they spend more of the server's capacity to improve one client's odds, and make an overload worse
  - Retries at every layer multiply: five layers with three retries each can raise load on the bottom layer 243 times
  - Retries can be limited locally with a token bucket; the AWS SDK adopted this in 2016
  - A call with side effects is safe to retry only if the API is idempotent
- 注記: aws.amazon.com/builders-library/timeouts-retries-and-backoff-with-jitter/ redirects here. Read through a summary of the page, not word for word.

### Exponential Backoff And Jitter (AWS Architecture Blog)

- ID: `limits-backoff-jitter-blog`
- URL: <https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/architecture/exponential-backoff-and-jitter/>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 32
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Backoff without jitter takes more work and more time than any jittered variant
  - Full jitter needs the least work among the variants compared
- 注記: The formulas are in images on the page and were not read. The full-jitter formula in this chapter is the one in the SDK reference and the installed package.

### Amazon EC2 Testing Policy

- ID: `limits-ec2-testing-policy`
- URL: <https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/testing/>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 32
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The guidelines concern high volume network tests run from EC2 instances; a network stress test sends a large volume of legitimate or test traffic to a specific intended target application that is expected to handle it
  - Tests that purposefully attempt to overwhelm the target with floods are DDoS tests, and volumetric network-based DDoS simulations are prohibited from EC2
  - Endpoints hosted in AWS should be in the same Region as the test
  - AWS may shape traffic where surges exceed 25 Gbps or 100 Gbps, depending on the paths and Regions
- 注記: The page states no request-rate threshold and no approval step for a stress test. It says nothing about tests sent from outside AWS.

### AWS Customer Support Policy for Penetration Testing

- ID: `limits-pentest-policy`
- URL: <https://aws.amazon.com/security/penetration-testing/>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12
- 参照する章: 32
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Security assessments of the listed services need no prior approval; API Gateway, Lambda and CloudFront are on the list
  - Prohibited: DoS and DDoS, simulated or not, port flooding, protocol flooding, and request flooding (login request flooding, API request flooding)
  - Network stress testing or load testing is a performance test that sends a large volume of legitimate or test traffic to a specific intended target application; the page sends readers to the stress test policy

### GetCostAndUsage (AWS Billing and Cost Management API Reference)

- ID: `limits-ce-get-cost-and-usage`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-cost-management/latest/APIReference/API_GetCostAndUsage.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-12

- この出典が支える主張:
  - GroupBy takes up to two groups, of type DIMENSION, TAG, COST_CATEGORY or PRODUCT_ATTRIBUTE; grouping by TAG returns all tag values, including empty strings
  - The sample response shows a tag group key in the form key$value (Environment$Prod)
  - TimePeriod's start is inclusive and its end exclusive; Granularity is DAILY, MONTHLY or HOURLY
  - Amounts are returned as strings; the sample request is sent to ce.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
  - LimitExceededException: too many calls in a short period of time

### Automate cluster infrastructure with EKS Auto Mode

- ID: `eks-auto-mode`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/automode.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 34
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Auto Mode manages compute autoscaling, pod and service networking, application load balancing, cluster DNS, and block storage as core components instead of add-ons
  - Nodes are EC2 managed instances running Bottlerocket variants; SSH and SSM access to them is not allowed
  - Nodes have a maximum lifetime of 21 days, which can be reduced
  - Upgrades respect Pod Disruption Budgets; intervention might be required if a blocking budget prevents an update
  - The EKS Pod Identity Agent does not have to be installed on Auto Mode clusters
  - Auto scaling relies on Karpenter
  - Since April 22, 2026 new managed instances are hidden by default from EC2 console views and list APIs

### Create a Node Pool for EKS Auto Mode

- ID: `eks-auto-node-pool`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/create-node-pool.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 34
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The built-in system and general-purpose node pools cannot be modified, only enabled or disabled
  - A cluster can be created with nodePools and nodeRoleArn both empty; then no default NodeClass exists, and a custom NodeClass, an access entry for its role, and a custom NodePool are needed
  - A NodePool is a karpenter.sh/v1 object whose nodeClassRef names group eks.amazonaws.com, kind NodeClass
  - Supported requirement labels include kubernetes.io/arch, karpenter.sh/capacity-type, and node.kubernetes.io/instance-type
  - By default Auto Mode consolidates underutilized instances, terminates instances after 336 hours, and sets one disruption budget of 10% of nodes
  - limits.cpu and limits.memory bound what a node pool may provision

### Enable or Disable Built-in NodePools

- ID: `eks-auto-builtin-node-pools`

- 参照する章: 34
- この出典が支える主張:
  - general-purpose uses only the amd64 architecture; system supports amd64 and arm64 and carries a CriticalAddonsOnly taint
  - Both built-in pools use on-demand capacity, the C, M, and R families, and generation 5 or newer
  - At least one built-in pool must be enabled for EKS to provision the default NodeClass

### Create a Node Class for Amazon EKS

- ID: `eks-auto-node-class`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/create-node-class.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 34
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A NodeClass is an eks.amazonaws.com/v1 object with role, subnetSelectorTerms, securityGroupSelectorTerms, ephemeralStorage, and advancedNetworking
  - advancedNetworking.associatePublicIPAddress controls whether instances get a public IP address; unset, it follows the subnet's MapPublicIpOnLaunch
  - A custom node class needs an access entry of type EC2 with the AmazonEKSAutoNodePolicy access policy, or its nodes cannot join; the page gives the CloudFormation for it
  - subnetSelectorTerms and securityGroupSelectorTerms select by tags or by id; nodes are distributed across the matching subnets
  - ephemeralStorage.size accepts 1 to 59000Gi; the specification example shows 80Gi, iops 3000 and throughput 125

### Create an IngressClass to configure an Application Load Balancer

- ID: `eks-auto-alb`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/auto-configure-alb.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 34
- この出典が支える主張:
  - An IngressClass with controller eks.amazonaws.com/alb and an IngressClassParams (eks.amazonaws.com/v1) make Auto Mode create an ALB for an Ingress
  - IngressClassParams fields include scheme, subnets.ids, and subnets.matchTags (filters with a key and a list of values); targetType defaults to ip
  - IngressClass annotations cannot configure the load balancer; annotations on individual Ingress resources can
  - The page lists the Ingress annotations that are not supported; the health check and target group attribute annotations are not on that list
  - Deleting the Ingress makes Auto Mode delete the load balancer
  - The page does not mention the Gateway API
- 注記: Whether each health check annotation of the open source controller takes effect under Auto Mode was not confirmed beyond its absence from the unsupported list.

### Learn how EKS Pod Identity grants pods access to AWS services

- ID: `eks-pod-identity`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/pod-identities.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 34
- この出典が支える主張:
  - An association maps an IAM role to a service account in a namespace of a cluster
  - The role's trust policy names the service principal pods.eks.amazonaws.com; no OIDC provider is involved
  - EKS sets environment variables in the pod's containers so that the AWS SDKs use the Pod Identity credentials
  - Up to 5,000 associations per cluster
  - Associations are eventually consistent, with delays of several seconds
  - Pod Identity is not available for pods on Fargate or on Windows instances
  - Containers are not a security boundary; pods on the same node share a kernel

### Understand the Kubernetes version lifecycle on EKS

- ID: `eks-versions`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/kubernetes-versions.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 34
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A minor version is in standard support for 14 months after its release on EKS, then in extended support for 12 months
  - Extended support is enabled by default; at its end the cluster is auto-upgraded to the oldest version still in extended support
  - On 2026-10-13 standard support covered 1.37, 1.36, 1.35, and 1.34; extended support covered 1.33, 1.32, and 1.31
  - The release calendar: 1.37 leaves standard support on December 1, 2027; 1.34 on December 2, 2026
  - A cluster upgraded in place can be rolled back to the previous minor version within 7 days
  - Billing for extended support starts at the beginning of the day (UTC) that standard support ends

### Prevent increased cluster costs by disabling EKS extended support

- ID: `eks-disable-extended-support`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/disable-extended-support.html>

- 参照する章: 34
- この出典が支える主張:
  - With the upgrade policy STANDARD the cluster is automatically upgraded to the next version at the end of standard support
  - Extended support cannot be disabled once the cluster has entered it

### Update existing cluster to new Kubernetes version

- ID: `eks-update-cluster`

- この出典が支える主張:
  - A cluster is updated one minor version at a time
  - An update needs up to five available IP addresses in the cluster's subnets
  - kubectl must be within one minor version of the control plane
  - After the 7-day window a cluster cannot be downgraded

### cdkd 0.296.28: how AWS::EKS types are routed

### Kubernetes: Deployments

- ID: `k8s-deployment`
- URL: <https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/deployment/>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 34
- この出典が支える主張:
  - maxUnavailable is calculated from a percentage by rounding down, maxSurge by rounding up; both default to 25%
  - maxUnavailable cannot be 0 if maxSurge is 0, and the reverse
  - progressDeadlineSeconds defaults to 600; Kubernetes takes no action on a stalled Deployment other than to report a status condition
  - minReadySeconds is how long a new pod must be ready before it counts as available

### Kubernetes: Specifying a Disruption Budget for your Application

- ID: `k8s-pdb`
- URL: <https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/run-application/configure-pdb/>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 34
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A budget has a selector and exactly one of minAvailable and maxUnavailable, each a number or a percentage
  - A minAvailable percentage rounds up; a maxUnavailable percentage rounds up the number of pods that may be disrupted
  - A budget does not guarantee the number of pods: a node may still fail

### Kubernetes: Disruptions

- ID: `k8s-disruptions`
- URL: <https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/disruptions/>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 34
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Draining a node is a voluntary disruption and goes through the eviction API, which respects budgets; deleting pods or deployments directly bypasses them
  - Pods unavailable because of a rolling upgrade count against the budget, but a Deployment is not limited by budgets when it rolls
  - Involuntary disruptions cannot be prevented by a budget, but count against it
  - The AlwaysAllow unhealthy pod eviction policy is recommended so that a misbehaving application cannot block a drain

### Kubernetes: API-initiated Eviction

- ID: `k8s-api-eviction`
- URL: <https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/api-eviction/>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 34
- この出典が支える主張:
  - An eviction the budget does not allow is answered with 429 Too Many Requests

### Kubernetes: Pod Lifecycle

- ID: `k8s-pod-lifecycle`
- URL: <https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle/>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 34
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The grace period defaults to 30 seconds; a preStop hook runs first and its time counts against the grace period
  - The kubelet sends TERM to process 1 of each container, and KILL when the grace period has expired
  - At the same time as the kubelet starts the graceful shutdown, the control plane removes the pod from EndpointSlices

### Lambda Managed Instances

- ID: `lmi-overview`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-managed-instances.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 35
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Lambda Managed Instances runs Lambda functions on current-generation EC2 instances in your account without you managing instance lifecycles, OS and runtime patching, routing, load balancing, or scaling policies
  - Capacity providers are the foundation: create a capacity provider, create a function attached to it, publish a function version
  - When a function version is published with a capacity provider, Lambda launches three instances by default for AZ resiliency and starts three execution environments before marking the version ACTIVE
  - One execution environment handles multiple invocations at the same time; Lambda (default) runs at most one invocation per execution environment
  - Managed Instances use containers on EC2 Nitro instances for isolation rather than Firecracker; the capacity provider is the security boundary
  - The instances are EC2 managed instances: the Operator field appears in DescribeInstances, they carry the aws:lambda:capacity-provider tag, they cannot be terminated directly, and they are hidden from the EC2 console and list operations by default while remaining billable
  - Pricing is EC2-based with a 15% management fee on top of the EC2 instance cost; EC2 Savings Plans, Reserved Instances and other EC2 discounts apply to the EC2 compute only, not to the management fee
  - Lambda Managed Instances scales asynchronously on CPU resource utilization, without cold starts, and scales to the configured minimum of execution environments without traffic; Lambda (default) scales to zero
  - By default Managed Instances scale to handle traffic doubling within five minutes

### Core concepts

- ID: `lmi-core-concepts`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-managed-instances-core-concepts.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 35
- この出典が支える主張:
  - All functions assigned to the same capacity provider must be mutually trusted
  - If traffic more than doubles within 5 minutes, throttles may occur while Lambda scales up
  - Users need lambda:PassCapacityProvider to assign functions to a capacity provider

### Capacity providers

- ID: `lmi-capacity-providers`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-managed-instances-capacity-providers.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 35
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A capacity provider takes a VPC configuration (1 to 16 subnets, security groups), an operator role, and optionally instance requirements and a scaling configuration
  - Architectures is x86_64 or arm64, default x86_64; AllowedInstanceTypes and ExcludedInstanceTypes are mutually exclusive
  - Lambda chooses instance types by default, and restricting them might result in lower availability
  - MaxVCpuCount defaults to 400; ScalingMode is Auto or Manual
  - KmsKeyArn is a KMS key for EBS encryption, defaulting to an AWS managed key
  - A capacity provider that has function versions attached cannot be deleted
  - States: Pending, Active, Failed, Deleting

### Scaling Lambda Managed Instances

- ID: `lmi-scaling`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-managed-instances-scaling.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 35
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Managed Instances does not scale when invocations arrive and does not support cold starts; it scales asynchronously on CPU utilization and multi-concurrency saturation
  - The smallest supported function size is 2 GB and 1 vCPU
  - Maximum concurrency per execution environment can be raised to 64 per vCPU
  - The default minimum is 3 execution environments across Availability Zones with no default maximum; values below 3 reduce Availability Zone redundancy
  - MinExecutionEnvironments and MaxExecutionEnvironments range from 0 to 15000 and are set together; a minimum of 0 is valid only when the maximum is also 0, which deactivates the function version
  - A deactivated function does not scale back up with traffic; Lambda terminates an instance once it has no active execution environments, and instance charges continue until termination completes
  - The Router and Scaler are shared Lambda components; a Lambda Agent runs on each instance
  - The default target keeps enough headroom for traffic to double within 5 minutes without throttles
  - For testing or development you might choose smaller instance types

### Lambda Managed Instances runtimes

- ID: `lmi-runtimes`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-managed-instances-runtimes.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 35
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Supported: Java 21 and later, Python 3.13 and later, Node.js 22 and later, .NET 8 and later, and Rust on the OS-only runtime provided.al2023 and later
  - Node.js uses worker threads with asynchronous execution; Python uses one process per concurrent request; Java uses OS threads

### Node.js runtime for Lambda Managed Instances

- ID: `lmi-nodejs-runtime`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-managed-instances-nodejs-runtime.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 35
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Function initialization occurs once per worker thread; concurrent requests on the same worker thread share the handler object and global state
  - For Node.js the default maximum is 64 concurrent requests per vCPU; the number of worker threads follows the vCPU count or AWS_LAMBDA_NODEJS_WORKER_COUNT
  - For mutable objects, avoid global state or use AsyncLocalStorage; AWS SDK clients are async safe
  - On Node.js 22, callback-based handlers cannot be used with Managed Instances
  - /tmp is shared across all concurrent requests in the execution environment
  - Functions on Managed Instances always use the structured JSON log format, which carries the requestId
  - context.awsRequestId and context.xRayTraceId are async-safe; the _X_AMZN_TRACE_ID environment variable is not supported
  - process.on() cannot be used with worker threads, so a function cannot subscribe to SIGTERM
  - Minimum versions: AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 3.933.0, Powertools for AWS Lambda (TypeScript) 2.29.0

### Networking for Lambda Managed Instances

- ID: `lmi-networking`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-managed-instances-networking.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 35
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Connectivity is needed for functions to reach resources outside the VPC and for transmitting telemetry to CloudWatch Logs and X-Ray
  - Three options: public subnet with an internet gateway, VPC endpoints, private subnet with a NAT gateway
  - VPC endpoints are recommended for production with strict security requirements and are billed per endpoint, per Availability Zone, and per GB

### Lambda operator role for Lambda Managed Instances

- ID: `lmi-operator-role`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-managed-instances-operator-role.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 35
