  - The role needs at least the AWSLambdaManagedEC2ResourceOperator managed policy; the page prints its statements (ec2:RunInstances, ec2:CreateTags, ec2:AttachNetworkInterface, ec2:CreateNetworkInterface, several ec2:Describe*, logs:CreateLogGroup, logs:CreateLogStream, logs:PutLogEvents)
  - The service-linked role is created with the first capacity provider, needs iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole for lambda.amazonaws.com, and holds ec2:TerminateInstances and ec2:DescribeInstances

### Lambda Managed Instances quotas

- ID: `lmi-quotas`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-managed-instances-quotas.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 35
- この出典が支える主張:
  - 1,000 capacity providers per account; 100 function versions per capacity provider (cannot be increased); 15,000 vCPUs per capacity provider
  - Capacity provider APIs: 15 read requests and 1 write request per second, not adjustable
  - EC2 quotas apply as well: vCPU limits, EBS volume limits, and free IP addresses in the subnets
  - Event source mappings on Managed Instances support SQS, DynamoDB Streams, Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon MSK, and self-managed Apache Kafka

### Understanding the Lambda Managed Instances execution environment

- ID: `lmi-execution-environment`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-managed-instances-execution-environment.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 35
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The execution environment stays active between invocations instead of being frozen
  - The configured timeout applies to each invocation; when one times out Lambda reports it failed but does not stop the code, which keeps running and keeps a runtime worker busy
  - If all runtime workers are busy, new invocations are rejected until one is free
  - Initialization may take up to the larger of 130 seconds and the function timeout
  - Unhealthy containers are terminated and replaced rather than reset

### Troubleshooting Lambda Managed Instances

- ID: `lmi-troubleshooting`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-managed-instances-troubleshooting.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 35
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Throttles are HTTP 429; the throttle reason metrics tell CPU, memory, disk and concurrency apart
  - Node.js state isolation issues: global variables are shared across concurrent invocations on the same worker thread
  - Missing logs are a VPC connectivity problem: the instances need a path to CloudWatch Logs, for example the com.amazonaws.<region>.logs interface endpoint with private DNS
  - A function version stays pending while Lambda launches three instances and starts three execution environments; this typically takes several minutes
  - Metrics are in the AWS/Lambda namespace with the dimensions CapacityProviderName, FunctionName, or InstanceType

  - On Managed Instances, asynchronous and event source mapping invocations may run up to 5,400 seconds (90 minutes); the general function timeout is 900 seconds
  - Managed Instances use a file descriptor limit of 4,096 and the process and thread limits of Bottlerocket

### Get validated JSON results from models

- ID: `br36-structured-output`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/structured-output.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 36
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Two mechanisms: a JSON Schema output format (outputConfig.textFormat for Converse) and strict tool use (strict: true on a tool definition)
  - Supported subset of JSON Schema Draft 2020-12; not supported: recursive schemas, external $ref, minimum/maximum/multipleOf, minLength/maxLength, additionalProperties other than false; array minItems only 0 and 1
  - A new schema is compiled on first use, which may take up to a few minutes; compiled grammars are cached for 24 hours
  - Supported with Converse/ConverseStream, InvokeModel, cross-Region inference, and (according to this page) batch inference; model support is on each model card
  - Structured outputs are incompatible with citations for Anthropic models
- 注記: This page lists batch inference as supported. The batch inference overview page says batch does not support tool calling or structured output. The two pages disagree; the chapter says so.

### Detect and filter harmful content by using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails

- ID: `br36-guardrails`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 36
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Filters: content filters (Hate, Insults, Sexual, Violence, Misconduct, Prompt Attack), denied topics, word filters, sensitive information filters, contextual grounding checks, Automated Reasoning checks
  - A guardrail has a working draft and numbered versions; it is used by passing its ID and version on an inference call, or alone through ApplyGuardrail
  - Reasoning content blocks are not evaluated

### Include a guardrail with the Converse API

- ID: `br36-guardrails-converse`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-use-converse-api.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 36
- この出典が支える主張:
  - guardrailConfig carries guardrailIdentifier, guardrailVersion, trace; ConverseStream adds streamProcessingMode
  - With tools, a guardrail does not evaluate toolResult content, tool definitions, or the toolUse input the model generates; it evaluates text and guardContent
  - When blocked: stopReason guardrail_intervened, the configured blocked message is returned as the output (in the streamed message for ConverseStream), the trace is in metadata, and the documented example shows zero tokens
  - Once any guardContent block is present, only guardContent blocks are evaluated; a system prompt is evaluated only inside guardContent

### Configure streaming response behavior to filter content

- ID: `br36-guardrails-streaming`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-streaming.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 36
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Synchronous mode (default) buffers and scans chunks before they are sent, adding latency; asynchronous mode sends chunks immediately and blocks later chunks once a violation is found
  - Masking of sensitive information is not supported in asynchronous mode

- ID: `br36-api-guardrail-config`

### Prompt caching for faster model inference

- ID: `br36-prompt-caching`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-caching.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 36
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Implicit caching is best effort; explicit caching uses cache checkpoints, with a per-model minimum prefix (512 to 4,096 tokens) counted cumulatively across tools, system and messages
  - Nova 2 Lite: minimum 1K tokens, 4 checkpoints, 5-minute TTL, checkpoints in system and messages, at most 20K cached tokens. Claude Haiku 4.5: 4,096 tokens, 4 checkpoints, 5 minutes or 1 hour, system, messages and tools
  - The TTL resets on each cache hit; a checkpoint in front of too few tokens still succeeds but is not cached; a ttl field on a model that supports only 5 minutes can cause a ValidationException
  - Usage reports cacheReadInputTokens and cacheWriteInputTokens; inputTokens then counts only non-cached input; total input = inputTokens + cacheReadInputTokens + cacheWriteInputTokens
  - Checkpoints are processed in the order tools, system, messages; prompt caching is not supported with batch inference

  - CachePointBlock: type default, optional ttl 5m | 1h

### How tokens are counted in Amazon Bedrock

- ID: `br36-token-burndown`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-token-burndown.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 36
- この出典が支える主張:
  - At the start of a request, total input tokens plus max_tokens is deducted from the tokens-per-minute quota; at the end the deduction becomes InputTokenCount + CacheWriteInputTokenCount + OutputTokenCount x burndown rate
  - Burndown rate for output tokens: 5x for Anthropic models version 4.7 and below, 1x for models not listed; cache reads do not count toward the quota

### What is AWS Data Pipeline?

- ID: `dm-datapipeline-what`

- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 38
- この出典が支える主張:
  - AWS Data Pipeline is no longer available to new customers; existing customers can continue to use the service as normal
  - The service is in maintenance mode and no new features or region expansions are planned
  - A pipeline definition specifies the business logic, a pipeline schedules and runs tasks by creating Amazon EC2 instances, and Task Runner polls for tasks and performs them
  - Tasks can be dependent on the successful completion of previous tasks

### Migrating workloads from AWS Data Pipeline

- ID: `dm-datapipeline-migration`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datapipeline/latest/DeveloperGuide/migration.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 38
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Typical Data Pipeline use cases can be migrated to AWS Glue, AWS Step Functions, or Amazon MWAA
  - Step Functions is recommended for a serverless orchestration service that charges per task execution and orchestrates other AWS services
  - The concept table maps pipelines to workflows, activities to states and tasks, attempts to catchers and retriers, and the pipeline schedule to EventBridge Scheduler
  - Glue is recommended when the pipeline came from a console template such as exporting a DynamoDB table to S3; MWAA when workflows are written in Python on Apache Airflow

### What is AWS DataSync?

- ID: `dm-datasync-what`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/what-is-datasync.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 38
- この出典が支える主張:
  - DataSync is a file transfer service for file or object data to, from, and between AWS storage services
  - The other clouds it lists include Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage, and Cloudflare R2 Storage
  - DataSync includes encryption in transit and data integrity validation

### How AWS DataSync transfers work

- ID: `dm-datasync-how`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/how-datasync-transfer-works.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 38
- この出典が支える主張:
  - An agent is a VM appliance; a location is where data is copied from or to; a task describes a transfer; a task execution is one run of it
  - By default DataSync prepares a transfer by scanning both locations to find differences; with transfer-all it does not compare
  - DataSync always performs integrity checks during a transfer and can verify again at the end
  - A file written to during a transfer can be detected at verification, and getting its latest version needs another run
  - Transfers between AWS storage services in one account need no agent and stay on the AWS network

### Choosing a task mode for your data transfer

- ID: `dm-datasync-task-mode`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/choosing-task-mode.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 38
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Enhanced mode lists, prepares, transfers, and verifies in parallel and works with virtually unlimited numbers of objects; Basic mode does these sequentially and is subject to quotas
  - Enhanced mode verifies only transferred data; Basic mode verifies all data by default
  - Enhanced mode logs are structured JSON; Basic mode logs are unstructured
  - The task mode cannot be changed after the task is created
  - Creating an Enhanced mode task needs iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole

### Where can I transfer my data with AWS DataSync?

- ID: `dm-datasync-locations`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/working-with-locations.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 38
- この出典が支える主張:
  - S3 to S3 needs no agent in Basic and Enhanced mode, within one account and across accounts
  - Other cloud storage to S3 needs an agent only in Basic mode; NFS and SMB always need an agent
  - Between AWS storage services in different Regions, one of the two locations must be in the Region where DataSync is used
  - Data transferred between Regions is billed as data transfer out from the source Region to the destination Region

### Do I need an AWS DataSync agent?

- ID: `dm-datasync-agent`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/do-i-need-datasync-agent.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 38
- この出典が支える主張:
  - An agent is needed between AWS storage and on-premises storage, and between EFS or FSx and other clouds
  - No agent is needed between AWS storage services in the same account, or between S3 and object storage in other clouds

### Configuring AWS DataSync transfers with Amazon S3

- ID: `dm-datasync-s3-location`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/create-s3-location.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 38
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The IAM permissions a source location role and a destination location role need, action by action
  - New objects get the storage class of the destination location; existing objects keep theirs unless the task transfers all data
  - In a versioned bucket DataSync creates a new version when the source object is modified, and only the latest version of a source object is transferred
  - DataSync makes LIST, HEAD, GET, PUT, and COPY requests on every run, HEAD requests even when nothing moves
  - Standard-IA, One Zone-IA, and Glacier Instant Retrieval can charge for overwriting, deleting, or retrieving, and objects under 128 KB are stored in S3 Standard instead; archived objects must be restored before DataSync can read them
  - A bucket encrypted with SSE-C cannot be accessed; SSE-KMS needs the role in the key policy

### Tutorial: Transferring data between Amazon S3 buckets across AWS accounts

- ID: `dm-datasync-cross-account`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/tutorial_s3-s3-cross-account-transfer.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 38
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The DataSync role, both locations, and the task are created in the source account
  - The destination bucket's policy names that role and allows ten S3 actions on the bucket and its objects
  - ACLs are disabled on the destination bucket so that its account owns the objects
  - A cross-account location cannot be created in the console; create-location-s3 is run with the destination bucket's Region
  - To avoid a network connection error the task is created in the same Region as the destination location; with Basic mode across accounts and Regions the alternative is an Enhanced mode task

### DataSync API: Options

- ID: `dm-datasync-options`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/API_Options.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 38
- この出典が支える主張:
  - TransferMode CHANGED (default) or ALL; OverwriteMode ALWAYS (default) or NEVER; PreserveDeletedFiles PRESERVE (default) or REMOVE
  - VerifyMode ONLY_FILES_TRANSFERRED, POINT_IN_TIME_CONSISTENT (default for Basic mode, not supported in Enhanced mode), or NONE
  - ObjectTags PRESERVE (default) or NONE; LogLevel OFF, BASIC, or TRANSFER
  - OverwriteMode NEVER protects against overwriting changes made in the destination

### Configuring how to handle files, objects, and metadata

- ID: `dm-datasync-metadata-options`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/configure-metadata.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 38
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A task cannot both delete data in the destination and transfer all data, because transfer-all does not scan the destination
  - Deleting or overwriting objects can incur minimum storage duration, retrieval, or early deletion charges in some storage classes

### Understanding how DataSync handles file and object metadata

- ID: `dm-datasync-metadata`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/metadata-copied.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 38
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Between object storage and Amazon S3, DataSync copies user-defined metadata, object tags, and Content-Disposition, Content-Encoding, Content-Language, and Content-Type
  - DataSync does not copy object ACLs, prior object versions, or the Last-Modified key

### Configuring how AWS DataSync verifies data integrity

- ID: `dm-datasync-verify`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/configure-data-verification-options.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 38
- この出典が支える主張:
  - During a transfer DataSync uses checksum verification; verification at the end is an additional, configurable step
  - Verify-all checks the entire source and destination at the end and cannot be used with Enhanced mode or with Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive destinations

### Transferring specific files, objects, and folders by using filters

- ID: `dm-datasync-filters`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/filtering.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 38
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A filter is patterns joined by a pipe; filters are case sensitive and relative to the source location path
  - /dir and /dir/ both match the folder and its content, and a slash in an S3 key is treated as a folder
  - Include filters support the wildcard only as the rightmost character of a pattern
  - A backslash escapes *, | and \
- 注記: The page does not say whether a destination object that a filter excludes is deleted when deleted files are removed.

### Transferring specific files or objects by using a manifest

- ID: `dm-datasync-manifest`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/transferring-with-manifest.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 38
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A manifest is a CSV file listing the exact files or objects to transfer, optionally with an S3 version ID
  - A manifest cannot be combined with filters, and DataSync deletes nothing in the destination when one is used
  - The maximum manifest size with Enhanced mode is 20 GB

### AWS DataSync quotas

- ID: `dm-datasync-quotas`

- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 38

  - 100 tasks per account and Region (adjustable)
  - Basic mode between AWS storage services: 25 million files, objects, and directories per execution, with S3 prefixes counted as directories; 50 million with on-premises or other clouds

### What is AWS Database Migration Service?

- ID: `dbmig-dms-what-is`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/Welcome.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 39
- この出典が支える主張:
  - AWS DMS creates the tables and associated primary keys if they don't exist on the target; you can create the target tables yourself
  - DMS Schema Conversion is for migrating to a different database engine: it assesses and converts source schemas to a new target engine

### High-level view of AWS DMS

- ID: `dbmig-dms-high-level`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Introduction.HighLevelView.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 39
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A task can consist of three phases: full load, application of cached changes, and ongoing replication (CDC)
  - AWS DMS doesn't capture changes for a given table until the full load for that table is started, so the point when change capture starts differs per table
  - After all cached changes are applied the tables are transactionally consistent and DMS moves to ongoing replication, applying changes as transactions
  - At steady state you can shut down your applications, allow any remaining transactions to be applied to the target, and bring your applications up pointing at the target
  - With the minimalist approach AWS DMS creates tables, primary keys, and in some cases unique indexes, and no other objects

### Components of AWS DMS

- ID: `dbmig-dms-components`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Introduction.Components.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 39
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A replication instance is a managed Amazon EC2 instance that hosts one or more replication tasks, and comes with 50 GB or 100 GB of storage depending on its class
  - The three migration types are full load, full load + CDC, and CDC only
  - Target table preparation modes are do nothing, drop tables on target, and truncate
  - If changes are captured faster than they can be applied, pending changes spill to disk on the replication instance and target latency exceeds source latency

  - The third-party managed PostgreSQL services listed are Microsoft Azure PostgreSQL Flexible Server and Google Cloud for PostgreSQL
  - The page lists neither Aurora DSQL, nor SQLite, nor Neon

### Using a PostgreSQL database as an AWS DMS source

- ID: `dbmig-dms-source-postgresql`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Source.PostgreSQL.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 39
- この出典が支える主張:
  - For an RDS for PostgreSQL source, CDC needs rds.logical_replication set to 1 in the parameter group, a static parameter that requires a reboot
  - The user on an AWS-managed source must have the rds_superuser role and the rds_replication role; using the master account is not recommended
  - A captured table must have a primary key; without one AWS DMS ignores DELETE and UPDATE operations for that table
  - For full load and CDC tasks AWS DMS uses logical replication slots to retain WAL until the logs are decoded; on restart (not resume) the slot is recreated
  - Slots remain open even when the task is no longer running; DMS drops a slot it created when the task is deleted
  - DMS uses the pglogical plugin if it is available on the source and test_decoding otherwise
  - If max_slot_wal_keep_size is set and a slot's restart_lsn falls behind by more than that size, the DMS task fails
  - Changes held in a slot can cause elevated disk usage; AWS recommends space usage alarms on the source
  - HeartbeatEnable mimics a dummy transaction so that idle slots do not hold on to old WAL; HeartbeatSchema defaults to public
  - With CaptureDdls false, DMS does not need its DDL audit table and event trigger on the source
  - FailTasksOnLobTruncation makes a task fail instead of truncating a LOB larger than LobMaxSize
  - The source data type table maps TEXT, JSON and JSONB to NCLOB, XML to CLOB, BYTEA to BLOB, and UUID to STRING
  - For PostgreSQL to PostgreSQL migrations of an entire database, AWS recommends native tools such as pg_dump
  - AWS DMS does not support CDC for Amazon RDS Proxy for PostgreSQL as a source, and does not support materialized views
  - AWS DMS does not support change processing of ALTER COLUMN SET DEFAULT or SET/DROP NOT NULL

### Using a PostgreSQL database as a target for AWS Database Migration Service

- ID: `dbmig-dms-target-postgresql`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Target.PostgreSQL.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 39
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Table order during full load cannot be guaranteed, so active foreign keys can make the task fail; AWS recommends disabling them during the full load
  - AfterConnectScript=SET session_replication_role = replica makes AWS DMS bypass foreign keys and user triggers
  - AWS DMS doesn't migrate sequences during ongoing replication: update NEXTVAL for each sequence on the target after stopping replication from the source
  - The minimum grants for the target user: CONNECT and CREATE on the database, USAGE and CREATE on the schema, and UPDATE, INSERT, SELECT, DELETE, TRUNCATE on its tables

- 参照する章: 39

### AWS DMS Serverless components

- ID: `dbmig-dms-serverless-components`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Serverless.Components.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 39
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A DCU is 2 GB of RAM, and AWS DMS bills for each DCU the replication is currently using
  - AWS DMS Serverless supports PostgreSQL-compatible databases as sources and PostgreSQL as a target
  - After a serverless replication has been started it is resumed with the start type resume-processing; a replication that has not started in 48 hours is deprovisioned and cannot be resumed
  - MinCapacityUnits defaults to 1 DCU; MultiAZ is recommended for CDC
  - CDCLatencySource is the gap between the last event captured from the source and the current time, and can be 0 when there are no new events
  - CDCLatencyTarget is the gap between the first event waiting to commit on the target and the current time
  - Logs go to a log group named dms-serverless-replication-<replication config resource ID>, which DMS creates only when the replication runs
  - A configuration can be modified only in the CREATED, STOPPED, FAILED, or FAILED_PROVISION states

  - A replication configuration can be deleted only in the STOPPED or FAILED states

  - Data transfer into AWS DMS is free, and so is transfer between DMS and RDS in the same Availability Zone
  - DMS Schema Conversion is free to use; you pay for the S3 storage it uses

### PostgreSQL 18: 29.8. Restrictions (logical replication)

- ID: `dbmig-postgres-restrictions`
- URL: <https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/logical-replication-restrictions.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 39
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The database schema and DDL commands are not replicated
  - Sequence data is not replicated; for a switchover the sequences must be updated to the latest values
  - Large objects are not replicated, and only tables can be replicated, not views or materialized views

### What is Elastic Disaster Recovery?

- ID: `drs-what-is`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/drs/latest/userguide/what-is-drs.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 40
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Source servers are replicated to a staging area subnet in your account, in the Region you select
  - Drill and recovery instances are launched from the most up-to-date state or a previous point in time
  - After recovery you can keep applications on AWS or replicate back to the primary site and fail back

### Elastic Disaster Recovery initialization and permissions

- ID: `drs-initialization`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/drs/latest/userguide/getting-started-initializing.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 40
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The service must be initialized in each Region before use; the console does it when the default replication settings are saved
  - Initialization creates AWSServiceRoleForElasticDisasterRecovery and the Replication Server, Conversion Server, Recovery Instance, Agent, Failback, and RecoveryInstanceWithLaunchActions roles
  - Initialization through the API is `aws drs initialize-service`, after which the replication settings template still has to be created

- ID: `drs-regions`

  - ap-northeast-1 (Tokyo) and ap-northeast-3 (Osaka) are supported

### Elastic Disaster Recovery network requirements

- ID: `drs-network-requirements`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/drs/latest/userguide/Network-Requirements.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 40
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Source servers talk to drs.<region>.amazonaws.com on TCP 443, continuously
  - Source servers send replicated data to the replication servers on TCP 1500
  - The staging area subnet needs the DRS endpoint on TCP 443, S3, and outbound access to the EC2 endpoint of its Region
  - The S3 buckets to allow include aws-elastic-disaster-recovery-<REGION> and the Amazon Linux 2023 repository bucket, because replication servers run Amazon Linux 2023
  - Replication uses TLS 1.2 from the agent to the replication server

### Elastic Disaster Recovery network setting preparations

- ID: `drs-network-preparations`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/drs/latest/userguide/Network-Settings-Preparations.html>

- 参照する章: 40
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The staging area subnet is named in the replication template; a dedicated subnet is the stated best practice
  - Drill and recovery instances launch in the subnet named in each source server's EC2 launch template, which is created when the server is added

### Elastic Disaster Recovery network diagrams

### Point in time (PIT) policy

- ID: `drs-point-in-time`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/drs/latest/userguide/point-in-time.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 40
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Snapshots can be kept for 1 to 365 days
  - The policy has exactly three rules; MINUTE (every 10, kept 60) and HOUR (every 1, kept 24) are fixed, and only the DAY rule's retention is configurable

### Replication related FAQ

- ID: `drs-replication-faq`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/drs/latest/userguide/Replication-Related-FAQ.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 40
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The default snapshot retention is 7 days
  - A t3.small replication server is provisioned by default; the typical ratio of volumes to replication servers is 15:1
  - Replication is crash consistent
  - Replication servers are recycled approximately every 14 days
  - Snapshots no longer used, or past the retention, are deleted automatically

### Elastic Disaster Recovery concepts FAQ

- ID: `drs-concepts-faq`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/drs/latest/userguide/CloudEndure-Concepts.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 40
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The guide states an RPO typically in the sub-second range and an RTO typically ranging between 5 and 20 minutes
  - RPO is measured to the latest crash-consistent point copied to the staging area; data still in memory on the source is not there
  - The RTO depends on the operating system's boot time
  - "Use most recent data" needs a connection to the source server and may time out when it is offline

### Preparing for recovery

- ID: `drs-preparing`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/drs/latest/userguide/preparing-failover.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 40
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A recovery drill is a non-disruptive test that performs the same steps as a recovery, with the same launch settings and snapshots
  - Drills are recommended at least quarterly
  - A drill can be performed once the initial sync has completed, even in lag or stall status
  - `aws drs start-recovery --source-servers ... --is-drill` starts a drill; `aws drs terminate-recovery-instances` cleans up
  - Drill instances are billed until deleted, and are cleaned up when the same server is drilled again

- ID: `drs-failback-overview`

- 参照する章: 40
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Recovery launches instances; failover, the redirection of traffic, is performed by you outside the service
  - For an EC2 source in the same account, failback is reversed replication started on the recovery instance

### Performing a failover with Elastic Disaster Recovery

- ID: `drs-failover`

### Linux containers on Fargate container image pull behavior for Amazon ECS

- ID: `fg-pull-behavior`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/fargate-pull-behavior.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 41
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Every Fargate task runs on its own single use, single tenant instance
  - Images and layers are not cached: the whole image is pulled for every task, and the pull time is directly correlated to the time taken to start a task
  - The size of the image, the compression algorithm, and the number of vCPUs affect the time; zstd decompresses faster
  - For images larger than 250 MB lazy loading may be better than downloading all of the image

### Task retirement and maintenance for AWS Fargate on Amazon ECS

- ID: `fg-task-maintenance`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/task-maintenance.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 41
- この出典が支える主張:
  - When a platform version revision is retired, all tasks running on it are stopped; running tasks are never migrated
  - Notices go to the AWS Health Dashboard and by email; the default wait before retirement is 7 days
  - Service tasks are replaced by the scheduler: with the defaults (minimum healthy percent 100, maximum percent 200) a new task is started and running before an old one is retired
  - A standalone task is stopped on or after the retirement date and is not replaced
  - If a replacement cannot be launched, the retired task is stopped without one
  - A fault in the underlying host is handled by replacing the host without a retirement notice
  - Task retirement cannot be opted out of
- 注記: The page credits maximumPercent in one passage and minimum healthy percent in another for start-before-stop.

### Amazon ECS task definition differences for Fargate

- ID: `fg-task-sizes`

  - The 8, 16, and 32 vCPU sizes need Linux platform version 1.4.0 or later
  - Tasks on Linux platform version 1.4.0 can use Seekable OCI (SOCI) indexes to start without waiting for the whole image; new users are limited to index manifest v2
  - SOCI works for X86_64 and ARM64, for images in Amazon ECR private registries, compressed with gzip or not at all (not zstd), and is recommended for images larger than 250 MiB compressed

### Amazon ECS clusters for Fargate

- ID: `fg-capacity-providers`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/fargate-capacity-providers.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 41
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A capacity provider must be associated with a cluster before a strategy can name it; a strategy has at most 20 providers
  - Only one provider in a strategy can have a base; at least one needs a weight above zero
  - A service can be changed from a launch type to a capacity provider strategy, with a forced new deployment
  - A Fargate Spot task gets a two-minute warning before it is stopped, as a task state change event and as SIGTERM to the task
  - When Spot capacity is unavailable, services retry until it is; Fargate does not replace Spot capacity with on-demand capacity
  - The stop code of an interrupted task is SpotInterruption; stopTimeout can be at most 120 seconds

### Amazon ECS API Reference: CapacityProviderStrategyItem

- ID: `fg-api-capacity-provider-strategy`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/APIReference/API_CapacityProviderStrategyItem.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 41
- この出典が支える主張:
  - base is how many tasks, at a minimum, run on the provider; it is satisfied before weights; range 0 to 100,000
  - weight is the relative share of tasks beyond the base; range 0 to 1,000; weights 1 and 4 mean one task on A for every four on B
  - FARGATE_SPOT supports Linux X86_64 on platform version 1.3.0 or later and ARM64 on 1.4.0 or later

### Use a target metric to scale Amazon ECS services

- ID: `fg-target-tracking`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/service-autoscaling-targettracking.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 41
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The service scales out proportionally to the metric as fast as it can, and scales in more gradually
  - With several target tracking policies it scales out if any is ready and in only if all are
  - A policy does not scale on insufficient data
  - ALBRequestCountPerTarget is not supported for the blue/green deployment type
  - Scale-in is turned off while a deployment is in progress

### Automatically scale your Amazon ECS service

- ID: `fg-service-auto-scaling`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/service-auto-scaling.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 41
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Target tracking, step scaling, scheduled scaling, and predictive scaling are supported
  - Scale-in is blocked until the scale-in cooldown has expired; a scale-out during it happens immediately
  - Scaling starts from the running task count, not the desired count
  - With a minimum capacity of 0 and target tracking, Service Auto Scaling waits for one data point of demand and then scales out by the minimum possible amount
  - Step scaling lets you react more quickly because you define the thresholds and adjustments yourself

### How target tracking scaling for Application Auto Scaling works

- ID: `fg-aas-target-tracking`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/application/userguide/target-tracking-scaling-policy-overview.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 41
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The default cooldown for ECS services is 300 seconds
  - Scale-in happens only when utilization is far enough below the target, usually more than 10% lower
  - A metric that emits real zeros, such as ALBRequestCountPerTarget, lets a target with minimum capacity 0 scale in to 0
  - A scheduled action can start a scaling activity during a cooldown

### Application Auto Scaling API Reference: PredefinedMetricSpecification

- ID: `fg-aas-api-predefined-metric`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/application/APIReference/API_PredefinedMetricSpecification.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 41
- この出典が支える主張:
  - ECSServiceAverageCPUUtilization, ECSServiceAverageMemoryUtilization, and ALBRequestCountPerTarget are predefined metric types; high-resolution variants of the first two use 20-second metrics
  - ResourceLabel is app/<load-balancer-name>/<load-balancer-id>/targetgroup/<target-group-name>/<target-group-id>
- 注記: DisableScaleIn and the cooldown fields are on API_TargetTrackingScalingPolicyConfiguration.html.

- ID: `fg-scaling-best-practice`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/capacity-autoscaling-best-practice.html>

### Protect your Amazon ECS tasks from being terminated by scale-in events

- ID: `fg-task-scale-in-protection`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/task-scale-in-protection.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 41
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Task scale-in protection keeps a service's task from being terminated by scale-in from service auto scaling or deployments: 2 hours by default, 48 hours at most
  - A container sets it at $ECS_AGENT_URI/task-protection/v1/state; the task role needs ecs:GetTaskProtection and ecs:UpdateTaskProtection
  - It is supported only for tasks deployed from a service

### Monitor Amazon ECS containers with ECS Exec

- ID: `fg-ecs-exec`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/ecs-exec.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 41
- この出典が支える主張:
  - ECS Exec uses Systems Manager Session Manager; the agent's binaries are bind-mounted into the container
  - Commands run as root, even when the container specifies a user
  - A read-only root file system (readonlyRootFilesystem) is not supported, because the agent has to write to the container's file system
  - ECS Exec cannot be turned on for existing tasks, only for new ones
  - A session's idle timeout is 20 minutes and cannot be changed
  - CloudTrail records an ExecuteCommand event; commands and output can be logged to CloudWatch Logs or S3
  - Access can be limited with condition keys such as ecs:container-name and ecs:ResourceTag, and enabling it can be denied with ecs:enable-execute-command
  - Tasks without internet access need the ssmmessages interface endpoint
  - initProcessEnabled is recommended to clean up zombie processes

### Creating an AWS Firewall Manager policy

- ID: `fwm-create-policy`

  - With automatic remediation, a policy can also remove existing web ACL associations that are not managed by another active Firewall Manager policy, associating its own web ACL first
  - A content audit security group policy must be created without automatic remediation
  - Resource tags can include or exclude, not both in one policy
  - The creation of a policy can take several minutes

### Using the AWS Firewall Manager policy scope

- ID: `fwm-policy-scope`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/policy-scope.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 42
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Scope by accounts: all, an include list of accounts and OUs, or an exclude list
  - Scope by resource tags: all of the tags or any of the tags, included or excluded; a tag matches on the same key and the same value
  - A resource that leaves the scope stays associated and protected unless the policy removes protections from resources that leave the scope
  - The AWS Config managed rules and web ACLs with no resources are deleted regardless of that option

- ID: `fwm-policy-deleting`

### Using AWS WAF policies with Firewall Manager

- ID: `fwm-waf-policies`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-policies.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 42
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A policy either creates new web ACLs for all in-scope resources, replacing ones in use, or retrofits the web ACLs already associated
  - In a managed web ACL an account can manage its own rules and rule groups in addition to the policy's

### Rule group management for AWS WAF policies

- ID: `fwm-waf-rule-groups`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-policies-rule-groups.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 42
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A managed web ACL has three sets: the policy's first rule groups, the account's rules and rule groups, and the policy's last rule groups
  - The first and last sets take rule groups only, not individual rules
  - The rule groups are named PREFMManaged- and POSTFMManaged- followed by the policy name and a timestamp

### Web ACL management for AWS WAF policies

- ID: `fwm-waf-web-acls`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/how-fms-manages-web-acls.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 42
- この出典が支える主張:
  - With optimizeUnassociatedWebACL, a web ACL is created in an account only if a resource will use it; without it, every in-scope account gets one
  - A web ACL the policy creates is named FMManagedWebACLV2-<policy name>-<timestamp>
  - Retrofitting (webACLSource RETROFIT_EXISTING) requires the web ACL to be owned by the account and associated only with in-scope resources
  - A customer-owned web ACL that a customer associates manually is still overridden by the policy's web ACL

### Using security group policies in Firewall Manager to manage Amazon VPC security groups

- ID: `fwm-sg-policies`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/security-group-policies.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 42
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Best practices: exclude the administrator account, start with automatic remediation disabled, and keep Firewall Manager and other tools from managing the same security groups
  - Changes to security groups on EC2 network interfaces are usually detected within several hours, and can take as much as six
  - Network interfaces created by Amazon RDS are not supported, and those of Fargate tasks and requester-managed interfaces cannot be updated

### Using content audit security group policies with Firewall Manager

- ID: `fwm-sg-audit`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/security-group-policies-audit.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 42
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A content audit policy applies to customer-created security groups in scope, for the resource types EC2 instance, network interface, and security group
  - The audit security group is created in the administrator account and is only a comparison reference
  - With custom policy rules, allow means every in-scope rule must be within the allowed range of the audit group's rules; deny means none may be
  - With automatic remediation, Firewall Manager updates or removes non-compliant rules
  - Peer security groups cannot be referenced in a content audit policy

### Configuring job properties for Spark jobs in AWS Glue

- ID: `glue-add-job`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/add-job.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13

- この出典が支える主張:
  - Job types and their commands: Spark (glueetl), Spark Streaming (gluestreaming), Python shell (pythonshell)
  - AWS Glue versions: 6.0 is Spark 4.1.1 and Python 3.13, 5.1 is Spark 3.5.6 and Python 3.11; a job created without a version gets 5.1
  - A DPU is 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of memory; G.1X is 1 DPU per worker, G.2X is 2 DPU; G.025X is for streaming jobs only
  - The job timeout defaults to 480 minutes for AWS Glue 5.0 and later (2,880 for 4.0 and earlier); the maximum is 10,080 minutes; jobs are billed for execution time
  - Number of retries is 0 to 10; a job that reaches its timeout is not restarted
  - Maximum concurrency defaults to 1 and an error is returned when it is reached
  - The flexible execution class is for non-urgent jobs, and is supported with G.1X and G.2X on AWS Glue 3.0 or later
  - Jobs that access Lake Formation tables with cell-level filters cannot use job bookmarks or push-down predicates

### Tracking processed data using job bookmarks

- ID: `glue-job-bookmarks`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/monitor-continuations.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 43
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A job bookmark is state persisted from a job run so that later runs process only new data; the default option is Disable, with which the job always processes the entire dataset
  - For Amazon S3 sources the bookmark checks the last modified time of objects; a timestamp is used to filter the new files
  - The state elements are saved atomically when job.commit is invoked from the user script
  - Only source files are tracked: when a bookmark is rewound or reset, AWS Glue does not clean the target files, and the page suggests different output targets to avoid duplicate data
  - Bookmarks are kept per job and are deleted with the job
  - Changing a source's path without changing its transformation_ctx makes the job use the old bookmark state and skip files

### What is AWS Health?

- ID: `health-what-is`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/health/latest/ug/what-is-aws-health.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 44
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The AWS Health Dashboard is available to all AWS customers at no additional cost and requires no setup
  - All AWS customers can receive AWS Health events through Amazon EventBridge at no additional cost
  - The AWS Health API needs an AWS Business Support+, AWS Enterprise Support, or AWS Unified Operations plan; in a Region that does not offer these plans, or for an account that has not transitioned, a Business, Enterprise On-Ramp, or Enterprise Support plan

### Concepts for AWS Health

- ID: `health-concepts`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/health/latest/ug/aws-health-concepts-and-terms.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 44
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Health events are notifications that AWS Health sends on behalf of other AWS services; there are account-specific events and public events
  - A public event is reported even if the account does not use that service or has no resources in that Region
  - Public events are not available through AWS managed notifications in AWS User Notifications; an EventBridge rule or a user-configured notification is needed
  - Event type categories: account notification, issue, scheduled change; all scheduled change events are account-specific
  - Example event type codes, including AWS_EC2_OPERATIONAL_ISSUE, AWS_EBS_VOLUME_ATTACHMENT_ISSUE, AWS_ABUSE_PII_CONTENT_REMOVAL_REPORT (listed under issue), AWS_EC2_INSTANCE_RETIREMENT_SCHEDULED, AWS_RDS_PLANNED_LIFECYCLE_EVENT, AWS_S3_OPEN_ACCESS_BUCKET_NOTIFICATION, AWS_BILLING_SUSPENSION_NOTICE
  - Event status is open, closed, or upcoming; events can be viewed in the dashboard or the API for up to 90 days
  - Actionability is ACTION_REQUIRED, ACTION_MAY_BE_REQUIRED, or INFORMATIONAL; events about service issues carry no actionability label
  - Personas are OPERATIONS, SECURITY, and BILLING
  - Calling the AWS Health API without one of the required Support plans returns SubscriptionRequiredException
  - The public Service health page is https://health.aws.amazon.com/health/status and needs no account; the signed-in dashboard is https://health.aws.amazon.com/health/home

### Viewing your account events in the AWS Health Dashboard

- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/health/latest/ug/aws-health-account-views.html>

### Monitoring events in AWS Health with Amazon EventBridge

- ID: `health-eventbridge`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/health/latest/ug/cloudwatch-events-health.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 44
- この出典が支える主張:
  - AWS Health delivers events on a durable basis and attempts to deliver each to EventBridge at least once
  - A rule receives events for its own account only; organizational view is needed for other accounts
  - Public events might take up to one hour to start arriving after a rule is created

### Creating EventBridge rules for AWS Region coverage

- ID: `health-eventbridge-regions`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/health/latest/ug/choosing-a-region.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 44
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A rule is created in each Region whose events are wanted
  - In the standard partition US West (Oregon) is the backup Region of every other Region and US East (N. Virginia) is the backup of US West (Oregon); events are sent to both the primary and the backup Region
  - A rule in a backup Region that should not receive copies filters on detail.backupEvent
  - Simplified integration: one rule in US West (Oregon) receives account-specific events of all standard-partition Regions, without public events and without high availability
  - Global events, such as those of IAM, require a rule in US East (N. Virginia)
  - For a highly available setup, rules in both Regions and de-duplication by detail.communicationId

### Monitoring account-specific and public events for AWS Health

- ID: `health-eventbridge-public`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/health/latest/ug/about-public-events.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 44
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A rule with "source": ["aws.health"] delivers both account-specific and public events; a wildcard such as "aws.health*" matches nothing
  - eventScopeCode is PUBLIC or ACCOUNT_SPECIFIC and can be filtered on
  - Public events reach the backup Region only when a valid rule exists in the impacted Region; account-specific events reach both regardless of rules
  - AWS recommends de-duplicating by eventARN and communicationId

### Viewing paginated lists of AWS Health events on EventBridge

- ID: `health-eventbridge-pagination`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/health/latest/ug/pagnation-of-health-events.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 44
- この出典が支える主張:
  - An event whose resources or affectedEntities exceed EventBridge's 256 KB limit is split into pages published as separate messages with the same eventARN
  - For human-readable notifications a filter on detail.page keeps only the first page
  - The communicationId carries the page number after a hyphen even when there is one page

### Reference: AWS Health events Amazon EventBridge schema

- ID: `health-eventbridge-schema`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/health/latest/ug/aws-health-events-eventbridge-schema.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 44
- この出典が支える主張:
  - detail-type is AWS Health Event or AWS Health Abuse Event; source is aws.health
  - region is the Region the notification was delivered to; the impacted Region is detail.eventRegion
  - The fields of detail, their required flags, and the time format 'DoW, DD MMM YYYY HH:MM:SS TZ'
  - eventTypeCategory is issue, accountNotification, investigation, or scheduledChange; statusCode is open, closed, or upcoming
  - An event ARN is not unique to an account or Region; communicationId with the account ID helps de-duplicate
  - For public events latestDescription holds only the latest update, not the history
  - page, totalPages and backupEvent are strings in the sample payloads
  - The five sample payloads copied into examples/44-health/fixtures/documented.json
  - Events that include MAINTENANCE_SCHEDULED are generally pushed about two weeks before the start time
- 注記: The field table marks lastUpdatedTime as required, but two of the five samples leave it out; one sample leaves out resources. The table spells the persona OPERATIONAL while the samples and the concepts page say OPERATIONS. The samples' weekdays do not fit their dates. No sample and no field list is given for AWS Health Abuse Event.

### Planned lifecycle events for AWS Health

- ID: `health-planned-lifecycle`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/health/latest/ug/aws-health-planned-lifecycle-events.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 44
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Planned lifecycle events are scheduled changes with the type code AWS_{SERVICE}_PLANNED_LIFECYCLE_EVENT
  - The start time is the soonest date resources are affected and is to be treated as the change date; an end time is not always given
  - Lead time is designed to be at least 180 days for major changes and 90 days for minor ones, where possible
  - Affected resources are PENDING until acted on, then RESOLVED; these updates can lag by up to 72 hours
  - An event with unresolved resources stays open for four years after its start or end date

  - The embedded experience in the CloudFormation console is replaced by a visual editor integrated in that console
  - The Export to Infrastructure Composer entries in the Lambda and Step Functions consoles are removed
  - Infrastructure Composer exposes no customer-facing API, SDK or CLI
  - Templates saved locally or in Amazon S3, and existing stacks, are not affected
  - How to open a template in VS Code: the button in the editor, the context menu, or the Command Palette

### Edit templates visually with template studio - AWS CloudFormation User Guide

- ID: `cfn-template-studio`

  - Template studio shows the template as text beside a diagram of its resources; the text is authoritative and the diagram cannot be edited
  - The diagram draws a connection wherever one resource refers to another through Ref, Fn::GetAtt, Fn::Sub, or DependsOn; a resource nothing references appears on its own
  - A role assumed by three functions is shown inside each function although the template declares one
  - It opens from the navigation pane, from Create stack, from an existing stack's update, and wherever the console shows a template

  - Validate uses ValidateTemplate with TemplateBody, limited to 51,200 bytes
  - The diagram downloads as a PNG
  - Permissions: cloudformation:GetTemplate, s3:GetObject, cloudformation:ValidateTemplate, s3:PutObject, s3:CreateBucket, s3:ListBucket

### How AWS Shield and Shield Advanced work

- ID: `shield-how-it-works`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-overview.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 46
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Shield Standard is provided automatically and at no extra charge when you use AWS; Shield Advanced is a subscription for higher levels of protection
  - Classes of attack: network volumetric (layer 3), network protocol (layer 4, such as a TCP SYN flood), and application layer (layer 7, such as web request floods)

### AWS Shield Standard overview

- ID: `shield-standard-overview`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-standard-summary.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 46
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Shield Standard defends against the most common, frequently occurring network and transport layer DDoS attacks, for all AWS customers, at no additional charge
  - Route 53 hosted zones, CloudFront distributions and Global Accelerator standard accelerators receive comprehensive availability protection against all known network and transport layer attacks
  - If the first point of entry is in an AWS Region the application perimeter is the VPC; with CloudFront or Global Accelerator it begins at the edge of the AWS network

### AWS Shield Advanced overview

- ID: `shield-advanced-overview`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-advanced-summary.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 46
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The subscription covers standard AWS WAF fees (web ACL, rule, and base request fee up to 1,500 WCUs and the default body size) for resources protected with Shield Advanced, up to 50 billion requests a calendar month
  - It does not cover AWS WAF for resources that are not protected with Shield Advanced, nor Bot Control, CAPTCHA and other non-standard costs
  - The subscription includes access to the Layer 7 Anti-DDoS managed rule group
  - For accounts in one AWS Organizations consolidated billing family, one subscription price covers all subscribed accounts

### List of AWS resources that AWS Shield Advanced protects

- ID: `shield-advanced-protected-resources`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-advanced-summary-protected-resources.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 46
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Protection applies only to resources explicitly specified in Shield Advanced or through a Firewall Manager Shield Advanced policy; nothing is protected automatically
  - Resource types: CloudFront distributions, Route 53 hosted zones, Global Accelerator standard accelerators, EC2 Elastic IP addresses (and instances and Network Load Balancers through them), Application Load Balancers, Classic Load Balancers

### AWS Shield Advanced capabilities and options

- ID: `shield-advanced-capabilities`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-advanced-summary-capabilities.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 46
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Capabilities: AWS WAF integration, automatic application layer DDoS mitigation, health-based detection, protection groups, enhanced visibility, Firewall Manager policies at no additional charge, the Shield Response Team (SRT), proactive engagement, cost protection
  - To use the services of the SRT you must also be subscribed to the Business Support plan or the Enterprise Support plan
  - Health-based detection is available for any resource type except Route 53 hosted zones; proactive engagement only for resources with health-based detection
  - Cost protection is provided in the form of Shield Advanced service credits

### Deciding whether to subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced and apply additional protections

- ID: `shield-advanced-deciding`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-advanced-summary-deciding.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 46
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Consider Shield Advanced where you need guaranteed availability, rapid access to DDoS mitigation experts, awareness and notification by AWS, or predictability in cloud costs during an attack
  - You pay one monthly subscription fee for all accounts under a consolidated billing account, plus usage fees based on GB of data transferred out

### Managed DDoS event response with Shield Response Team (SRT) support

- ID: `shield-srt-support`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-srt-support.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 46
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The SRT can analyze AWS WAF logs and, with approval, change the web ACL; build custom network mitigations; engage AWS networking teams; and recommend architecture changes
  - To use the SRT you must be subscribed to the Business Support plan or the Enterprise Support plan

### Requesting a credit in AWS Shield Advanced after an attack

- ID: `shield-cost-protection-credit`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-request-service-credit.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 46
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Credits cover only: Shield Advanced data transfer out, CloudFront HTTP/HTTPS requests, CloudFront data transfer out, Route 53 queries, Global Accelerator data transfer, Application Load Balancer capacity units, and EC2 instances launched by auto scaling in response to the attack
  - Prerequisites: the resource had Shield Advanced protection before the attack began; for CloudFront and Application Load Balancers a web ACL with a rate-based rule in Block mode was associated; the DDoS resiliency best practices were implemented
  - The request is a billing case with 'DDoS Concession' in the subject, submitted within 15 days after the billing month of the attack; credits apply only to Shield Advanced usage and are valid for 12 months

### Health-based detection using health checks with Shield Advanced and Route 53

- ID: `shield-health-based-detection`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-advanced-health-checks.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 46
- この出典が支える主張:
  - You define a Route 53 health check, verify it reports healthy, and associate it with the protection; Shield Advanced does not manage health checks
  - With an unhealthy health check Shield Advanced requires smaller deviations to alert and reports events more quickly; with a healthy one it requires larger deviations
  - Health checks are required for proactive engagement

### Automating application layer DDoS mitigation with Shield Advanced

- ID: `shield-automatic-app-layer`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-automatic-app-layer-response.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 46
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Starting March 26, 2026, the Anti-DDoS Managed Rule Group for AWS WAF is the default solution against HTTP request floods and supersedes Layer 7 Auto Mitigation; a new Shield Advanced customer who needs the legacy solution contacts AWS Support
  - The Anti-DDoS Managed Rule Group detects and mitigates attacks within seconds rather than minutes
  - The legacy automatic mitigation needs between 24 hours and 30 days to establish a traffic baseline after a web ACL is associated

### Grouping your AWS Shield Advanced protections

- ID: `shield-protection-groups`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-protection-groups.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 46
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A protection group treats several protected resources as one unit for detection and mitigation; membership can be all protected resources, a resource type, or named resources
  - Automatic application layer mitigation does not interact with protection groups

### AWS Shield Advanced metrics

- ID: `shield-metrics`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/shield-metrics.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 46
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Shield Advanced publishes detection, mitigation and top contributor metrics in the AWS/DDoSProtection namespace for the resources it protects
  - DDoSDetected has a non-zero value during an event and is posted with no dimension other than the resource; DDoSAttackRequestsPerSecond is reported only for the most significant layer 7 events
  - Metrics for CloudFront, Route 53 and protection groups are reported in us-east-1
  - Metrics are reported once a minute during an event and once a day otherwise
  - AWS recommends an alarm for each protected resource when DDoSDetected is non-zero, and says a non-zero value does not necessarily imply an attack

### Responding to DDoS events in AWS

- ID: `shield-responding`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-responding.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 46
- この出典が支える主張:
  - AWS automatically mitigates network and transport layer attacks
  - For application layer attacks AWS attempts to detect and notify Shield Advanced customers through CloudWatch alarms and by default does not automatically apply mitigations, to avoid blocking valid traffic
  - A Shield Advanced customer can contact the AWS Support Center; critical and urgent cases are routed directly to DDoS experts

### Subscribing to AWS Shield Advanced

- ID: `shield-subscribing`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/enable-ddos-prem.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 46
- この出典が支える主張:
  - You subscribe each account in the AWS WAF & Shield console; you do not subscribe to Shield Standard
  - Once subscribed, to unsubscribe you must contact AWS Support; auto-renewal is disabled with the UpdateSubscription API
  - Subscribing does not protect any resource: you must specify the resources

### AWS Shield detection logic for infrastructure layer threats (layer 3 and layer 4)

- ID: `shield-detection-infrastructure`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-event-detection-infrastructure.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 46
- この出典が支える主張:
  - For CloudFront and Route 53 all packets are inspected by a fully inline DDoS mitigation system and attacks are mitigated in real time, regardless of whether you use Shield Advanced
  - For regional resources such as load balancers and Elastic IP addresses, traffic is evaluated every minute and a mitigation is placed when the resource's capacity is exceeded; mitigations reduce DDoS traffic but might not eliminate it
  - Shield Advanced adds lower detection thresholds (half the calculated capacity), intermittent attack protection, and health-based detection

### AWS Shield mitigation logic for CloudFront and Route 53

- ID: `shield-mitigation-cloudfront-route53`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-event-mitigation-logic-continuous-inspection.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 46
- この出典が支える主張:
  - CloudFront only lets traffic that is valid for web applications through; TCP SYN floods are mitigated by a SYN proxy and TLS is terminated at the edge, so the origin only receives well-formed web requests
  - Shield Advanced does not support CloudFront tenants

### Setting up proactive engagement for the SRT to contact you directly

- ID: `shield-proactive-engagement`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-srt-proactive-engagement.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 46
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Proactive engagement needs the Business or Enterprise Support plan, a Route 53 health check on the protected resource, and at least one contact (up to ten)
  - Proactive engagement is not available for events detected by the Anti-DDoS managed rule group

### AWS Shield Pricing

- ID: `shield-pricing-page`
- URL: <https://aws.amazon.com/shield/pricing/>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 46
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Shield Advanced requires a 1-year subscription commitment and charges a monthly fee plus a usage fee on data transfer out
  - Subscriptions auto-renew annually; the renewal can be cancelled through the Support Center between 30 and 5 days before the renewal date
  - All Shield Advanced benefits, including DDoS cost protection, are subject to fulfillment of the 1-year commitment
  - If CloudFront is in front of a load balancer that receives all its traffic from CloudFront, only CloudFront needs protection
  - To contact the Shield Response Team customers need the Enterprise or Business Support levels
- 注記: The monthly fee is filled in by script on the page; the amount was read from the Price List (shield-price-list).

### Rate-based rule high-level settings in AWS WAF

- ID: `shield-waf-rate-based-settings`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-statement-type-rate-based-high-level-settings.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 46
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The evaluation window is 60, 120, 300 or 600 seconds, 300 by default; it sets how far back AWS WAF looks, not how often it checks
  - The lowest rate limit is 10
  - A rate-based rule that counts all requests together needs a scope-down statement

### Rate-based rule caveats in AWS WAF

- ID: `shield-waf-rate-based-caveats`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-statement-type-rate-based-caveats.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 46
- この出典が支える主張:
  - AWS WAF rate limiting is not intended for precise request-rate limiting and does not guarantee an exact limit match
  - Requests can come in at too high a rate for up to several minutes before AWS WAF detects and rate limits them; usually this delay is below 30 seconds
  - Changing a rate limit setting resets the rule's counts and can pause rate limiting for up to a minute

### Choosing workflow type in Step Functions

- ID: `sfn-types-guarantees`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/choosing-workflow-type.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 47
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The workflow type cannot be changed after a state machine is created
  - Standard: up to one year, exactly-once workflow execution unless Retry is specified in ASL, execution state persisted between state transitions, history retrievable through the API for 90 days after completion, billed by state transition
  - Express: up to five minutes, billed by number of executions, duration and memory; asynchronous Express is at-least-once, synchronous Express is at-most-once; execution state is not persisted between transitions and history is not captured by Step Functions
  - Express Workflows do not support the .sync and .waitForTaskToken integration patterns, Distributed Map, or activities
  - For Standard, starting an execution with the name of a running one returns an idempotent response; for Express, the same name results in concurrent executions
  - StartSyncExecution from the console expires after 60 seconds

### Transforming data with JSONata in Step Functions

- ID: `sfn-jsonata`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/transforming-data.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 47
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Step Functions implements JSONata based on the 2.0.6 specification; $eval is not available, $parse replaces it
  - When creating a workflow in the console, AWS recommends JSONata as the top-level QueryLanguage; without the field the default is JSONPath
  - JSONata states use Arguments and Output in place of InputPath, Parameters, ResultSelector, ResultPath and OutputPath, and a string is an expression only when it starts with {% and ends with %}
  - $states holds input, result, errorOutput (in a Catch) and context
  - An expression that returns no value, a type error, an evaluation longer than one second, and exceeded memory all raise States.QueryEvaluationError, which Retry and Catch can name
  - Step Functions adds $partition, $range, $hash, $random, $uuid and $parse
  - A Choice rule in JSONata has a Condition

### Passing data between states with variables

- ID: `sfn-variables`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/workflow-variables.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 47
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Assign is available on Pass, Task, Map, Parallel, Choice and Wait states, and inside Catch and Choice rules
  - All expressions in an Assign are evaluated with the values on state entry, then assigned; the new values are visible from the next state
  - Assign and Output are processed in parallel
  - A variable is at most 256 KiB, all variables in one Assign at most 256 KiB together, and all stored variables at most 10 MiB per execution
  - Parallel branches and Map iterations read outer variables and keep their own; a Distributed Map cannot reference outer variables

### Amazon States Language (specification)

- ID: `asl-spec`
- URL: <https://states-language.net/spec.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 47
- この出典が支える主張:
  - In JSONata states a Catcher may have Output and Assign, which may reference $states.errorOutput; without Output the state output is the Error Output, an object with Error and usually Cause
  - When a state reports an error, the matching Catcher's Assign is evaluated and the state's top-level Assign is not
  - ItemSelector overrides each item of a Map; $states.context.Map.Item.Value and .Index describe the item
  - A MaxConcurrency of 1 processes the items in order
- 注記: The specification states the default of a missing Output twice and differently: "the result in a Task, Map, and Parallel State" in the section on Arguments and Output, and "the Task State copies its input through to its output" in the section on the Task state. The chapter's definitions write Output in every Task and Map so that neither reading matters.

### Discover service integration patterns in Step Functions

- ID: `sfn-patterns`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/connect-to-resource.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 47
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Three patterns: Request Response, Run a Job (.sync), Wait for a Callback with Task Token (.waitForTaskToken), chosen by the suffix of Resource
  - AWS SDK integrations: Request Response in Standard and Express, .waitForTaskToken in Standard, no .sync
  - Optimized DynamoDB supports Request Response only; SQS, SNS and Lambda support Request Response and, in Standard, the callback; Step Functions, ECS, and others support .sync
  - A task waiting for a token waits until the execution reaches one year unless HeartbeatSeconds or TimeoutSeconds is set
  - If a task using a callback token times out, a new random token is generated
  - Task tokens must be returned by principals in the same account
  - A .sync task that is aborted is cancelled on a best-effort basis; .sync polling consumes API quota

### Handling errors in Step Functions workflows

- ID: `sfn-retry-catch`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/concepts-error-handling.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 47
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Retrier fields and defaults: IntervalSeconds 1, MaxAttempts 3 (0 never retries), BackoffRate 2.0, MaxDelaySeconds, JitterStrategy FULL or NONE (default NONE; FULL randomizes each interval between 0 and its computed value)
  - A retrier's counters apply across all visits to it within one state execution (the page's complex retry scenario: ErrorA, ErrorB, ErrorC, ErrorB)
  - States.ALL matches every known error name except States.Runtime and States.DataLimitExceeded, must be alone and last; States.TaskFailed matches every error except States.Timeout
  - Retries are treated as state transitions
  - Catchers exist for Task, Parallel and Map states, not for the execution as a whole
  - The page lists States.HeartbeatTimeout as the error of a missed heartbeat

### Task workflow state

- ID: `sfn-task-fields`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/state-task.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 47
- この出典が支える主張:
  - TimeoutSeconds and HeartbeatSeconds both default to 99,999,999; HeartbeatSeconds must be smaller than TimeoutSeconds
  - The page says a missed heartbeat fails the task with States.Timeout
  - The optimized Lambda integration is arn:aws:states:::lambda:invoke; a function ARN as Resource is the legacy form
  - Arguments and Output are the JSONata fields of a Task
- 注記: Two pages name the error of a missed heartbeat differently (States.Timeout here and on the integration patterns page, States.HeartbeatTimeout on the error handling page). The chapter's Retry names both.

### Send messages to an Amazon SQS queue with Step Functions

- ID: `sfn-connect-sqs`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/connect-sqs.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 47
- この出典が支える主張:

### Retry behavior - AWS SDKs and Tools Reference Guide

- ID: `sdk48-retry-behavior`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdkref/latest/guide/feature-retry-behavior.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 48
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The behaviour the page describes requires opting in with AWS_NEW_RETRIES_2026=true until it becomes the default; without it the SDK uses pre-2026 retry behaviour
  - Retry modes standard and adaptive; legacy is not available in JavaScript; adaptive is not recommended as a general default
  - AWS_RETRY_MODE / retry_mode and AWS_MAX_ATTEMPTS / max_attempts, and the precedence code, environment, shared config file, default
  - Under the 2026 behaviour: base delay 50 ms for transient errors and 1,000 ms for throttling, cap 20 seconds, full jitter
  - Under the 2026 behaviour: retry quota of 500 tokens, 14 per transient retry, 5 per throttling retry, 1 restored by a success without retry
  - Under the 2026 behaviour: DynamoDB and DynamoDB Streams clients default to 4 max attempts with a 25 ms transient base delay
  - x-amz-retry-after is a delay in milliseconds, clamped between the computed backoff and that plus 5,000 ms
  - The token budget is typically scoped to a single client instance
- 注記: The page describes the opt-in behaviour only. The pre-2026 numbers in the chapter (100 ms, 500 ms, costs 10 and 5) are from the installed @smithy/core 3.35.2, not from this page.

### @smithy/core 3.35.2 (installed package source)

- ID: `sdk48-smithy-core`
- URL: <https://www.npmjs.com/package/@smithy/core/v/3.35.2>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 48
- この出典が支える主張:
  - submodules/retry/util-retry/retries-2026-config.js: Retry.v2026 is read once at module load from SMITHY_NEW_RETRIES_2026 === "true"; delay 100 or 50, throttling delay 500 or 1,000, costs 5/10 or 14/5
  - submodules/retry/util-retry/StandardRetryStrategy.js: capacity 500, refusal by error type, attempts, then capacity; retry-after hint clamped to computed delay + 5,000 ms
  - submodules/retry/service-error-classification: the throttling codes, the transient codes and statuses 500, 502, 503, 504, and that 429 or $retryable.throttling is throttling
  - submodules/retry/middleware-retry/retryMiddleware.js: amz-sdk-invocation-id and amz-sdk-request headers, $metadata.attempts and totalRetryDelay, a streaming payload is not retried, step finalizeRequest with priority high
  - submodules/client/middleware-stack/MiddlewareStack.js: the five steps and three priorities
  - submodules/client/smithy-client/defaults-mode.js and config/defaults-mode: defaultsMode is legacy when unset and then sets no timeout
  - submodules/client/util-waiter: minDelay, maxDelay, maxWaitTime, exponential backoff with jitter between polls, TimeoutError and AbortError
  - submodules/config: the Region is read from AWS_REGION or the profile's region; a missing Region throws 'Region is missing'
  - submodules/endpoints: AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_<SERVICE> and AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, and endpoint_url in the shared config file
- 注記: Read from node_modules, the dist-es build. Node.js loads the dist-cjs build of the same version; the tests run against that.
