### Considerations and limitations for CTAS queries

- ID: `athena49-ctas-considerations`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/ctas-considerations-limitations.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 49
- この出典が支える主張:
  - If the workgroup overrides the client-side setting for the query results location, Athena creates a CTAS table under <results location>/tables/<query-id>/
  - external_location must be empty; CTAS never overwrites data
  - A failed CTAS or INSERT INTO can leave orphaned data files that later queries read; the data manifest file lists them; Iceberg is recommended for atomic transactions
  - CTAS ignores ORDER BY; Parquet is the default format with GZIP as the default compression; a partitioned CTAS writes at most 100 partitions

### CREATE TABLE AS

- ID: `athena49-create-table-as`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/create-table-as.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 49
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A CTAS query that specifies external_location in a workgroup that enforces a query results location fails with an error
  - table_type is HIVE or ICEBERG, default HIVE; for Iceberg, is_external must be false and location is required; partitioned_by does not apply to Iceberg tables, partitioning does

### INSERT INTO

- ID: `athena49-insert-into`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/insert-into.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 49
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Each INSERT operation creates a new file rather than appending to an existing one; Athena does not rewrite or modify existing files
  - INSERT INTO writes at most 100 partitions, is not supported on bucketed tables or for federated queries, and expects the partition column last in the SELECT list
  - Supported formats include Parquet with ParquetHiveSerDe and JSON with the Hive JsonSerDe
  - Athena writes a data manifest file for each INSERT query to the query result location

### UNLOAD

- ID: `athena49-unload`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/unload.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 49
- この出典が支える主張:
  - UNLOAD writes the result of a SELECT as Parquet, ORC, Avro, JSON or text files without creating a table; SELECT itself only produces CSV
  - Except when writing to partitions, the TO location must hold no data; UNLOAD does not overwrite
  - Files are written in parallel with no ordering between them; orphaned data is not deleted on failure; at most 100 partitions; UNLOAD can be used with prepared statements

### Use parameterized queries (with the pages on execution parameters and prepared statements)

- ID: `athena49-parameterized-queries`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/querying-with-prepared-statements.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 49
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Parameterized queries help prevent SQL injection; they are execution parameters in any DML query, or PREPARE and EXECUTE statements
  - Execution parameters are not workgroup specific; prepared statements are, and a workgroup holds at most 1,000 of them
  - Parameterized queries are supported only for SELECT, INSERT INTO, CTAS and UNLOAD statements
  - Parameters are positional question marks, cannot be placed in quotes, and a value to be treated as a string must be enclosed in single quotes; CAST can be used in a value
  - The CLI passes the values in --execution-parameters
- 注記: Also read: querying-with-prepared-statements-querying-using-execution-parameters.html, ...-using-the-aws-cli.html, querying-with-prepared-statements-querying.html and ...-sql-statements.html.

### Reuse query results in Athena

- ID: `athena49-result-reuse`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/reusing-query-results.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 49
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Reuse is enabled per query; Athena looks for a previous execution of the same query in the same workgroup and returns its result without running the query
  - The default maximum age is 60 minutes and the largest is 7 days; Athena does not check for changes in the source data within that age, so stale results can be returned
  - The caller must have access to the tables and to the S3 location of the stored result
  - Not reused: non-deterministic queries such as LIMIT without ORDER BY, statements other than SELECT and EXECUTE, federated catalogs, tables under Lake Formation, and workgroups with managed query results

- この出典が支える主張:
  - A workgroup can store query results in Athena-managed storage instead of an S3 bucket of yours; results are kept 24 hours at no cost and then deleted
  - Managed query results do not support query result reuse; access is through GetQueryResults on the workgroup

### Query Apache Iceberg tables

- ID: `athena49-iceberg`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/querying-iceberg.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 49
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Athena performs read, time travel, write and DDL queries on Iceberg tables; it creates and operates on Iceberg v2 tables only
  - Only Iceberg tables in the AWS Glue catalog are supported, with AWS Glue optimistic locking only
  - Parquet, ORC and Avro files are supported; timestamps have millisecond precision in Athena

### Create Iceberg tables

- ID: `athena49-iceberg-create`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/querying-iceberg-creating-tables.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 49
- この出典が支える主張:
  - CREATE TABLE … PARTITIONED BY (col | transform) LOCATION … TBLPROPERTIES ('table_type'='ICEBERG'); CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE is an error for Iceberg
  - Partition columns are declared among the columns first and named in PARTITIONED BY without a type
  - Table properties and defaults: format parquet, vacuum_min_snapshots_to_keep 1, vacuum_max_snapshot_age_seconds 432000 (5 days), optimize_rewrite_delete_file_threshold 2

### Update Iceberg table data

- ID: `athena49-iceberg-update`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/querying-iceberg-updating-iceberg-table-data.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 49
- この出典が支える主張:
  - INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE each produce a new snapshot; UPDATE and DELETE write position delete files and enforce snapshot isolation
  - Athena always uses merge-on-read for UPDATE, MERGE INTO and DELETE FROM, whatever the table properties say

### MERGE INTO

- ID: `athena49-merge-into`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/merge-into-statement.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 49
- この出典が支える主張:
  - MERGE INTO target [AS alias] USING { source_table | query } [AS alias] ON condition, with WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE or UPDATE and WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (…) VALUES (…)
  - MERGE INTO is transactional and supported only for Iceberg tables in engine version 3
  - An error is raised when a single target row matches more than one source row

### Perform time travel and version travel queries

- ID: `athena49-iceberg-time-travel`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/querying-iceberg-time-travel-and-version-travel-queries.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 49
- この出典が支える主張:
  - SELECT … FROM table FOR TIMESTAMP AS OF timestamp reads a consistent snapshot as of that time; FOR VERSION AS OF takes a snapshot ID
  - The example uses FOR TIMESTAMP AS OF (current_timestamp - interval '1' day)

### Optimize Iceberg tables (with the OPTIMIZE and VACUUM statement pages)

- ID: `athena49-iceberg-optimize`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/querying-iceberg-data-optimization.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 49
- この出典が支える主張:
  - OPTIMIZE table REWRITE DATA USING BIN_PACK [WHERE predicate] rewrites data files by size and by the number of delete files; only partition columns are allowed in WHERE; it is charged by the data scanned during the rewrite
  - VACUUM table expires snapshots and removes orphan files; expired snapshots can no longer be reached by time travel; its S3 requests are charged
  - VACUUM needs s3:DeleteObject on the table's location; without it the query succeeds but the files are not deleted; it fails if the table sits at the root of a bucket
- 注記: Also read: optimize-statement.html and vacuum-statement.html.

- この出典が支える主張:
  - With a columnar format, reading fewer columns reduces the data read from S3; many small files hurt, columnar files most of all
  - Most compression formats must be read from the beginning, so compressed text files cannot in general be processed in parallel
  - ORDER BY with LIMIT is run as a top N query
- 注記: Also read: performance-tuning-query-optimization-techniques.html. Neither page says that LIMIT reduces the bytes scanned, or that it does not.

### Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: Overview

- ID: `agentcore-overview`

- この出典が支える主張:
  - The page lists these services by name: Harness, Runtime, Memory, Gateway, Identity, Code Interpreter, Browser, Observability, Payments, Evaluations, Optimization, Policy, Registry
  - Runtime is described as a secure, serverless runtime environment purpose-built for deploying and scaling dynamic AI agents and tools, with true session isolation and built-in identity
  - Gateway converts APIs, Lambda functions, and existing services into MCP-compatible tools and connects to pre-existing MCP servers
  - AgentCore offers consumption-based pricing with no upfront commitments or minimum fees
  - AgentCore services work together or independently with any open-source framework and with any foundation model

### Amazon Bedrock AgentCore pricing

- ID: `agentcore-pricing-page`
- URL: <https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agentcore/pricing/>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 50
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Runtime microVMs: v1 USD 0.0895 per vCPU-hour and USD 0.00945 per GB-hour; v2 USD 0.1276 per vCPU-hour and USD 0.0169 per GB-hour (consumption)
  - CPU is not charged during I/O wait; billing is per second with a 1-second minimum and a 128 MB memory minimum, over the whole session from microVM ready until session termination, idle periods included
  - With v2, idle memory is reclaimed after 120 seconds
  - Gateway: USD 0.005 per 1,000 API invocations, USD 0.025 per 1,000 search invocations, USD 0.02 per 100 tools indexed per month
  - Identity: USD 0.010 per 1,000 tokens or API keys requested for non-AWS resources, and no additional charge when used through Runtime or Gateway
  - Short-term memory: USD 0.25 per 1,000 new events through 2026-10-05; from 2026-10-06 USD 1.00 per GB ingested, USD 0.20 per GB retrieved, USD 0.10 per GB-month stored, each event billed at a minimum of 12 KB
  - Observability is charged under Amazon CloudWatch pricing
- 注記: The page states no Region for its table. The short-term memory prices by GB have no SKU in the ap-northeast-1 Price List read the same day.

### Quotas for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

### Host agent or tools with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime

- ID: `agentcore-runtime`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/agents-tools-runtime.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 50
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Each user session runs in a dedicated microVM with isolated CPU, memory, and filesystem; after session completion the microVM is terminated and memory is sanitized
  - Two compute types: microVMs and Instances; sessions run up to 8 hours on microVMs and up to 14 days on Instances
  - Works with frameworks such as LangGraph, Strands and CrewAI, and with custom agents that do not use a specific framework
  - A newer platform version, V2, starts the agent from a snapshot

### AgentCore Runtime: microVMs (key components, platform versions)

- ID: `agentcore-runtime-how`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-how-it-works.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 50
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A runtime has immutable versions; a DEFAULT endpoint is created with the runtime and follows the latest version
  - platformVersion is V1 or V2 and V1 is the default; V2 is available in us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-2, eu-west-1 and ap-northeast-1
  - On V2 create and update take minutes and the container must report healthy within 120 seconds
  - AWS CloudFormation and the AWS CDK do not currently support setting platformVersion
- 注記: aws-cdk-lib 2.273.0 does declare a platformVersion property on CfnRuntime. The stack leaves it unset.

### AgentCore Runtime: HTTP protocol contract

- ID: `agentcore-http-contract`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-http-protocol-contract.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 50
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The agent listens on host 0.0.0.0, port 8080
  - POST /invocations takes JSON and answers JSON or text/event-stream
  - GET /ping answers a JSON body whose status is Healthy or HealthyBusy; while HealthyBusy the session is considered active
  - A 4xx or 5xx from the agent is returned to the caller as 424 RuntimeClientError
  - Without an Authorization header an OAuth-configured runtime answers 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header

### Use isolated sessions for agents

- ID: `agentcore-sessions`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-sessions.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 50
- この出典が支える主張:
  - AgentCore does not enforce session-to-user mappings; the client backend should maintain the relationship between users and their session IDs
  - A session is created on the first invoke with a runtimeSessionId provided by the application, of at least 33 characters
  - A session's compute stops after inactivity (default 15 minutes) or at the maximum lifetime (default 8 hours); the next invocation with the same ID provisions new compute
  - Data in memory or on disk persists only for the compute lifecycle; AgentCore Memory is the documented place for what must outlive it
  - The session header for HTTP is X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Session-Id

### Authenticate and authorize with Inbound Auth and Outbound Auth

- ID: `agentcore-runtime-auth`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-oauth.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 50
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A runtime supports either IAM SigV4 or JWT bearer token inbound auth, not both at once
  - The JWT authorizer takes a discovery URL, allowed audiences, allowed clients, allowed scopes and required custom claims; allowedClients is checked against the client_id claim
  - The X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-User-Id header is not verified against an authenticated identity and needs bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeForUser
  - The Authorization header can be passed to the agent through the request header allowlist, and the agent may skip signature validation because the runtime has already validated the token
  - The invoke URL for a bearer token is https://bedrock-agentcore.<region>.amazonaws.com/runtimes/<escaped ARN>/invocations?qualifier=DEFAULT
  - Agents created on or after 2025-10-13 get workload identity permissions from a service-linked role

### Security best practices for AgentCore Runtime

- ID: `agentcore-security`

### What is the Amazon Chime SDK?

- ID: `chime-sdk-what-is`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/chime-sdk/latest/dg/what-is-chime-sdk.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13

- この出典が支える主張:
  - The Amazon Chime SDK is a set of real-time communications components for messaging, audio, video, and screen sharing in web or mobile applications
  - Pay-for-use pricing with no upfront fees; messaging, media pipelines, speech enhancement and PSTN audio are priced separately

### Using the Amazon Chime SDK (prerequisites, concepts, architecture)

- ID: `chime-sdk-concepts`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/chime-sdk/latest/dg/meetings-sdk.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 51
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The SDK works independently of any Amazon Chime administrator account
  - A server application manages meeting and attendee resources; a client application uses them to make media connections
  - A meeting is an ephemeral resource; an attendee is identified by an AttendeeId; a join token is an opaque secret the server must transfer securely to the client authorized to join on behalf of the attendee
  - Clients signal over secure WebSockets and DTLS; audio is mixed by the service; video is forwarded by an SFU, up to 25 simultaneous videos per meeting
  - Data messages of up to 2 KB; quotas are per API endpoint
  - Supported browsers for the JavaScript client library

### Creating meetings using the Amazon Chime SDK

- ID: `chime-sdk-create-meetings`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/chime-sdk/latest/dg/create-mtgs.html>

- この出典が支える主張:
  - The server calls CreateMeeting with a MediaRegion and CreateAttendee, and transfers both to the client
  - A meeting ends on DeleteMeeting, when it exceeds 24 hours, or when no attendees are connected for five continuous minutes

### Understanding Amazon Chime SDK meeting lifecycle events

- ID: `chime-sdk-events`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/chime-sdk/latest/dg/using-events.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 51
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Events go to EventBridge, SNS or SQS with source aws.chime and detail-type 'Chime Meeting State Change'
  - chime:AttendeeAuthorized is sent when a user already in the meeting joins again with the same join token: the meeting is handed off to the new device
  - chime:AttendeeDropped is sent when the service receives no packets for 10 to 15 seconds; AttendeeLeft and AttendeeDropped are never both sent for one leave
  - chime:MeetingEnded is also sent on DeleteMeeting

### Preventing image tags from being overwritten in Amazon ECR

- ID: `ecr52-tag-mutability`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/image-tag-mutability.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 52
- この出典が支える主張:
  - With tag immutability on, pushing an image with a tag that is already in the repository returns ImageTagAlreadyExistsException
  - Immutable applies to all tags; exclusion filters with wildcards (*) make a few tags mutable in an immutable repository, or immutable in a mutable one
  - Mutable is recommended for repositories that use pull through cache, so ECR can update cached images
  - Encryption settings cannot be changed once the repository is created

### Encryption at rest

- ID: `ecr52-encryption`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/encryption-at-rest.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 52
- この出典が支える主張:
  - By default ECR encrypts with Amazon S3-managed keys (AES-256) at no additional charge
  - A repository can instead use a KMS key: the AWS managed key aws/ecr or a customer managed key in the same Region
  - The encryption configuration cannot be changed after the repository is created
  - Revoking the grants ECR created on the KMS key makes the repository's images unreadable; KMS keys have their own cost
  - DSSE-KMS is only available in the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions

### Automate the cleanup of images by using lifecycle policies in Amazon ECR

- ID: `ecr52-lifecycle`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/LifecyclePolicies.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 52
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Images are expired or archived within 24 hours after they meet the criteria, and each action is recorded in CloudTrail
  - All rules are evaluated at the same time; then they are applied by priority, and an image is expired by exactly one or zero rules
  - An image that matches the tagging requirements of a rule cannot be expired by a rule with a lower priority
  - An image referenced by a manifest list cannot be expired before the manifest list
  - imageCountMoreThan sorts by pushed_at_time, youngest first, and expires everything beyond the count; sinceImagePushed expires images older than the given number of days
  - Reference artifacts are expired within 24 hours of their subject image
  - A filter of prod* matches prod, prod1 and production-team1

### Lifecycle policy properties in Amazon ECR

- ID: `ecr52-lifecycle-properties`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/lifecycle_policy_parameters.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 52
- この出典が支える主張:
  - rulePriority must be unique; a rule with tagStatus any must have the highest value
  - tagStatus is tagged, untagged or any; tagged requires tagPatternList or tagPrefixList, untagged must omit both
  - At most four wildcards per pattern string
  - countType is imageCountMoreThan, sinceImagePushed, sinceImagePulled or sinceImageTransitioned; countUnit is days and only for the time-based types; countNumber is a positive integer
  - The action type is expire or transition (to archive storage)

  - Archived images have a minimum storage duration of 90 days

### Scan images for software vulnerabilities in Amazon ECR

- ID: `ecr52-scanning`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/image-scanning.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13

- この出典が支える主張:
  - Basic scanning uses AWS native technology and covers operating system vulnerabilities, on push or manually
  - Enhanced scanning integrates with Amazon Inspector, covers operating system and programming language packages, on push or continuously
  - Switching between the two makes the previously established scans unavailable
  - Basic scanning results are read with DescribeImageScanFindings, not from DescribeImages
  - Archived images cannot be scanned

  - An image can be scanned once per 24 hours with basic scanning, the scan on push included
  - Repositories that match no scan-on-push filter are set to manual
  - ECR sends an event to EventBridge when an image scan completes
  - Severity comes from the upstream distribution when available, otherwise from the CVSS score

### Scan images for OS and programming language package vulnerabilities in Amazon ECR

- ID: `ecr52-scanning-enhanced`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/image-scanning-enhanced.html>

- 参照する章: 52
- この出典が支える主張:
  - ECR does not charge for enhanced scanning; Amazon Inspector does
  - When enhanced scanning is first turned on, only images pushed in the last 14 days are recognized; older ones show SCAN_ELIGIBILITY_EXPIRED
  - With enhanced scanning on, repositories that match no filter are not scanned, and manual scans are not supported
  - Inspector emits EventBridge events when an initial scan completes and when a finding is created, updated or closed
  - By default Inspector monitors images until they are deleted or enhanced scanning is disabled

### Sync an upstream registry with an Amazon ECR private registry

- ID: `ecr52-pull-through-cache`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/pull-through-cache.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 52
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Upstreams: Amazon ECR Public, the Kubernetes registry and Quay without authentication; Docker Hub, Azure Container Registry, GitHub Container Registry, GitLab Container Registry and Chainguard with a Secrets Manager secret; Amazon ECR with an IAM role
  - The first pull creates the repository and caches the image; later pulls check upstream at most once every 24 hours
  - If the upstream cannot be reached, the last cached image is still pulled
  - Secrets must be named with the ecr-pullthroughcache/ prefix, in the same account and Region
  - Lambda does not support pulling through a pull through cache rule
  - Repositories created by a rule are mutable, AES256, with no policy and no lifecycle policy unless a repository creation template matches
  - Turning on tag immutability stops ECR from updating a cached tag
  - The first pull may need a route to the internet even when interface VPC endpoints are used; later pulls do not

### Private image replication in Amazon ECR

- ID: `ecr52-replication`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/replication.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 52
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Replication is configured on the registry, across Regions and across accounts
  - Only content pushed after replication is configured is replicated
  - Cross-account replication needs a registry policy in the destination account allowing ecr:ReplicateImage and ecr:CreateRepository; the source needs none
  - Most images replicate in under 30 minutes
  - Replication performs no deletes; repository settings and lifecycle policies are not replicated unless a repository creation template supplies them
  - With tag immutability on in the destination, an image whose tag already exists is replicated without the tag
  - Up to 25 rules and 25 unique destinations

### AWS CLI 2.35.11: ECR service model and waiters

- ID: `ecr52-awscli-model`
- URL: <https://github.com/aws/aws-cli/blob/2.35.11/awscli/botocore/data/ecr/2015-09-21/service-2.json>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 52
- この出典が支える主張:
  - StartLifecyclePolicyPreview takes repositoryName and lifecyclePolicyText; GetLifecyclePolicyPreview returns status, previewResults (imageDigest, imageTags, imagePushedAt, action, appliedRulePriority) and summary
  - The waiter image-scan-complete polls DescribeImageScanFindings every 5 seconds up to 60 times, succeeding on COMPLETE and failing on FAILED; lifecycle-policy-preview-complete polls every 5 seconds up to 20 times
  - FindingSeverity is INFORMATIONAL, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL or UNDEFINED
- 注記: Read from the copy installed in the Nix shell (awscli2 2.35.11, service-2.json and waiters-2.json), not from this URL.

### How Amazon EFS works

- ID: `efs-how-it-works`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/how-it-works.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 53
- この出典が支える主張:
  - EFS is mounted in a VPC through NFS versions 4.0 and 4.1
  - A file system can be accessed concurrently from multiple NFS clients, in multiple Availability Zones of the same Region
  - A mount target provides an IP address for an NFSv4 endpoint; one mount target can be created in each Availability Zone, in one of its subnets
  - The file system's DNS name resolves to the mount target in the client's own Availability Zone
  - An EFS file system can have mount targets in only one VPC at a time
  - AWS recommends reaching the file system through a mount target in the same Availability Zone, for performance and cost
  - A One Zone file system can have only a single mount target

### Features of Amazon EFS

- ID: `efs-features`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/features.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 53
- この出典が支える主張:
  - "Amazon EFS provides the close-to-open consistency semantics that applications expect from NFS"
  - Writes to a Regional file system are durably stored across Availability Zones when the application writes synchronously (O_DIRECT, fsync) or closes the file
  - Applications that perform synchronous data access and non-appending writes have read-after-write consistency
  - EFS supports only advisory locking; reads and writes do not check for conflicting locks
  - A single file can have up to 512 locks across all connected instances and users
  - Regional file systems store data across multiple Availability Zones; One Zone file systems store it in one and are not resilient to the loss of that zone
  - One Zone file systems are available in Tokyo only in apne1-az1 and apne1-az4
  - Storage classes: Standard, Infrequent Access, Archive; IA and Archive have a minimum billing charge of 128 KiB per file and first-byte latency of tens of milliseconds; Archive has a 90-day minimum storage duration and needs Elastic throughput
  - Replication keeps a destination file system in a Region of your choice in step, designed for an RPO and RTO of minutes

### Amazon EFS performance specifications

- ID: `efs-performance`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/performance.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 53
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Latency for General Purpose Regional file systems: about 1 ms for reads and about 2.7 ms for writes, stated as best case under optimal conditions; One Zone: about 1 ms and about 1.6 ms
  - General Purpose is the default performance mode and is recommended for all file systems; Max I/O is a previous generation and is not supported with Elastic throughput or One Zone
  - Throughput modes: Elastic (recommended, the default), Provisioned, Bursting
  - With Elastic throughput you pay only for the metadata and data read or written
  - Bursting: baseline 50 KiBps per GiB of Standard storage, bursts to 100 MiBps minimum while credits last, and a metered 1 MiBps for every file system
  - Every NFS request counts as 4 KB of throughput or its actual size, whichever is larger
  - After switching to Provisioned or changing its amount, switching away or lowering it is blocked for 24 hours

### Amazon EFS quotas

- ID: `efs-limits`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/limits.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 53
- この出典が支える主張:
  - 1,000 file systems per account per Region and 10,000 access points per file system by default (both can be raised)
  - 25,000 connections per file system; one mount target per file system per Availability Zone; one VPC per file system; 5 security groups per mount target
  - 512 locks on a single file across all instances and users; 65,536 locks per mount per connection
  - File name up to 255 bytes; single file up to 47.9 TiB; 177 hard links
  - Unsupported NFSv4 features include mandatory locking, ACLs, extended attributes, and client delegations
  - EFS does not support NFSv2 or NFSv3, the nconnect mount option, or Microsoft Windows clients

### Working with access points

- ID: `efs-access-points`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/efs-access-points.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 53
- この出典が支える主張:
  - An access point is an application-specific entry point that can enforce a user identity and a root directory
  - Security groups apply at the mount target, not at the access point; an access point is available in every zone that has a mount target
  - Mounting through an access point on EC2 uses the EFS mount helper with the tls option: mount -t efs -o tls,iam,accesspoint=fsap-... fs-...: /mountpoint

### Enforcing a user identity using an access point

- ID: `efs-enforce-identity`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/enforce-identity-access-points.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 53
- この出典が支える主張:
  - EFS replaces the NFS client's user and group IDs with the access point's for all file system operations
  - New files and directories are owned by the access point's user ID and group ID
  - Setting the access point's UID or GID to 0 requires the ClientRootAccess permission

### Enforcing a root directory with an access point

- ID: `efs-enforce-root`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/enforce-root-directory-access-point.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 53
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The access point's Path becomes the root directory for clients that mount through it
  - EFS creates the root directory only when owner UID, owner GID, and permissions are given; otherwise mounting fails if the directory does not exist
  - The path can be at most 100 characters and include up to four subdirectories

### Using IAM to control access to file systems

- ID: `efs-iam-nfs`

- この出典が支える主張:
  - The default file system policy grants full access to any anonymous client that can connect through a mount target, and is in effect whenever no user-configured policy is
  - An allow in either an identity policy or the file system policy grants access; it does not need to be in both
  - Client actions: elasticfilesystem:ClientMount (read-only access), ClientWrite, ClientRootAccess
  - Condition keys for NFS clients: aws:SecureTransport, aws:SourceIp, elasticfilesystem:AccessPointArn, elasticfilesystem:AccessedViaMountTarget
  - IAM authorization on EC2 requires the EFS mount helper

### Managing storage lifecycle

- ID: `efs-lifecycle`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/lifecycle-management-efs.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 53

  - The page gives the defaults as 30 days to IA, 90 days to Archive, and no transition back to Standard
  - File metadata always stays in Standard; listing a directory does not count as access

### How Amazon EFS reports file system and object sizes

- ID: `efs-metered-sizes`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/metered-sizes.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 53
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Each file, directory, symlink is metered as 2 KiB of metadata plus data in 4 KiB increments
  - An empty file contributes 6 KiB; a new file system has an empty root directory and a metered size of 6 KiB
  - With Elastic throughput, metadata operations are metered in 1 KiB increments after the first 4 KiB, and data operations in 1 KiB increments after the first 32 KiB
  - IA and Archive are metered with a minimum of 128 KiB per file, and their data access in 128 KiB increments; their metadata (2 KiB per file) stays in Standard
  - Reads are metered at one third the rate of other operations for throughput accounting

### Backing up EFS file systems

- ID: `efs-backup`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/awsbackup.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 53
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Automatic backups are on by default for file systems created in the console; through the CLI or API, only for One Zone file systems
  - The default plan takes daily backups and keeps them 35 days, in a default vault that cannot be deleted
  - Backups are incremental; a restore goes to a new or an existing file system, whole or item by item
  - The default EFS backup vault's access policy denies deleting recovery points until the policy is changed
  - Changes made while a backup runs can leave it inconsistent

### What is Amazon S3? (data consistency model)

- ID: `efs-s3-consistency`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/Welcome.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 53
- この出典が支える主張:
  - S3 gives strong read-after-write consistency for PUT and DELETE
  - Updates to a single key are atomic: a concurrent GET returns the old data or the new data, never partial or corrupt data
  - S3 does not lock objects for concurrent writers; of two simultaneous PUTs the later timestamp wins

### Amazon Kinesis Data Streams Terminology and concepts

- ID: `kinesis-concepts`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/key-concepts.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 54
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A stream is a set of shards, and each shard has a sequence of data records with a sequence number assigned by Kinesis Data Streams
  - A partition key is a Unicode string of at most 256 characters; MD5 maps it to a 128-bit integer, and the hash key ranges of the shards decide which shard a record belongs to
  - The retention period is 24 hours by default and can be raised to 8,760 hours (365 days), with additional charges above 24 hours
  - A shard supports up to 5 read transactions a second and 2 MB a second of reads, and up to 1,000 records a second and 1 MB a second of writes including partition keys
  - There can be several applications for one stream, each consuming it independently and concurrently
  - The Kinesis Client Library keeps its consumption metadata in DynamoDB tables
- 注記: This page still says a data blob can be up to 1 MB. The quotas page and the API reference, read the same day, say 1 MiB by default and up to 10 MiB as a setting of the stream.

### Quotas and limits (Kinesis Data Streams)

- ID: `kinesis-quotas`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/service-sizes-and-limits.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 54
- この出典が支える主張:
  - On-demand: 50 streams per account by default; a new stream has 4 MB/s of write and 8 MB/s of read throughput and scales up to 200 MB/s of write outside us-east-1, us-west-2 and eu-west-1
  - Provisioned: each shard supports up to 1 MB/s or 1,000 records/s of writes and up to 2 MB/s of reads; the default shard quota outside three named Regions is 1,000 or 6,000 per account
  - GetRecords: 5 transactions per second per shard, up to 10,000 records and 10 MB per call
  - PutRecords: up to 500 records per request and 10 MiB for the entire request including partition keys
  - A shard iterator expires 5 minutes after it is returned
  - Up to 20 registered (enhanced fan-out) consumers per stream in On-demand Standard and Provisioned modes, 50 in On-demand Advantage
  - A stream can switch between on-demand and provisioned twice within 24 hours
- 注記: The PutRecord row says 10 MiB per second per shard and the PutRecords row 1 MB per second. The chapter uses 1 MB per second, which the concepts page and the pricing page also give.

### Choose the right mode to stream in

- ID: `kinesis-modes`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/how-do-i-size-a-stream.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 54
- この出典が支える主張:
  - There are three modes: On-demand Standard, On-demand Advantage, and Provisioned
  - On-demand manages shards itself, accommodates up to double the peak write throughput of the previous 30 days, and splits a shard when its traffic exceeds 500 KB/s
  - On-demand does not isolate a single hot partition key: a key that exceeds one shard's 1 MB/s or 1,000 records/s keeps being throttled, and provisioned mode is recommended for such keys
  - On-demand Advantage is an account-level setting with no per-stream charge that commits the account to at least 25 MiB/s of ingest and 25 MiB/s of retrieval across its on-demand streams, for at least 24 hours
  - number_of_shards = ceiling(max(incoming_write_bandwidth_in_KiB/1024, outgoing_read_bandwidth_in_KiB/2048)) for provisioned mode

### Change the data retention period

- ID: `kinesis-retention`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/kinesis-extended-retention.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 54
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Records are stored for 24 hours by default and up to 8,760 hours
  - Decreasing the retention period makes records older than the new period inaccessible almost immediately
  - The retention period is described as a safety net that gives consumers more time to recover

- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 54
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A failed record in a PutRecords request does not stop the records after it, and the response array has one element per request record in the same order
  - Unsuccessful records carry ErrorCode (ProvisionedThroughputExceededException or InternalFailure) and are to be included in a subsequent request
  - All records with the same partition key map to the same shard
  - Records received through GetRecords are strictly ordered by sequence number

### PutRecords (Kinesis API Reference)

- ID: `kinesis-api-putrecords`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kinesis/latest/APIReference/API_PutRecords.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 54
- この出典が支える主張:
  - PutRecords does not guarantee the ordering of records, because a single record failure does not stop the processing of subsequent records
  - To read records in the order they were written, the reference says to use PutRecord instead and write to the same shard
  - A request holds at most 500 records and 10 MiB including partition keys
  - After a record is written, neither the record nor its order within the stream can be changed

### PutRecord (Kinesis API Reference)

- ID: `kinesis-api-putrecord`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kinesis/latest/APIReference/API_PutRecord.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 54
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Sequence numbers increase over time and are specific to a shard, not comparable across shards
  - SequenceNumberForOrdering guarantees strictly increasing sequence numbers for puts from the same client to the same partition key; without it records are coarsely ordered by arrival time
  - The data blob plus the partition key must not exceed the maximum record size (10 MiB)

### GetShardIterator (Kinesis API Reference)

- ID: `kinesis-api-getsharditerator`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kinesis/latest/APIReference/API_GetShardIterator.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 54
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The iterator types are AT_SEQUENCE_NUMBER, AFTER_SEQUENCE_NUMBER, AT_TIMESTAMP, TRIM_HORIZON (the oldest record still in the shard), and LATEST
  - A shard iterator expires 5 minutes after it is returned

### GetRecords (Kinesis API Reference)

- ID: `kinesis-api-getrecords`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kinesis/latest/APIReference/API_GetRecords.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 54
- この出典が支える主張:
  - When a shard has been closed and read to its end, NextShardIterator is null
  - MillisBehindLatest tells how far the reader is behind the tip of the shard
  - A record is up to 1 MiB by default, and large records of up to 10 MiB are supported
  - ApproximateArrivalTimestamp is set when the stream stores a record; its accuracy and monotonicity are not guaranteed

### Develop enhanced fan-out consumers with dedicated throughput

- ID: `kinesis-efo`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/enhanced-consumers.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 54
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Shared-throughput consumers share 2 MB/s per shard among them and pull with GetRecords; an enhanced fan-out consumer gets its own 2 MB/s per shard, pushed over HTTP/2 with SubscribeToShard
  - Propagation delay averages around 200 ms with one shared-throughput consumer and around 1,000 ms with five, against typically 70 ms with enhanced fan-out
  - Enhanced fan-out has a data retrieval cost and a consumer-shard hour cost

### Complete the resharding action

- ID: `kinesis-resharding`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/kinesis-using-sdk-java-after-resharding.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 54
- この出典が支える主張:
  - After a reshard the parent shard is closed: no records are added, and its existing records stay readable until they expire
  - Reading a child shard before the parent is exhausted can return a hash key's records out of the order of their sequence numbers; the guide says to read the parent to its end first

### Using Lambda to process records from Amazon Kinesis Data Streams

- ID: `kinesis-lambda-overview`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-kinesis.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 54
- この出典が支える主張:
  - With a standard iterator Lambda polls each shard at a base rate of once per second and shares read throughput with the shard's other consumers
  - Lambda processes the records of each shard in order and stops processing further records of a shard when the function returns an error
  - A batching window of up to 5 minutes can be set; a batch is also cut at the 6 MB payload limit
  - Event source mappings process each event at least once, and the guide strongly recommends idempotent function code
  - ParallelizationFactor from 1 to 10 processes one shard with several concurrent batches while keeping order at the partition-key level
  - The shape of the event a function receives from a Kinesis event source

### Process Amazon Kinesis Data Streams records with Lambda

- ID: `kinesis-lambda-create`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-kinesis-create.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 54
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The permissions Lambda needs: kinesis:DescribeStream, DescribeStreamSummary, GetRecords, GetShardIterator, ListShards, and SubscribeToShard
  - Polling starts and stops with a delay of up to several minutes, so a mapping created with LATEST can miss events; TRIM_HORIZON or AT_TIMESTAMP avoids it
  - Several event source mappings can process the same stream with several functions

### Lambda parameters for Amazon Kinesis Data Streams event source mappings

- ID: `kinesis-lambda-parameters`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-kinesis-parameters.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 54
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Defaults: BatchSize 100 (maximum 10,000), BisectBatchOnFunctionError false, MaximumBatchingWindowInSeconds 0, MaximumRecordAgeInSeconds -1 (maximum 604,800), MaximumRetryAttempts -1 (maximum 10,000), ParallelizationFactor 1 (maximum 10)
  - StartingPosition is AT_TIMESTAMP, TRIM_HORIZON, or LATEST

### Configuring partial batch response with Kinesis Data Streams and Lambda

- ID: `kinesis-lambda-batch-failures`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-kinesis-batchfailurereporting.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 54
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Without ReportBatchItemFailures in FunctionResponseTypes Lambda does not process a partial batch response, even when the function returns one
  - With several batchItemFailures Lambda uses the lowest sequence number as the checkpoint and retries all records from there
  - With both BisectBatchOnFunctionError and ReportBatchItemFailures, the batch is bisected at the returned sequence number and only the remaining records are retried
  - An empty or null batchItemFailures list is a complete success

### Retain discarded batch records for a Kinesis Data Streams event source in Lambda

- ID: `kinesis-lambda-failure-destination`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/kinesis-on-failure-destination.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 54
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A function error is retried until the records expire, exceed MaximumRecordAgeInSeconds, or reach MaximumRetryAttempts; splitting a batch does not consume the retry quota
  - With the default settings a bad record can block processing on its shard for up to one week
  - An SQS or SNS destination receives only metadata (shardId, startSequenceNumber, endSequenceNumber, arrival times, batchSize, streamArn); the records must be read back from the stream before they expire. An S3 destination also receives the invocation record
  - The execution role needs sqs:SendMessage for an SQS destination

### Configure network access to your Amazon Managed Grafana workspace

### How to prevent object overwrites with conditional writes

- ID: `nova-s3-conditional-writes`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/conditional-writes.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 56
- この出典が支える主張:
  - PutObject with If-None-Match: * fails with 412 when the key exists; of several such writes the first to finish succeeds
  - PutObject with If-Match compares the ETag and fails with 412 when it differs; it needs s3:PutObject and s3:GetObject
  - A 409 Conflict is possible when a delete races a conditional write; a 404 when the object was deleted before an If-Match write

### Quotas in Amazon Polly

- ID: `polly-limits`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/polly/latest/dg/limits.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 57
- この出典が支える主張:
  - SynthesizeSpeech input is up to 3000 billed characters (6000 total characters); SSML tags are not counted as billed characters
  - The output audio stream of SynthesizeSpeech is limited to 10 minutes; any remaining speech is cut off
  - StartSpeechSynthesisTask input is up to 100,000 billed characters (200,000 total characters)
  - SynthesizeSpeech throttle rates: standard 80 tps (burst 100), neural 8 tps (burst 10), long-form 8 tps (burst 10), generative 8 tps; neural supports up to 18 concurrent requests
  - A throttled request returns HTTP status 400 with ThrottlingException; the page recommends retrying with backoff and jitter
  - Up to 100 lexicons per account, names up to 20 alphanumeric characters, each up to 40,000 characters; up to five lexicons per request; the size of a lexicon affects the latency of SynthesizeSpeech
  - SSML limits: the audio, lexicon, lookup and voice tags are not supported; a break is at most 10 seconds

### SynthesizeSpeech

- ID: `polly-api-synthesize-speech`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/polly/latest/dg/API_SynthesizeSpeech.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 57
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Engine is standard, neural, long-form or generative; standard is the default, and a voice the standard engine does not support results in an error
  - OutputFormat is json, mp3, ogg_opus, ogg_vorbis, pcm, mulaw or alaw; pcm is signed 16-bit mono little-endian
  - TextType is ssml or text, text by default; SpeechMarkTypes are sentence, ssml, viseme, word
  - The response carries ContentType (audio/mpeg for mp3) and x-amzn-RequestCharacters, the number of characters synthesized
  - TextLengthExceededException: at most 6000 characters, of which no more than 3000 billed; InvalidSsmlException for invalid SSML

  - A speech request and a speech marks request for the same text are both billed
  - Generated speech can be cached and replayed at no additional cost

### AWS ブログ: 監査のユースケースで Amazon QLDB を Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL に置き換える

- ID: `ledger-qldb-blog-audit`
- URL: <https://aws.amazon.com/jp/blogs/news/replace-qldb-with-amazon-aurora-postgresql/>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 58
- この出典が支える主張:
  - QLDB's journal was an append-only structure holding a sequential, immutable record of transactions in blocks chained with cryptographic hashes; the post calls immutability and cryptographic verifiability the two properties unique to QLDB
  - Aurora PostgreSQL keeps no persistent, immutable record of changes; the history has to be produced as audit data and stored outside the database
  - The post's replacements are pgAudit with CloudWatch Logs, audit tables filled by triggers, AWS DMS, and Database Activity Streams; it names no replacement for the cryptographic verification
- 注記: Japanese translation (2024-08-20) of the AWS Database Blog post of 2024-07-18. The English URL I tried answered with a redirect, so the Japanese page is the one that was read.

### Locking objects with Object Lock

- ID: `ledger-s3-object-lock`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 58
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Object Lock works only in buckets that have S3 Versioning enabled, and a lock protects one object version
  - Retention periods and legal holds do not prevent new versions from being created or delete markers from being added on top
  - Putting an object under the key of a protected object creates a new version; the protected version stays locked
  - Compliance mode: a protected version cannot be overwritten or deleted by any user, including the root user; the mode cannot be changed and the period cannot be shortened; the only way to delete it early is to delete the AWS account
  - Governance mode: deleting or changing the lock needs s3:BypassGovernanceRetention and the x-amz-bypass-governance-retention:true header; the S3 console sends that header by default
  - A DELETE with a version ID on a protected version returns 403; a DELETE without one returns 200 and inserts a delete marker
  - The page notes that S3 Object Lock has been assessed by Cohasset Associates for use in environments subject to SEC 17a-4, CFTC, and FINRA regulations
  - A bucket default retention is a duration in days or years, added to each new version's creation time; a retention period can be extended by anyone with s3:PutObjectRetention

### Configuring S3 Object Lock

- ID: `ledger-s3-object-lock-configure`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock-configure.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 58
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Object Lock can be enabled when a bucket is created or on an existing bucket
  - After Object Lock is enabled on a bucket, it cannot be disabled and versioning cannot be suspended
  - A bucket with Object Lock cannot be a destination for server access logs

### How to prevent object overwrites with conditional writes

- ID: `ledger-s3-conditional-writes`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/conditional-writes.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 58
- この出典が支える主張:
  - PutObject with If-None-Match: * fails with 412 Precondition Failed when an object with that key exists, and needs only s3:PutObject
  - In a versioned bucket the header looks at the current version only: when there is none, or it is a delete marker, the write succeeds
  - A 409 Conflict is possible when a delete finishes first; a PutObject can be retried after it

### Multi-AZ DB instance deployments for Amazon RDS

- ID: `rds59-multi-az-instance`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZSingleStandby.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A Multi-AZ DB instance deployment keeps a synchronous standby replica in another Availability Zone
  - The standby cannot serve read traffic
  - Synchronous replication can raise write and commit latency compared with Single-AZ

### Failing over a Multi-AZ DB instance for Amazon RDS

- ID: `rds59-multi-az-failover`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZ.Failover.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Failover times are typically 60-120 seconds, longer with large transactions or a lengthy recovery
  - Failover changes the DNS record of the DB instance to point to the standby, and existing connections must be re-established
  - The listed reasons for a failover include OS patching, an unhealthy or unreachable primary host, a customer modification, a storage failure, and a reboot with failover

### Best practices for Amazon RDS

- ID: `rds59-best-practices`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_BestPractices.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A client that caches DNS should use a TTL of less than 30 seconds, because the address of a DB instance can change after a failover
  - Test failover to learn how long it takes for your use case

### Multi-AZ DB cluster deployments for Amazon RDS

- ID: `rds59-multi-az-cluster`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/multi-az-db-clusters-concepts.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A Multi-AZ DB cluster has one writer and two readable DB instances in three Availability Zones
  - Replication is semisynchronous: a commit needs the acknowledgment of at least one reader
  - Supported instance classes are db.c6gd, db.m5d, db.m6gd, db.m6id, db.m6idn, db.m8gd, db.r5d, db.r6gd, db.r6id, db.r6idn, db.r8gd and db.x2iedn
  - Multi-AZ DB clusters are not Aurora DB clusters

### Failing over a Multi-AZ DB cluster for Amazon RDS

- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/multi-az-db-clusters-concepts-failover.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59

### Working with read replicas for Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL

- ID: `rds59-pg-read-replicas`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PostgreSQL.Replication.ReadReplicas.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - PostgreSQL read replicas are read-only, and a promotion cannot be reversed
  - Point-in-time recovery is not supported for read replicas
  - With no transactions on the source, a PostgreSQL replica reports a lag of up to five minutes

### Read replica configuration with PostgreSQL

- ID: `rds59-pg-read-replica-config`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PostgreSQL.Replication.ReadReplicas.Configuration.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A PostgreSQL read replica is an asynchronously created physical replica that uses native streaming replication
  - Up to 15 read replicas per source DB instance in the same Region
  - A read replica can itself be a Multi-AZ DB instance

### Monitoring and tuning the replication process

- ID: `rds59-pg-read-replica-monitor`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PostgreSQL.Replication.ReadReplicas.Monitor.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The ReplicaLag metric is the result of SELECT extract(epoch from now() - pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp())

### Amazon CloudWatch metrics for Amazon RDS

- ID: `rds59-metrics`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-metrics.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:

  - The T DB instance classes are recommended only for development, test and other non-production servers
  - Surplus CPU credits beyond what an instance can earn in 24 hours incur an additional charge

### DB instance class types

- ID: `rds59-instance-classes`

- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The families are general purpose (db.m), memory optimized (db.r, db.x, db.z), compute optimized (db.c6gd, Multi-AZ DB clusters only), and burstable (db.t)
  - db.t4g instances are configured for Unlimited mode and can burst beyond the baseline for an additional charge

### Amazon RDS DB instance storage

- ID: `rds59-storage`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_Storage.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - gp3 gives a baseline of 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s; for PostgreSQL the baseline rises to 12,000 IOPS and 500 MiB/s from 400 GiB
  - gp3 storage for PostgreSQL ranges from 20 to 65,536 GiB
  - Magnetic storage is deprecated and new DB instances cannot use it

### Managing capacity automatically with Amazon RDS storage autoscaling

- ID: `rds59-storage-autoscaling`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PIOPS.Autoscaling.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Autoscaling starts when free space is at most 10 percent of allocated storage for at least five minutes, and fewer than four storage modifications happened in the past 24 hours
  - The increment is the greatest of 10 GiB, 10 percent of allocated storage, and the growth predicted for the next 7 hours
  - Allocated storage cannot be reduced after it has been allocated
  - The maximum storage threshold must be at least 10 percent above the allocated storage

### Overview of parameter groups

- ID: `rds59-parameter-groups`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/parameter-groups-overview.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The settings of a default parameter group cannot be modified
  - A static parameter takes effect only after a manual reboot; a dynamic parameter takes effect immediately by default
  - A pending-reboot status does not cause an automatic reboot in the next maintenance window

### Maintaining a DB instance

- ID: `rds59-maintenance`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_UpgradeDBInstance.Maintenance.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Every DB instance has a weekly maintenance window; an unspecified one is a 30-minute window on a random day inside an 8-hour block per Region (13:00-21:00 UTC for Tokyo)
  - The window decides when pending operations start and does not limit how long they run
  - With Multi-AZ, operating system updates are applied to the standby first, then the standby is promoted
  - For an engine upgrade of a Multi-AZ DB instance, primary and standby are upgraded at the same time and both are unavailable

### Upgrading a DB instance engine version

- ID: `rds59-upgrading`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_UpgradeDBInstance.Upgrading.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Major version upgrades must be started manually; minor version upgrades can be automatic
  - Database engine upgrades require downtime
  - RDS applies a minor version upgrade even with auto minor version upgrade off for critical security issues or an end of support

### Upgrades of the RDS for PostgreSQL DB engine

- ID: `rds59-pg-upgrade`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_UpgradeDBInstance.PostgreSQL.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - RDS uses pg_upgrade for major version upgrades, and an upgrade cannot be reverted
  - With a backup retention above 0, RDS takes two DB snapshots during a major upgrade
  - In-Region read replicas are upgraded together with the source in a major version upgrade

### How to perform a major version upgrade for RDS for PostgreSQL

- ID: `rds59-pg-upgrade-process`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_UpgradeDBInstance.PostgreSQL.MajorVersion.Process.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A major upgrade does not upgrade extensions, and optimizer statistics must be regenerated with ANALYZE afterwards
  - A version-compatible parameter group must be ready before the upgrade

### Performing a minor version upgrade for RDS for PostgreSQL

- ID: `rds59-pg-minor`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_UpgradeDBInstance.PostgreSQL.Minor.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - One minor version per major version is designated as the automatic upgrade version and is applied in the maintenance window

### Release calendars for Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL

- ID: `rds59-release-calendar`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/PostgreSQLReleaseNotes/postgresql-release-calendar.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - PostgreSQL 18 is the newest major version on RDS; its RDS end of standard support is 28 February 2031
  - RDS end of standard support: 17 on 28 February 2030, 16 on 28 February 2029, 15 on 29 February 2028, 14 on 28 February 2027; 13 ended on 28 February 2026
  - Each major version has dates for the start of Extended Support year 1 pricing, year 3 pricing, and the end of Extended Support

### Amazon RDS Extended Support with Amazon RDS

- ID: `rds59-extended-support`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/extended-support.html>

  - After Extended Support ends, RDS upgrades the major version automatically

### Creating a DB instance with Amazon RDS Extended Support

- ID: `rds59-extended-support-creating`

  - With open-source-rds-extended-support-disabled, RDS upgrades the instance to a supported version on or shortly after the end of standard support

### Overview of Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments

- ID: `rds59-blue-green`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/blue-green-deployments-overview.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A blue/green deployment creates a staging (green) environment that stays in sync with production
  - The switchover causes downtime, usually under one minute

### Limitations and considerations for Amazon RDS blue/green deployments

- ID: `rds59-blue-green-considerations`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/blue-green-deployments-considerations.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Blue/green deployments do not support managing master user passwords with AWS Secrets Manager
  - Blue/green deployments are not supported with CloudFormation
  - Point-in-time recovery history does not carry over to the new production instance after a switchover

### PostgreSQL replication methods for blue/green deployments

- ID: `rds59-blue-green-replication`

- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - RDS for PostgreSQL uses physical replication for blue/green deployments, and logical replication when a major version upgrade is requested

### Introduction to backups

- ID: `rds59-backup-intro`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_WorkingWithAutomatedBackups.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Automated backups are storage volume snapshots of the whole DB instance, and the instance can be recovered to any point in the retention period
  - Automated backups are deleted with the DB instance unless retained; final and manual snapshots are not
  - Automated backups do not occur while the instance is in a state other than available, such as storage_full

### Backup retention period

- ID: `rds59-backup-retention`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_WorkingWithAutomatedBackups.BackupRetention.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The retention period is 0 to 35 days; 0 disables automated backups; the default is one day through the API or CLI and seven days in the console
  - Changing the retention between 0 and a nonzero value causes an outage

### Managing automated backups

- ID: `rds59-backup-window`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ManagingAutomatedBackups.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - During the backup window storage I/O might be suspended briefly while the backup initializes, typically under a few seconds
  - For PostgreSQL Multi-AZ deployments I/O is not suspended on the primary, because the backup is taken from the standby
  - The backup window cannot overlap with the weekly maintenance window

### Amazon RDS Proxy

- ID: `rds59-proxy`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-proxy.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - RDS Proxy pools and shares database connections, and queues or rejects connections it cannot serve
  - A proxy must be in the same VPC as the database and cannot be publicly accessible
  - For DB instances in replication configurations, a proxy can be associated only with the writer DB instance, not a read replica
  - Each account is limited to 20 proxies by default

### Planning where to use RDS Proxy

- この出典が支える主張:
  - Lambda functions and DB instances that hit too many connections are good candidates for a proxy
  - RDS Proxy bypasses DNS caches to reduce failover times by up to 66% for RDS Multi-AZ DB instances

### Avoiding pinning an RDS Proxy

- ID: `rds59-proxy-pinning`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-proxy-pinning.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 59
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A pinned client connection keeps one database connection until the session ends
  - For PostgreSQL, SET commands, PREPARE/DEALLOCATE/EXECUTE, temporary objects, cursors, LISTEN, session-level advisory locks and sequence functions cause pinning; transaction-level advisory locks do not
  - Any statement larger than 16 KB pins the session
  - DatabaseConnectionsCurrentlySessionPinned shows how often pinning occurs

### Amazon Aurora storage

- ID: `aurora60-storage`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Overview.StorageReliability.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 60
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Aurora data is stored in the cluster volume, a single virtual volume with copies of the data across three Availability Zones in one Region
  - The amount of replication is independent of the number of DB instances in the cluster
  - Adding a DB instance does not copy the table data; removing one removes no data; only deleting the cluster removes the data
  - Two storage configurations: Aurora Standard (pay per 1 million I/O requests) and Aurora I/O-Optimized (no I/O charge)
  - AWS's guidance: I/O-Optimized when I/O spending is 25% or more of total Aurora spending
  - Switching from Standard to I/O-Optimized is possible once every 30 days; back to Standard at any time; no downtime for serverless instances
  - The volume grows automatically and you are charged for the space used; freed space reduces the charge

  - Up to 15 Aurora Replicas handle read-only traffic

  - During a failover the reader endpoint might direct connections to the new primary for a short time

### High availability for Amazon Aurora

- ID: `aurora60-high-availability`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Concepts.AuroraHighAvailability.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 60
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Writes are replicated synchronously across Availability Zones to six storage nodes; replicas use asynchronous replication
  - With a replica, failover promotes it: read and write operations fail with an exception meanwhile; service is typically restored in less than 60 seconds, often less than 30
  - Without a replica, the primary is recreated in the same AZ, which typically takes less than 10 minutes
  - If an AZ outage takes a single-instance cluster's primary, you must create a new instance in another AZ yourself
  - Promotion tiers 0 to 15 decide which replica is promoted
  - RDS Proxy bypasses DNS caches and can reduce failover times by up to 66%

- ID: `aurora60-fast-failover`

  - Recommended TCP keepalive settings: idle 1 second, interval 1 second, count 5
  - Updating the DNS record of an endpoint typically takes less than 30 seconds
  - After connecting, SHOW transaction_read_only tells a writer (OFF) from a reader (ON)
  - FailoverDBCluster promotes another instance and is the API for testing a failover; the cluster needs two or more instances

### How Aurora serverless works

- ID: `aurora60-serverless-how`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.how-it-works.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 60
- この出典が支える主張:
  - One ACU is approximately 2 GiB of memory with corresponding CPU and networking; capacity ranges from 0 to 256 ACUs
  - A minimum of 0 ACUs needs Aurora PostgreSQL 13.15, 14.12, 15.7, 16.3 or higher
  - Scaling happens in increments as small as 0.5 ACU, while connections are open and transactions are in progress, without disrupting them
  - The larger the current capacity, the larger the scaling increment
  - Readers in promotion tiers 0 and 1 are kept at least as large as the writer; tiers 2 to 15 scale on their own
  - A cluster with n instances consumes about n times the minimum ACUs when idle
  - The page now calls the feature 'Aurora serverless' and says Serverless v1 is a deprecated product

### Scaling to Zero ACUs with automatic pause and resume for Aurora serverless

- ID: `aurora60-auto-pause`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2-auto-pause.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 60
- この出典が支える主張:
  - With a minimum of 0 ACUs an instance pauses after a period with no user connections; the instance charge is zero while paused; storage is still charged
  - The interval is 300 seconds (the default) to 86,400 seconds
  - Resuming typically takes about 15 seconds; after more than 24 hours paused it can take 30 seconds or longer
  - An open user connection, an RDS Proxy, logical replication, a zero-ETL integration, and membership of a global database prevent pausing
  - A request through the RDS Data API resumes a paused writer
  - Aurora resumes paused instances for some maintenance, and then waits at least 20 minutes before pausing again
  - An instance resumes at a relatively small capacity whatever it had before
  - AWS recommends retry logic for connections, and timeouts longer than 15 seconds (30 or more if idle for over a day)

### Amazon SQS queue types

- ID: `sqs61-queue-types`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-queue-types.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Standard queues: at-least-once delivery and best-effort ordering; FIFO queues: order preserved and no duplicates introduced
  - With batching a FIFO queue handles up to 3,000 messages per second per API method, from 300 API calls per second
- 注記: This page says high throughput mode scales to 30,000 TPS 'with relaxed ordering within message groups'. The message quotas page gives per-Region figures (9,000 TPS in Tokyo) and the high throughput page does not mention relaxed ordering. The chapter quotes the quotas page and says the two differ.

### Amazon SQS FIFO queues

- ID: `sqs61-fifo`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-fifo-queues.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The order in which messages are sent and received is preserved, and a message is delivered once and remains unavailable until a consumer processes and deletes it
  - A FIFO queue can hold many ordered message groups, with no quota on their number
  - FIFO queues are available in all Regions where SQS is

### FIFO queue delivery logic in Amazon SQS

- ID: `sqs61-fifo-logic`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/FIFO-queues-understanding-logic.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A send without a message group ID fails
  - Ordering holds within a message group; messages of different groups may be processed out of order relative to each other
  - One receive may return several messages of the same group, up to 10, and may add messages of other groups
  - No more messages of a group are returned by later receives until the received ones are deleted or become visible again
  - A consumer cannot ask for a particular message group
  - A producer may retry SendMessage with the same deduplication ID without introducing duplicates, as long as an acknowledgment arrives before the deduplication interval expires

### Exactly-once processing in Amazon SQS

- ID: `sqs61-exactly-once`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/FIFO-queues-exactly-once-processing.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A SendMessage retried within the 5-minute deduplication interval introduces no duplicate
  - Content-based deduplication uses a SHA-256 hash of the message body, not of its attributes
  - Deduplication needs either content-based deduplication or an explicit deduplication ID

### Using the message deduplication ID in Amazon SQS

- ID: `sqs61-dedup-id`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/using-messagededuplicationid-property.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A message whose deduplication ID was already accepted is acknowledged and not delivered
  - SQS keeps tracking the deduplication ID after the message has been received and deleted

### When to provide a message deduplication ID in Amazon SQS

- ID: `sqs61-dedup-when`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/providing-message-deduplication-id.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A producer should give an explicit ID when identical bodies must count as different messages, or different bodies as the same message

### Using the message group ID with Amazon SQS FIFO Queues

- ID: `sqs61-group-id`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/using-messagegroupid-property.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Messages of one message group are processed one at a time, in strict order
  - On a standard queue a MessageGroupId enables fair queues and does not order anything

### FIFO queue and message identifiers in Amazon SQS

- ID: `sqs61-identifiers`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-fifo-queue-message-identifiers.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A FIFO queue's name ends in .fifo, and the suffix counts toward the 80 characters of a name
  - Each receive returns a different receipt handle, and a delete needs the most recent one
  - The sequence number is a large, non-consecutive number SQS assigns to each message

### Moving from a standard queue to a FIFO queue in Amazon SQS

- ID: `sqs61-moving`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/FIFO-queues-moving.html>

- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:

  - FIFO queues support a delay per queue, not per message

### Amazon SQS FIFO queue and Lambda concurrency behavior

- ID: `sqs61-fifo-lambda`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/fifo-queue-lambda-behavior.html>

### High throughput for FIFO queues in Amazon SQS

- ID: `sqs61-high-throughput`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/high-throughput-fifo.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:

  - SQS recommends message group IDs with many distinct values

### Enabling high throughput for FIFO queues in Amazon SQS

- ID: `sqs61-enable-high-throughput`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/enable-high-throughput-fifo.html>

### Amazon SQS message quotas

- ID: `sqs61-quotas-messages`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/quotas-messages.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A message is at most 1,048,576 bytes (1 MiB) and at least 1 byte
  - Retention defaults to 4 days and ranges from 60 seconds to 14 days
  - The visibility timeout defaults to 30 seconds and ranges from 0 seconds to 12 hours
  - A batch holds at most 10 messages, a message at most 10 attributes, and a message timer at most 15 minutes
  - Without high throughput a FIFO queue allows 300 transactions per second per API action, 3,000 messages with batching
  - With high throughput the limit in Asia Pacific (Tokyo) is 9,000 transactions per second, 90,000 messages with batching
  - A message group ID is at most 128 characters of alphanumerics and punctuation

### Amazon SQS FIFO queue quotas

- ID: `sqs61-quotas-fifo`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/quotas-fifo.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A FIFO queue supports at most 120,000 in-flight messages; no error is returned when the limit is reached
  - The longest long polling wait is 20 seconds, and the longest queue delay 15 minutes

### Amazon SQS visibility timeout

- ID: `sqs61-visibility`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-visibility-timeout.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A received message stays in the queue, hidden for the visibility timeout, and becomes visible again unless deleted
  - While a message of a FIFO message group is in flight, later messages of the group are not made available until it is deleted or its timeout expires
  - ChangeMessageVisibility extends or shortens the timeout of one message; 0 makes it available at once
  - The limit is 12 hours from when the message was first received, and extending does not reset it
  - The guide suggests a heartbeat that keeps extending the timeout when the processing time is not known

### Processing messages in a timely manner in Amazon SQS

- ID: `sqs61-timely`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/best-practices-processing-messages-timely-manner.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A visibility timeout shorter than the processing time lets another consumer receive the message while the first still works on it
  - A heartbeat can start with 2 minutes and add 2 minutes every minute
  - A consumer that needs longer than 12 hours should use Step Functions

### Configuring visibility timeouts in Amazon SQS

- ID: `sqs61-visibility-sdk`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/working-with-visibility-timeouts.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13

### Amazon SQS short and long polling

- ID: `sqs61-polling`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-short-and-long-polling.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Short polling asks a subset of servers and answers at once, even with nothing; long polling asks all servers and answers when a message is available or the wait time ends
  - The longest wait is 20 seconds
  - Long polling is in effect when the receive's WaitTimeSeconds, or else the queue's ReceiveMessageWaitTimeSeconds, is greater than 0

### Amazon SQS batch actions

- ID: `sqs61-batch`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-batch-api-actions.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13

- この出典が支える主張:

  - The messages of one SendMessageBatch may not exceed 1 MiB in total
  - Permission for a batch action is the permission for the single action

### Managing large Amazon SQS messages with Extended Client Library and Amazon S3

- ID: `sqs61-large`

### Amazon SQS delay queues

- ID: `sqs61-delay`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-delay-queues.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61

### Amazon SQS message timers

- ID: `sqs61-timers`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-message-timers.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
