### Message metadata for Amazon SQS

- ID: `sqs61-metadata`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-message-metadata.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A message can carry up to 10 attributes, each with a name, a type (String, Number, Binary), and a value
  - All parts of an attribute count toward the 1 MiB size limit

### Using dead-letter queues in Amazon SQS

- ID: `sqs61-dlq`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-dead-letter-queues.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A dead-letter queue must be in the same account and Region as its source queue
  - The guide warns against a dead-letter queue on a FIFO queue when the exact order of operations must not be broken
  - For a FIFO queue the enqueue timestamp resets when a message moves to the dead-letter queue; for a standard queue it does not
  - A redrive allow policy can restrict which source queues may use a queue as their dead-letter queue

### Learn how to configure a dead-letter queue redrive in Amazon SQS

- ID: `sqs61-redrive`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-configure-dead-letter-queue-redrive.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A redrive moves messages to the source queue or another queue of the same type, oldest first
  - Redriven messages are new messages with a new message ID and enqueue time, and they interleave with what producers are sending
  - When a message moves from a FIFO queue to its FIFO dead-letter queue, its deduplication ID is replaced by its message ID
  - Messages cannot be filtered or changed while redriving; a task runs at most 36 hours

### Encryption at rest in Amazon SQS

- ID: `sqs61-sse`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-server-side-encryption.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A queue is encrypted with SQS-managed keys (SSE-SQS) or with a KMS key (SSE-KMS)
  - SSE encrypts the body; not the queue metadata, the message metadata including attributes, or the metrics
  - The data key reuse period is 60 seconds to 24 hours, 5 minutes by default
  - A queue encrypted with the AWS managed key for SQS cannot invoke a Lambda function in another account

### Amazon SQS Key management

- ID: `sqs61-kms`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-key-management.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A producer to an SSE-KMS queue needs kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt; a consumer needs kms:Decrypt
  - Calls to KMS per queue are estimated as R = (B / D) * (2 * P + C)
  - An AWS service that sends to an encrypted queue needs a customer managed key whose policy allows that service

### Available CloudWatch metrics for Amazon SQS

- ID: `sqs61-metrics`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-available-cloudwatch-metrics.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage: a standard queue moves a message received three or more times to the back, so the metric skips it; a FIFO queue does not reorder, and a failed message blocks its group until it is deleted or expires
  - NumberOfEmptyReceives counts ReceiveMessage calls that returned nothing
  - NumberOfDeduplicatedSentMessages and ApproximateNumberOfGroupsWithInflightMessages exist for FIFO queues
  - NumberOfMessagesSent does not count messages SQS moves to a dead-letter queue itself

### Amazon SQS fair queues

- ID: `sqs61-fair`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-fair-queues.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13

  - A MessageGroupId on a standard queue does not enforce ordering

### Basic examples of Amazon SQS policies

- ID: `sqs61-policies`

### SendMessage

- ID: `sqs61-api-send`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/APIReference/API_SendMessage.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A message sent with a deduplication ID that was accepted before is accepted and not delivered during the 5-minute deduplication interval
  - If the acknowledgment is lost and the message is resent with the same deduplication ID after the interval, SQS cannot detect the duplicate
  - DelaySeconds cannot be set per message on a FIFO queue
  - A body may contain only the characters #x9, #xA, #xD, #x20 to #xD7FF, #xE000 to #xFFFD, #x10000 to #x10FFFF; anything else is rejected with InvalidMessageContents
  - A deduplication ID is at most 128 characters; the sequence number keeps increasing within a message group

### SendMessageBatch

- ID: `sqs61-api-send-batch`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/APIReference/API_SendMessageBatch.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - For a FIFO queue, the messages of one batch are enqueued in the order they are sent
  - Each entry's result is reported individually, so a call that returns HTTP 200 can contain failures

### ReceiveMessage

- ID: `sqs61-api-receive`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/APIReference/API_ReceiveMessage.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A receive returns at most 10 messages
  - If a consumer is still processing when the visibility timeout expires, another worker can receive the same messages and process duplicates, and the first consumer's delete fails
  - ReceiveRequestAttemptId lets a FIFO consumer retry a receive whose answer was lost and get the same messages, for 5 minutes
  - The system attributes include ApproximateReceiveCount, MessageGroupId, MessageDeduplicationId, and SequenceNumber

### ChangeMessageVisibility

- ID: `sqs61-api-change-visibility`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/APIReference/API_ChangeMessageVisibility.html>

- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The new timeout counts from the moment of the call
  - Asking for more than the time left of the 12 hours is an error; SQS does not shorten the request
  - The changed timeout applies to this receive only; the next receive uses the queue's value again

- この出典が支える主張:

### Using Lambda with Amazon SQS

- ID: `sqs61-lambda-sqs`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Lambda polls the queue and invokes the function synchronously with a batch; it deletes the messages when the function succeeds
  - An event source mapping processes each event at least once, and the documentation strongly recommends idempotent function code
  - A FIFO record carries SequenceNumber, MessageGroupId, and MessageDeduplicationId among its attributes
  - Provisioned mode gives an event source mapping dedicated pollers, at extra cost
- 注記: The page gives the maximum number of provisioned pollers as 10,000 in one place and the parameters page says 2,000. The chapter does not use provisioned mode and quotes neither.

### Creating and configuring an Amazon SQS event source mapping

- ID: `sqs61-lambda-configure`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-configure.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The queue's visibility timeout should be at least six times the function's timeout, plus the batch window if there is one
  - Lambda refuses an event source mapping whose function timeout exceeds the queue's visibility timeout
  - The batch size is at most 10 for a FIFO queue and 10,000 for a standard queue
  - maxReceiveCount of at least 5 is recommended
  - An encrypted queue needs kms:Decrypt in the execution role

### Configuring scaling behavior for SQS event source mappings

- ID: `sqs61-lambda-scaling`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-scaling.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Maximum concurrency is a setting of the event source, from 2 to 1,000, and cannot be combined with provisioned mode
  - For a FIFO queue, concurrent invocations are capped by the number of message group IDs or by maximum concurrency, whichever is lower
  - When the function returns an error, all retries on the affected messages happen before Lambda receives more messages of the same group
  - At low traffic Lambda scales back to five concurrent invokes, and the further reduction to two is not available when maximum concurrency is set

### Handling errors for an SQS event source in Lambda

- ID: `sqs61-lambda-errors`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-errorhandling.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 61
- この出典が支える主張:
  - With partial batch responses on a FIFO queue, the function should stop at the first failure and return the failed and all unprocessed messages
  - An exception fails the whole batch; an empty or null list is a complete success; an unknown or empty itemIdentifier fails the whole batch

### Secure use reference (GitHub Actions)

- ID: `cir-gh-secure-use`
- URL: <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 62
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Self-hosted runners 'do not have guarantees around running in ephemeral clean virtual machines, and can be persistently compromised by untrusted code in a workflow'
  - Self-hosted runners 'should almost never be used for public repositories'; for private repositories anyone who can fork and open a pull request can compromise the runner environment
  - Just-in-time runners 'perform at most one job before being automatically removed'; 're-using hardware to host JIT runners can risk exposing information from the environment'; started with ./run.sh --jitconfig
  - 'there is no way to guarantee that a self-hosted runner only runs one job' is said of runners destroyed by automation after each job, before the JIT section
  - pull_request_target and workflow_run are privileged triggers and must not check out untrusted code

  - A new runner version must be installed within 30 days
  - 'GitHub recommends implementing autoscaling with ephemeral self-hosted runners; autoscaling with persistent self-hosted runners is not recommended'

### Securely deploying AI agents (Claude Code docs)

- ID: `sbx-cc-secure-deployment`
- URL: <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/secure-deployment>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 63
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Agents can take unintended actions due to prompt injection (instructions embedded in content they process) or model error
  - Isolation technologies compared: sandbox runtime, containers (setup dependent), gVisor, VMs such as Firecracker
  - Cloud deployments: private subnet with no internet gateway, firewall rules that block all egress except to a proxy, a proxy that enforces domain allowlists, minimal IAM permissions, traffic logged at the proxy
  - The recommended credential pattern is a proxy outside the agent's boundary that injects credentials; the agent never sees them
  - With HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY the proxy sees only an opaque CONNECT tunnel for HTTPS unless it terminates TLS
  - Not all programs respect HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY

### Choose a sandbox environment (Claude Code docs)

- ID: `sbx-cc-sandbox-environments`
- URL: <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 63
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Sandbox isolation reduces the impact of a breach but does not eliminate risk; any approach that allows network egress can still leak data the agent can read
  - A custom container can run Claude Code with your own network policies; unprivileged containers need enableWeakerNestedSandbox for the built-in Bash sandbox
  - A dedicated virtual machine provides the strongest separation, with its own kernel; options include microVMs such as Firecracker
  - A cloud session runs in an isolated, Anthropic-managed virtual machine; a proxy holds the GitHub token outside the sandbox

### Configure the sandboxed Bash tool (Claude Code docs)

- ID: `sbx-cc-sandboxing`
- URL: <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 63
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The Bash sandbox covers shell commands only; Read, Edit, Write, WebFetch and WebSearch, MCP servers and hooks run outside it
  - Linux uses bubblewrap and socat; network connections go through a proxy that checks each host against the allowed domains
  - The proxy decides from the client-supplied hostname without inspecting TLS, so domain fronting can reach hosts outside the allowlist
  - sandbox.failIfUnavailable makes Claude Code exit when the sandbox cannot start; allowUnsandboxedCommands false disables the unsandboxed retry
  - In an unprivileged container bubblewrap cannot mount a fresh /proc; enableWeakerNestedSandbox bind-mounts the container's /proc, weakens security, and should be used only when the outer container is the boundary
  - A tool that ignores the proxy environment variables cannot connect from inside the sandbox

### Run Claude Code programmatically (Claude Code docs)

- ID: `sbx-cc-headless`
- URL: <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 63
- この出典が支える主張:
  - claude -p runs non-interactively and exits 0 on success and non-zero on failure
  - Without --bare a -p session runs the hooks in a project's .claude/settings.json and connects the servers in its .mcp.json, even in a folder never trusted
  - --bare skips hooks, skills, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory and CLAUDE.md; Amazon Bedrock credentials are still read as usual
  - --output-format stream-json emits newline-delimited JSON; the last line is a result message with cost and session metadata
  - dontAsk denies every call that would otherwise prompt
  - On SIGTERM Claude Code terminates the process tree of a running Bash command and exits with code 143

### CLI reference (Claude Code docs)

- ID: `sbx-cc-cli`
- URL: <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 63
- この出典が支える主張:
  - --max-budget-usd stops the run once estimated spend reaches the amount (print mode only); the estimate is client-side, can differ from the bill, and spend can pass the cap
  - --max-turns limits the number of agentic turns (print mode only) and exits with an error when the limit is reached
  - --tools restricts which built-in tools Claude can use; --settings takes a settings JSON file; --no-session-persistence; --permission-mode accepts dontAsk

### Configure permissions (Claude Code docs)

- ID: `sbx-cc-permissions`

### workerd, Cloudflare's JavaScript/Wasm Runtime (README at v1.20261012.1)

- ID: `iso-workerd-readme`
- URL: <https://github.com/cloudflare/workerd/blob/v1.20261012.1/README.md>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 64
- この出典が支える主張:
  - workerd is a JavaScript / Wasm server runtime based on the same code that powers Cloudflare Workers
  - Its stated uses: an application server to self-host applications designed for Cloudflare Workers, a development tool, and a programmable HTTP proxy
  - WARNING: workerd is not a hardened sandbox. It tries to isolate each Worker, but on its own does not contain suitable defense-in-depth against implementation bugs; to run possibly-malicious code you must run it inside an appropriate secure sandbox, such as a virtual machine
  - When one nanoservice calls another, the callee runs in the same thread and process
  - Updating workerd never breaks existing code; the version number is a date, the maximum compatibility date that version supports
  - Configuration is a file in Cap'n Proto text format; `workerd serve my-config.capnp` serves it
  - Prebuilt binaries are distributed via npm; on Linux they need glibc 2.35 or higher (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian Bookworm), on macOS 13.5 or higher
  - Tested on Linux and macOS (x86-64 and arm64) and Windows (x86-64)
  - For production the README suggests systemd, with sockets inherited through --socket-fd, and Restart=always
- 注記: The README on the main branch was byte-identical to the one at the tag on 2026-10-13.

### workerd.capnp: the configuration schema (v1.20261012.1)

- ID: `iso-workerd-capnp`
- URL: <https://github.com/cloudflare/workerd/blob/v1.20261012.1/src/workerd/server/workerd.capnp>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 64
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A Config has services, sockets, v8Flags, extensions, autogates, and logging; a Service is a worker, a network, an external server, or a disk directory
  - A Worker has modules or a serviceWorkerScript, a required compatibilityDate, compatibilityFlags, bindings, globalOutbound, Durable Object namespaces and storage
  - Binding kinds include text, data, json, cryptoKey, service, durableObjectNamespace, kvNamespace, r2Bucket, queue, analyticsEngine, hyperdrive, fromEnvironment, memoryCache, and workerLoader
  - kvNamespace, r2Bucket, and queue bindings turn operations into HTTP requests aimed at a service named in the configuration; workerd does not contain the stores
  - fromEnvironment takes the value from getenv() of the named variable; the binding is null if the variable is not set
  - Durable Object storage is none, inMemory (for local testing), or localDisk (marked EXPERIMENTAL); objects are always local to one instance of the runtime
  - A worker that inherits another runs in the same isolate as the base worker
  - The default globalOutbound is the service `internet`, which allows publicly routable addresses only
  - HttpOptions.forwardedProtoHeader names the header that tells the worker which protocol the original client used
  - The schema has no field that limits a worker's CPU time or memory (the only limits struct is MemoryCacheLimits)
  - `workerd compile` builds a self-contained binary from the workerd binary, a configuration, and its source code

### Cloudflare Workers: How Workers works

- ID: `iso-cf-how-workers-works`
- URL: <https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/reference/how-workers-works/>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 64
- この出典が支える主張:
  - V8 isolates are lightweight contexts; one instance of the runtime runs hundreds or thousands of them, and each isolate's memory is completely isolated
  - An isolate is created within an existing environment instead of a virtual machine per function, which eliminates the cold starts of the virtual machine model
  - Any given isolate can start around a hundred times faster than a Node process on a container or virtual machine, and on startup consumes an order of magnitude less memory
  - A single Workers instance may handle multiple requests, including concurrent requests, in a single-threaded event loop; Cloudflare recommends you do not use or mutate global state
  - Isolates may be evicted for resource limits on the machine, suspicious scripts, or individual resource limits
- 注記: Page last updated 2026-09-18.

### Cloudflare Workers: Security model

- ID: `iso-cf-security-model`
- URL: <https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/reference/security-model/>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 64
- この出典が支える主張:
  - V8 isolates prevent code from accessing memory outside the isolate, even within the same process, which lets Cloudflare run many isolates in a single process
  - Around the isolates Cloudflare adds: a process-level sandbox built from Linux namespaces and seccomp that prohibits all filesystem and network access, a supervisor process that mediates everything else, cordons that separate Workers by trust level into different processes, and process isolation for some Workers
  - Date.now() is locked in place while code executes, no other timers are provided, and there is no multi-threading, as defenses against Spectre
  - Cloudflare builds and deploys a new runtime after a V8 security patch within 24 hours
  - V8 creates a wider attack surface than virtual machines
- 注記: Page last updated 2026-09-18.

### Cloudflare Workers: Pricing

- ID: `iso-cf-pricing`
- URL: <https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing/>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 64
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Workers Paid has a minimum charge of USD 5 a month per account, with no additional charges for data transfer (egress) or throughput (bandwidth)
  - Standard usage model: 10 million requests included per month, then USD 0.30 per additional million; 30 million CPU milliseconds included, then USD 0.02 per additional million; no charge or limit for duration
  - Example on the page: 15 million requests a month at 7 ms of CPU time each costs USD 8.00; 100 million at 7 ms costs USD 45.40

- ID: `iso-cf-limits`

- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 64
- この出典が支える主張:
  - CPU time per HTTP request: 10 ms on Free; on Paid, 30 seconds by default and up to 5 minutes
  - Memory per isolate: 128 MB, per isolate and not per invocation; when exceeded the runtime lets in-flight requests complete and creates a new isolate
  - A Worker that exceeds its CPU time limit is answered with Error 1102
  - Worker startup time limit: 1 second

### Manual deployment: Start YB-Masters

- ID: `distsql-yb-start-masters`
- URL: <https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable/deploy/manual-deployment/start-masters/>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 66
- この出典が支える主張:
  - yb-master is started with --master_addresses, --rpc_bind_addresses, --fs_data_dirs and the --placement_cloud, --placement_region, --placement_zone flags, or with --flagfile
  - The number of nodes running YB-Masters, and of addresses in --master_addresses, must equal the replication factor
  - The masters discover each other and elect a Raft leader; the page tells you to add the start command to cron so the process is restarted if it goes down

### Manual deployment: System configuration

- ID: `distsql-yb-system-config`
- URL: <https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable/deploy/manual-deployment/system-config/>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 66
- この出典が支える主張:
  - chrony is the preferred NTP implementation; a YB-TServer or YB-Master shuts down when it detects clock skew larger than --max_clock_skew_usec (500 ms by default)
  - On cloud providers the provider's link-local time service should be used
  - Recommended limits include 1048576 open files and 12000 user processes; transparent hugepages should be enabled; on virtual machines vm.swappiness=0 and vm.max_map_count=262144
  - ClockBound is supported on AWS and optional; PTP is currently available only for AWS

### Deployment checklist

- ID: `distsql-yb-checklist`
- URL: <https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable/deploy/checklist/>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 66
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The default replication factor is 3; with it a cluster tolerates one node failure, and needs at least as many nodes, YB-Masters and YB-TServers as the RF
  - Minimum 2 cores and 2 GB RAM; for production YSQL 16+ cores and 64 GB+ RAM
  - x86 and ARM (aarch64) are supported; SSDs are required, XFS recommended, noatime on data drives
  - On AWS use the M instance family and gp3 volumes of at least 250 GB; avoid T2 instance types
  - Nodes communicate on 7100 (YB-Master RPC) and 9100 (YB-TServer RPC); 5433 serves YSQL clients; 7000 is the YB-Master admin UI

  - certs_dir names the directory with the certificates

### Transaction isolation levels

- ID: `distsql-yb-isolation`
- URL: <https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable/architecture/transactions/isolation-levels/>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 66
- この出典が支える主張:
  - YSQL supports Serializable, Snapshot and Read Committed; Snapshot maps to the SQL Repeatable Read level
  - For manually deployed universes yb_enable_read_committed_isolation defaults to false, and Read Committed falls back to the stricter Snapshot isolation

### Concurrency control

- ID: `distsql-yb-concurrency`
- URL: <https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable/architecture/transactions/concurrency-control/>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 66
- この出典が支える主張:
  - With wait queues a transaction waits for the conflicting ones to finish, then proceeds only if they made no conflicting permanent change, and otherwise aborts
  - A statement that is the first of its transaction is retried internally with a later snapshot

### Transaction retries in YSQL

- ID: `distsql-yb-retries`
- URL: <https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable/develop/learn/transactions/transactions-retries-ysql/>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 66
- この出典が支える主張:
  - 40001 (serialization failure) and 40P01 (deadlock detected) are to be handled by rolling back and retrying the whole transaction with backoff
  - A COMMIT must not be retried blindly, because it is unclear whether the commit happened

### Synchronous replication in DocDB

- ID: `distsql-yb-replication`
- URL: <https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable/architecture/docdb-replication/replication/>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 66
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A tablet has as many peers as the replication factor; they form a Raft group and elect a leader
  - A write is applied after its Raft log entry is replicated to and persisted on a majority of the peers
  - Tolerating f fault domains needs a replication factor of at least 2f + 1
  - Only the tablet leader processes user-facing reads and writes by default; the stated recovery time after a zone outage is 3 seconds

### Transactions overview

- ID: `distsql-yb-transactions`
- URL: <https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable/architecture/transactions/transactions-overview/>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 66
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Every update is a transaction; timestamps come from hybrid logical clocks that combine physical time and a logical counter, and nodes exchange them on every RPC
  - Conflict resolution between concurrent transactions depends on the maximum clock skew in the cluster

### Hash and range sharding

- ID: `distsql-yb-sharding`
- URL: <https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable/architecture/docdb-sharding/sharding/>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 66
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Tables are split into shards called tablets; the primary key of a row decides its tablet
  - Hash sharding spreads rows evenly over the 2-byte hash space 0x0000 to 0xFFFF; range sharding keeps rows in primary key order

### YB-Master service

- ID: `distsql-yb-master`
- URL: <https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable/architecture/yb-master/>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 66
- この出典が支える主張:
  - YB-Master keeps the system metadata, the map from tablets to servers, balances load and re-replicates the data of a failed server; it is not in the I/O path
  - The masters form a Raft group of their own

- ID: `distsql-yb-replace-tserver`

- ID: `distsql-yb-upgrade`

  - It is finalized with `yb-admin promote_auto_flags` and `yb-admin upgrade_ysql`; after finalizing there is no rollback, and the monitoring phase should not exceed two days

### Firecracker README (v1.17.0)

- ID: `fc-readme`
- URL: <https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/blob/v1.17.0/README.md>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 67
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Firecracker is a virtual machine monitor that uses KVM to create and run microVMs, and excludes unnecessary devices and guest-facing functionality
  - It was developed at Amazon Web Services to accelerate the speed and efficiency of services like AWS Lambda and AWS Fargate, and is open source under Apache 2.0
  - One Firecracker process exposes an API endpoint; the defaults are 1 vCPU and 128 MiB
  - What the API can configure, including rate limiters for virtio devices, a vsock, an entropy device, pmem, memory hotplug
  - The jailer applies a cgroup and namespace barrier and drops privileges
  - Tested platforms are EC2 .metal instances of Intel, AMD and Graviton generations with host kernels 5.10, 6.1 and 6.18; 8th generation Intel only with 6.1 or 6.18
  - The security of microVMs depends on a well configured Linux host

### Firecracker Specification (v1.17.0)

- ID: `fc-specification`
- URL: <https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/blob/v1.17.0/SPECIFICATION.md>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 67
- この出典が支える主張:
  - On M5D.metal and M6G.metal: the VMM starts within 8 CPU ms, with wall-clock from 6 ms to 60 ms
  - For 1 vCPU and 128 MiB with the Firecracker-tuned kernel: VMM memory overhead <= 5 MiB, depending on workload and configuration
  - <= 125 ms from the InstanceStart call to the start of /sbin/init, measured with the serial console disabled and a minimal kernel and root file system
  - Guest CPU performance > 95% of bare metal, marked integration test pending
  - The API conforms to the in-tree OpenAPI specification

### Firecracker Design (v1.17.0)

- ID: `fc-design`
- URL: <https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/blob/v1.17.0/docs/design.md>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 67
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Each Firecracker process encapsulates one and only one microVM; threads are API, VMM and one per vCPU
  - Up to 32 vCPUs; 5 microVMs per host core per second with a minimal kernel, one vCPU and 128 MiB
  - Network devices are backed by TAP devices and block devices by files on the host
  - All vCPU threads are considered to run malicious code once started; Firecracker does not filter network traffic
  - Rate limiters are two token buckets, operations per second and bandwidth
  - Seccomp filters are installed by Firecracker; the jailer sets up cgroups and chroot, drops privileges, and execs Firecracker
  - In production builds the serial console is not exposed

### Firecracker FAQ (v1.17.0)

- ID: `fc-faq`
- URL: <https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/blob/v1.17.0/FAQ.md>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 67
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Lambda launched in November 2014 with per-customer EC2 instances for isolation
  - Firecracker started from crosvm and is written in Rust
  - Only 6 emulated devices are named: virtio-net, virtio-balloon, virtio-block, virtio-vsock, serial console, and a minimal keyboard controller
  - Guest and host must have the same CPU architecture
  - Firecracker does not support guest reboot; on x86 `reboot` with reboot=k ends the process
  - The serial console is disabled by default for boot time
- 注記: The FAQ's list of six devices is shorter than the README's feature list of the same tag, which also names an entropy device and pmem.

### The Firecracker Jailer (v1.17.0)

- ID: `fc-jailer`
- URL: <https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/blob/v1.17.0/docs/jailer.md>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 67
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The jailer's arguments and its steps: close file descriptors, clean the environment, copy the binary into a chroot, set resource limits, create cgroups, pivot_root, mknod /dev/net/tun and /dev/kvm, join a network namespace, drop privileges, exec
  - Copying the binary ensures the process shares no memory with another Firecracker process

### Production Host Setup Recommendations (v1.17.0)

- ID: `fc-prod-host`
- URL: <https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/blob/v1.17.0/docs/prod-host-setup.md>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 67
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Firecracker should be started with the jailer in production, or under constraints at least as restrictive
  - Each Firecracker process should correspond to a workload of a single tenant
  - Firecracker cannot mitigate the host's hardware vulnerabilities; SMT and kernel samepage merging should be disabled for tenant separation
  - Firecracker does not filter guest traffic; a rule dropping packets from TAP devices to 169.254.169.254 is given
  - The serial device should not be enabled in production

### Firecracker Snapshotting (v1.17.0)

- ID: `fc-snapshot`
- URL: <https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/blob/v1.17.0/docs/snapshotting/snapshot-support.md>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 67
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A snapshot is a guest memory file and a microVM state file; disk files are managed by the user
  - Loading maps the memory file MAP_PRIVATE, so pages load on demand and writes go to anonymous memory
  - Pause, Resume and CreateSnapshot only after boot; LoadSnapshot only before configuration
  - Diff snapshots are in developer preview
  - Resuming the same snapshot more than once is considered insecure without a mechanism for uniqueness; VMGenID reseeds the guest kernel's PRNG on Linux 5.18 and later
  - Network connectivity is not guaranteed after resume

### Firecracker: Lightweight Virtualization for Serverless Applications (NSDI '20)

- ID: `fc-nsdi`
- URL: <https://www.usenix.org/system/files/nsdi20-paper-agache.pdf>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 67
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Lambda first isolated functions with Linux containers and customers with virtual machines
  - Containers trade security against compatibility through the syscalls they allow; language VM isolation was unsuitable because Lambda and Fargate run arbitrary binaries
  - Firecracker has no BIOS, cannot boot arbitrary kernels, emulates no legacy devices nor PCI, and supports no VM migration (as of the paper)
  - Each Lambda worker runs hundreds or thousands of microVMs, each a slot for one function and one concurrent invocation, reused for serial invocations
  - A pool of pre-booted microVMs hides boot latency; slots lived at most 12 hours
  - Measured with Firecracker v0.20.0 on m5d.metal: memory overhead around 3 MB; boot figures; block and network throughput
  - The seccomp profile then allowed 24 syscalls and 30 ioctls
  - Lambda migrated to Firecracker on EC2 bare metal instances starting in 2018
- 注記: Published February 2020 about Firecracker v0.20.0 and the Lambda of that time.

### The Security Design of the AWS Nitro System: introduction

- ID: `nitro-wp-intro`

  - Its three key components are the Nitro Cards, the Nitro Security Chip, and the Nitro Hypervisor

### The Nitro System journey

- ID: `nitro-wp-journey`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/security-design-of-aws-nitro-system/the-nitro-system-journey.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 68
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Starting with C5 in 2017 the Nitro System eliminated dom0; a minimized hypervisor based on KVM provides the VMM, and what device models did moved to Nitro Cards

### The components of the Nitro System

- ID: `nitro-wp-components`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/security-design-of-aws-nitro-system/the-components-of-the-nitro-system.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 68
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Nitro Cards provide all I/O interfaces and all outward-facing control interfaces, on hardware physically separate from the system main board that runs customer workloads
  - Nitro Cards present NVMe for block storage and ENA for networking over PCIe, divided into SR-IOV virtual functions assigned directly to VMs
  - Encryption keys for EBS, instance storage and VPC networking are present in plaintext only in the protected volatile memory of the Nitro Cards
  - The Nitro Controller is the hardware root of trust and the only gateway between the server and the EC2 control plane
  - The Nitro Security Chip mediates writes to firmware and holds the main board in reset until the controller has verified it, which is what makes bare metal instances possible
  - The Nitro Hypervisor has no networking stack, no general-purpose file system, no peripheral device drivers, no shell and no interactive access mode

### Putting the pieces together: EBS volume attachment

- ID: `nitro-wp-ebs-attach`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/security-design-of-aws-nitro-system/putting-the-pieces-together-ebs-volume-attachment.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 68
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Attaching a volume ends with the Nitro Card for EBS presenting an NVMe device and the hypervisor sending a hot-plug event to the VM
  - The volume's data key is decrypted in KMS, re-encrypted to the host's public key, and kept in plaintext only in the volatile memory of that Nitro Card

### No AWS operator access

- ID: `nitro-wp-no-operator`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/security-design-of-aws-nitro-system/no-aws-operator-access.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 68
- この出典が支える主張:
  - AWS's statement that there is no mechanism for any system or person to log in to EC2 Nitro hosts, access the memory of EC2 instances, or access customer data on encrypted instance storage or encrypted EBS volumes
  - Operators can use only a limited set of authenticated, authorized, logged and audited administrative APIs, none of which gives access to customer data
  - The stated trade-off: some issues cannot be debugged in place and must be reproduced on dedicated non-production hardware

### The EC2 approach to preventing side-channels

- ID: `nitro-wp-side-channels`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/security-design-of-aws-nitro-system/the-ec2-approach-to-preventing-side-channels.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 68
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Fixed performance instances get dedicated cores and memory; CPU cores are never shared simultaneously between customers through SMT
  - Burstable instances (T3, T3a, T4g) can use overcommitted CPU and memory and can run one after another on the same core, with state flushed between them
  - Graviton instances get multiples of one vCPU because the hardware has no SMT; SMT hardware gives multiples of two
  - A Nitro Enclave inherits the same isolation and side-channel mitigations as any EC2 instance; its vCPUs (at least one full core) and memory are hot-unplugged from the parent

### What is Nitro Enclaves?

- ID: `nitro-enclaves-what-is`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/enclaves/latest/user/nitro-enclave.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 68
- この出典が支える主張:
  - An enclave is a separate, hardened virtual machine with only a local socket to its parent instance: no persistent storage, no interactive access, no external networking
  - Data and applications inside the enclave cannot be accessed by processes, applications, or users (root or admin) of the parent instance
  - The list of parent instance types: no T family, no x86 .large (M6i, C6i start at xlarge), Graviton families from .large (M6g, C6g except medium and metal)
  - Up to four enclaves per parent; enclaves stop when the parent stops; hibernation and enclaves cannot be enabled together; supported in all Regions
  - There are no additional charges for Nitro Enclaves beyond the instance and other services used

- この出典が支える主張:
  - Nitro Enclaves is not available on bare metal instances, burstable instance types (for example T3), and instances with only one CPU core

### Nitro Enclaves concepts

- ID: `nitro-enclaves-concepts`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/enclaves/latest/user/nitro-enclave-concepts.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 68
- この出典が支える主張:
  - An enclave is a VM with its own kernel, memory and CPUs, made by partitioning memory and vCPUs from the parent instance
  - The KMS proxy runs on the parent; sessions with KMS are established logically between KMS and the enclave, and the traffic is protected from the parent
  - The vsock is the only channel an enclave has; the parent's CID is always 3

### Enclave workflow overview

- ID: `nitro-enclaves-flow`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/enclaves/latest/user/flow.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 68
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The three parties (data owner, parent instance administrator, application developer); the parent instance administrator should have no permission to use the key or to change the key policy
  - The decryption flow: the enclave sends the encrypted data key with its attestation document through the parent's KMS proxy, and KMS encrypts the plaintext key to the enclave's public key

### Cryptographic attestation

- ID: `nitro-enclaves-attestation`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/enclaves/latest/user/set-up-attestation.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 68
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The six measurements: PCR0 (image file), PCR1 (kernel and bootstrap), PCR2 (application), PCR3 (parent's IAM role), PCR4 (parent's instance ID), PCR8 (signing certificate)
  - PCR0 to PCR2 are printed by nitro-cli build-enclave; PCR3 and PCR4 are SHA-384 over 48 zero bytes followed by the ARN or the instance ID, with the example values the tests check
  - Enclaves started with --debug-mode or --attach-console produce attestation documents whose PCRs are all zeros, unusable for attestation
  - An attestation document can be requested only from inside the enclave

### Using cryptographic attestation with AWS KMS

- ID: `nitro-enclaves-kms`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/enclaves/latest/user/kms.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 68
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The example key policy: Allow for the instance role on kms:Decrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:GenerateRandom with StringEqualsIgnoreCase on kms:RecipientAttestation:ImageSha384 and PCR keys
  - If the request does not include an attestation document, the role has no permission because the condition cannot be satisfied

### Verifying the root of trust

- ID: `nitro-enclaves-verify-root`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/enclaves/latest/user/verify-root.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 68
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The attestation document is CBOR, signed as COSE_Sign1 with ECDSA 384, with the fields module_id, timestamp, digest, pcrs, certificate, cabundle and the optional public_key, user_data, nonce
  - Documents are signed by the AWS Nitro Attestation PKI, whose root certificate is published with its fingerprint

### Cryptographic attestation support in AWS KMS

- ID: `nitro-kms-attestation`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/cryptographic-attestation.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 68
- この出典が支える主張:
  - With a signed attestation document, Decrypt, DeriveSharedSecret, GenerateDataKey, GenerateDataKeyPair and GenerateRandom return the plaintext encrypted under the public key from the document instead of the plaintext
  - GenerateDataKey still returns the copy of the data key encrypted by the KMS key

### AWS KMS condition keys for attested platforms

- ID: `nitro-kms-conditions-attestation`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/conditions-attestation.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 68
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The default key policy allows the account every action including Decrypt; AWS recommends least privilege and mentions NotAction kms:Decrypt as one way to restrict it

### Condition keys for Nitro Enclaves

- ID: `nitro-kms-conditions-enclave`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/conditions-nitro-enclave.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 68
- この出典が支える主張:
  - kms:RecipientAttestation:ImageSha384 corresponds to PCR0, and kms:RecipientAttestation:PCR<PCR_ID> to a named PCR; both are single-valued strings for key policies and IAM policies
  - Both are effective only when the Recipient parameter carries a signed attestation document; without one, permission is denied because the condition is not satisfied
  - StringEqualsIgnoreCase is the operator AWS's examples use for PCR values

### How to make attested calls to AWS KMS

- ID: `nitro-kms-attested-calls`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/attested-calls.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 68
- この出典が支える主張:
  - The Recipient parameter carries the document and the key encryption algorithm; the response has CiphertextForRecipient and an empty Plaintext
  - KMS relies on the document's signature; you cannot supply your own certificate to sign it
  - AWS SDKs take the Recipient parameter; the document comes from the Nitro Secure Module through the NSM API

### Monitoring attested requests

- ID: `nitro-kms-attestation-cloudtrail`

- 参照する章: 68
- この出典が支える主張:
  - CloudTrail entries for attested requests carry a recipient field in additionalEventData

### KMS API: RecipientInfo

- ID: `nitro-kms-api-recipient`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/APIReference/API_RecipientInfo.html>

### Default key policy

- ID: `nitro-kms-default-policy`
- URL: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/key-policy-default.html>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 68
- この出典が支える主張:
  - A KMS key policy gives no permission to the account or its identities unless a statement says so
  - A statement whose principal is the account lets IAM policies allow the listed actions; without it IAM policies that allow access are ineffective

- この出典が支える主張:
  - The key policy alone can control access when the key and the IAM principal are in the same account

### cdkd 0.296.28: provider registry and property coverage

- ID: `nitro-cdkd-property-coverage`
- URL: <https://github.com/go-to-k/cdkd/tree/v0.296.28>
- 確認日: 2026-10-13
- 参照する章: 68
- この出典が支える主張:
  - Dedicated providers are registered for AWS::EC2::Instance, AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup, AWS::IAM::InstanceProfile, AWS::IAM::Role and AWS::KMS::Key
  - The EC2 instance provider does not wire EnclaveOptions ("not yet implemented by cdkd"); a template that sets it is routed through Cloud Control API with the full property map
- 注記: Read in the installed npm package (dist/deploy-engine-*.js), not on GitHub. No deploy was run.
